# SCSTG-TEST-0009: Blockchain Data and State Management


### **Description**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#description "Permanent link")

Effective management of blockchain data and state is crucial for ensuring the consistency and security of decentralized applications. Poor state management can lead to data corruption, inconsistencies between contracts, and vulnerabilities that attackers can exploit. Ensuring that data changes are properly tracked, validated, and secure is key to maintaining the integrity of the system. This includes ensuring that sensitive data is not exposed, and that critical functions such as state transitions are properly handled. This test focuses on validating that smart contracts effectively manage their state and data in a secure and robust manner.

* * *


### **Test 1: Validate Proper Use of Storage Variables**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#test-1-validate-proper-use-of-storage-variables "Permanent link")

#### Vulnerable Code[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#vulnerable-code "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-0-1)contract DataStorage {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-0-2)    uint256 public value; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-0-3)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-0-4)    function updateValue(uint256 newValue) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-0-5)        value = newValue;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-0-6)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-0-7)}`

title: SCSTG-TEST-0009: Blockchain Data and State Management
heading: **Test 2: Ensure Proper Validation of External Data Inputs**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#test-2-ensure-proper-validation-of-external-data-inputs "Permanent link")
text:
### **Why It’s Vulnerable**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#why-its-vulnerable "Permanent link")

-   The contract directly updates the state variable `value` without validating or securing the transaction, exposing the contract to potential manipulation.
-   If `newValue` is provided by an untrusted user, it could lead to data corruption or loss of value.

#### Fixed:[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#fixed "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-1-1)contract SecureDataStorage {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-1-2)    uint256 public value;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-1-3)    address public owner; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-1-4)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-1-5)    modifier onlyOwner() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-1-6)        require(msg.sender == owner, "Unauthorized");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-1-7)        _;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-1-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-1-9)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-1-10)    constructor() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-1-11)        owner = msg.sender;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-1-12)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-1-13)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-1-14)    function updateValue(uint256 newValue) public onlyOwner {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-1-15)        value = newValue;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-1-16)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-1-17)}`

#### How to Check[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#how-to-check "Permanent link")

-   **Code Review:** Ensure that state variables are updated only through validated functions, and that access to sensitive operations is restricted through appropriate access controls.
-   **Testing:** Test the contract by submitting values from different sources and verify that the state is only updated when appropriate conditions are met.

#### Vulnerable Code[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#vulnerable-code_1 "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-2-1)contract ExternalData {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-2-2)    uint256 public externalValue; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-2-3)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-2-4)    function updateExternalData(address oracle) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-2-5)        // Vulnerable: call returns (bool, bytes); no success check; invalid assignment        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-2-6)        (bool success, bytes memory data) = oracle.call(abi.encodeWithSignature("getData()"));        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-2-7)        if (data.length >= 32) {            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-2-8)            externalValue = abi.decode(data, (uint256));  // Proceeds without checking success        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-2-9)        }    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-2-10)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-2-11)}`

heading: **Test 3: Prevent Data Inconsistencies Through Proper Event Logging**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#test-3-prevent-data-inconsistencies-through-proper-event-logging "Permanent link")
text:
### **Why It’s Vulnerable**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#why-its-vulnerable_1 "Permanent link")

#### Example 2: Unsecured External Data Sources[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#example-2-unsecured-external-data-sources "Permanent link")

-   The contract calls external data sources without validating the data properly, allowing attackers to feed false or malicious data.
-   The `oracle.call()` method exposes the contract to arbitrary external calls, which could result in unintended consequences.

#### Fixed:[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#fixed_1 "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-3-1)interface IOracle {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-3-2)    function getData() external view returns (uint256); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-3-3)} [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-3-4)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-3-5)contract SecureExternalData {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-3-6)    uint256 public externalValue;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-3-7)    address public oracle; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-3-8)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-3-9)    modifier onlyOracle() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-3-10)        require(msg.sender == oracle, "Unauthorized");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-3-11)        _;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-3-12)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-3-13)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-3-14)    constructor(address _oracle) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-3-15)        oracle = _oracle;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-3-16)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-3-17)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-3-18)    function updateExternalData() public onlyOracle {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-3-19)        externalValue = IOracle(oracle).getData();  // Safe interaction with oracle interface    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-3-20)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-3-21)}`

#### How to Check[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#how-to-check_1 "Permanent link")

-   **Code Review:** Look for external contract calls and ensure that proper validation mechanisms (e.g., access control and data validation) are in place.
-   **Dynamic Testing:** Attempt to feed invalid or malicious data to the contract and verify that it rejects the input or fails gracefully.

* * *

### **Test 3: Prevent Data Inconsistencies Through Proper Event Logging**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#test-3-prevent-data-inconsistencies-through-proper-event-logging "Permanent link")

#### Vulnerable Code[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#vulnerable-code_2 "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-4-1)contract InconsistentState {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-4-2)    uint256 public data; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-4-3)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-4-4)    function setData(uint256 newData) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-4-5)        data = newData;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-4-6)        // No event emitted    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-4-7)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-4-8)}`


### **Why It’s Vulnerable**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#why-its-vulnerable_2 "Permanent link")

-   The contract does not emit events after updating the state, leading to a lack of transparency and difficulty tracking state changes.
-   The absence of events makes it harder to detect inconsistencies or malicious changes to the data.

#### Fixed:[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#fixed_2 "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-5-1)contract ConsistentState {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-5-2)    uint256 public data; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-5-3)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-5-4)    event DataUpdated(uint256 newData); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-5-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-5-6)    function setData(uint256 newData) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-5-7)        data = newData;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-5-8)        emit DataUpdated(newData);  // Emits event on state change    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-5-9)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#__codelineno-5-10)}`

#### How to Check[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCSTG-TEST-0009/#how-to-check_2 "Permanent link")

-   **Code Review:** Ensure that important state changes and data updates are accompanied by event emissions to track changes and ensure consistency.
-   **Testing:** Monitor the contract’s events and check that critical operations such as state changes are logged correctly.

heading: **Remediation**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/overview/#remediation "Permanent link")
text:
# Policies, Procedures, and Code Management


### **Description**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/overview/#description "Permanent link")

Policies, procedures, and code management play a crucial role in ensuring the security, maintainability, and scalability of smart contracts. Proper development practices, such as secure coding standards, thorough code reviews, and consistent documentation, are essential for preventing vulnerabilities and ensuring smooth development workflows. Without these practices, smart contracts may become difficult to manage, error-prone, or vulnerable to security exploits.

This section covers best practices in secure coding standards, code review processes, code clarity, and comprehensive testing to reduce vulnerabilities and improve the quality of the codebase.

**Example: Code With Redundant or Dead Code**

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/overview/#__codelineno-0-1)// Example: Code with redundant, duplicated, or dead code [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/overview/#__codelineno-0-2)function transfer(address recipient, uint256 amount) public {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/overview/#__codelineno-0-3)    // Redundant code: balance is checked twice    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/overview/#__codelineno-0-4)    require(balanceOf[msg.sender] >= amount, "Insufficient balance");    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/overview/#__codelineno-0-5)    balanceOf[msg.sender] -= amount;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/overview/#__codelineno-0-6)    balanceOf[recipient] += amount;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/overview/#__codelineno-0-7)    // Dead code: This line will never be reached    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/overview/#__codelineno-0-8)    if (amount == 0) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/overview/#__codelineno-0-9)        revert("Cannot transfer zero amount");    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/overview/#__codelineno-0-10)    }    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/overview/#__codelineno-0-11)    emit Transfer(msg.sender, recipient, amount); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/overview/#__codelineno-0-12)}`

In the above example, the check for `amount == 0` is redundant because the first `require` statement ensures that the sender has enough balance to make the transfer. Also, if `amount == 0`, the transaction would revert due to the `require` check, making the second check unnecessary. Additionally, the `revert("Cannot transfer zero amount")` will never be executed because of the earlier revert.


### **Impact**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/overview/#impact "Permanent link")

-   **Code Redundancy**: Redundant checks or logic lead to unnecessary computations and increased gas costs. This can also introduce confusion about the intended behavior of the contract, making it harder to maintain and audit.
-   **Dead Code**: Unreachable or unnecessary code bloats the contract, making it more complex and increasing the risk of errors or vulnerabilities. It can also lead to wasted gas when the contract executes, as unused code still contributes to the overall execution cost.
-   **Security Risks**: Redundant or dead code may hide actual vulnerabilities and complicate the auditing process, making it easier for attackers to find and exploit flaws.
-   **Maintainability Issues**: The presence of redundant or dead code makes the contract harder to maintain and extend, as developers may waste time debugging or managing parts of the code that do not affect the system's functionality.

title: Policies, Procedures, and Code Management
heading: **Remediation**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/overview/#remediation "Permanent link")
text:
### **Remediation**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/overview/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Remove Redundant and Dead Code**: Perform regular code reviews and refactor contracts to eliminate redundant or dead code. This reduces complexity and ensures that the contract remains efficient and understandable.
-   **Keep Logic Simple and Clear**: Avoid unnecessary checks or repeated logic that can be handled by existing conditions or functions. Keep the contract logic as simple and clear as possible to minimize the chance of introducing errors.
-   **Optimize Gas Costs**: Removing unnecessary logic reduces gas consumption, making the contract more cost-effective for users and improving overall network performance.
-   **Use Automated Tools**: Implement static analysis tools and linters to detect redundant or dead code, helping to streamline the codebase and enforce best practices.

# SCSTG-TEST-0010: Test Compiler Version and Deprecated Functions


### **Description**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#description "Permanent link")

Proper management of development policies, secure coding standards, code clarity, and test coverage ensures that smart contracts are secure, maintainable, and resilient to vulnerabilities. This test focuses on ensuring adherence to best practices and guidelines for developing and reviewing smart contracts. This includes the use of current compilers, avoiding deprecated functions, thorough code reviews, and ensuring proper test coverage. Code clarity is also critical for maintaining contracts over time and ensuring they remain understandable and auditable.

* * *


### **Test 1: Verify Compiler Version and Avoid Deprecated Functions**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#test-1-verify-compiler-version-and-avoid-deprecated-functions "Permanent link")

#### Vulnerable Code:[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#vulnerable-code "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.4.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-0-3)contract Example {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-0-4)    uint256 public value; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-0-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-0-6)    function setValue(uint256 _value) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-0-7)        value = _value;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-0-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-0-9)}`

#### **Why It’s Vulnerable**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#why-its-vulnerable "Permanent link")

-   The contract uses an outdated compiler version (^0.4.0). Using old versions of Solidity may lead to known security vulnerabilities and lack of support for modern features.
-   Older compiler versions also lack optimizations and security fixes that are available in newer versions.

#### Fixed:[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#fixed "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0;  // Update to the latest stable version [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-1-3)contract Example {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-1-4)    uint256 public value; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-1-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-1-6)    function setValue(uint256 _value) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-1-7)        value = _value;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-1-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-1-9)}`

#### **How to Check**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#how-to-check "Permanent link")

-   Code Review: Ensure that the pragma directive specifies an up-to-date version of Solidity (e.g., ^0.8.x) and not outdated ones such as ^0.4.x.
-   Automated Check: Use Solidity linting tools or automated CI/CD pipelines to flag usage of outdated compiler versions.

* * *

### **Test 2: Ensure Code Review Processes and Avoid Deprecated Functions**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#test-2-ensure-code-review-processes-and-avoid-deprecated-functions "Permanent link")

#### **Vulnerable Code:**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#vulnerable-code_1 "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-2-1)pragma solidity ^0.4.24; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-2-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-2-3)// Example: ETH vault (sends Ether, not ERC20 tokens). Variable names simplified for clarity. [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-2-4)contract Token {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-2-5)    string public name = "Token";    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-2-6)    uint public totalSupply = 1000000;  // Tracks remaining withdrawable ETH [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-2-7)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-2-8)    // Deprecated: uses transfer() for Ether; deprecated in Solidity 0.5+    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-2-9)    function transfer(address recipient, uint amount) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-2-10)        require(msg.sender != recipient, "Cannot transfer to yourself");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-2-11)        require(amount <= totalSupply, "Amount exceeds total supply"); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-2-12)        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-2-13)        totalSupply -= amount;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-2-14)        // Deprecated: The transfer method below is obsolete        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-2-15)        recipient.transfer(amount);    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-2-16)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-2-17)}`

#### Why It’s Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#why-its-vulnerable_1 "Permanent link")

-   The function transfer in the above example uses a deprecated `transfer()` method to send Ether to the recipient.
-   The `transfer()` method was removed in Solidity 0.5.x, and it’s recommended to use `call()` instead to prevent errors due to changes in gas limits and transfer behavior in newer Solidity versions.
-   Using deprecated functions can make your contract incompatible with future versions of Solidity and leave it vulnerable to unexpected behavior.

#### Fixed Code:[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#fixed-code "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-3-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-3-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-3-3)// ETH vault example: sends Ether via call{value} (see SCWE-079) [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-3-4)contract Token {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-3-5)    string public name = "Token";    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-3-6)    uint public totalSupply = 1000000; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-3-7)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-3-8)    function transfer(address payable recipient, uint amount) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-3-9)

require(msg.sender != recipient, "Cannot transfer to yourself");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-3-10)        require(amount <= totalSupply, "Amount exceeds total supply"); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-3-11)        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-3-12)        totalSupply -= amount;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-3-13)        // Replaced deprecated transfer method with call to ensure proper handling        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-3-14)        (bool success, ) = recipient.call{value: amount}("");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-3-15)        require(success, "Transfer failed");    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-3-16)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#__codelineno-3-17)}`

#### Why the Fix Works[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#why-the-fix-works "Permanent link")

-   The updated code uses the `call()` method instead of the deprecated `transfer()` method to send Ether.
-   The `call()` method is more flexible and is recommended in Solidity 0.5.x and later, as it allows specifying gas and properly handling errors.
-   This change ensures that the contract is compatible with newer Solidity versions (>=0.5.x) and avoids potential issues with future upgrades.

#### How to Check[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CODE/SCSTG-TEST-0010/#how-to-check_1 "Permanent link")

-   Code Review: Ensure the contract is not using any deprecated or obsolete functions. Look for any `transfer()`, `send()`, or other outdated methods, and replace them with the more secure `call()` method when sending Ether.
-   Static Analysis Tools: Use tools like SolidityScan, MythX, Slither, or linters to detect deprecated features and provide suggestions for updating the code.
-   Testing: Test the contract using the latest Solidity version and verify that no deprecated functions are used, ensuring compatibility with newer compilers.

title: Unchecked External Calls in Smart Contracts
heading: Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/overview/#remediation "Permanent link")
text:
# Unchecked External Calls in Smart Contracts


### **Description**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/overview/#description "Permanent link")

Unchecked external calls occur when a smart contract makes an external call to another contract or address without verifying the call's outcome. In Ethereum, external calls may fail silently, and the calling contract may mistakenly proceed as if the call succeeded. This leads to state inconsistencies and potential exploitation. The issue is particularly risky in functions like delegatecall, send, or call, where the outcome must be explicitly checked.

**Example: Code Without Proper Access Control**

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/overview/#__codelineno-0-1)// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/overview/#__codelineno-0-2)pragma solidity ^0.4.24; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/overview/#__codelineno-0-3)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/overview/#__codelineno-0-4)contract Proxy {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/overview/#__codelineno-0-5)    address public owner; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/overview/#__codelineno-0-6)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/overview/#__codelineno-0-7)    constructor() public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/overview/#__codelineno-0-8)        owner = msg.sender;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/overview/#__codelineno-0-9)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/overview/#__codelineno-0-10)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/overview/#__codelineno-0-11)    function forward(address callee, bytes memory _data) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/overview/#__codelineno-0-12)        require(callee.delegatecall(_data)); // Unchecked: no validation of callee; delegatecall executes in caller context    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/overview/#__codelineno-0-13)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/overview/#__codelineno-0-14)}`


### Impact[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/overview/#impact "Permanent link")

-   When external calls fail and their results are unchecked, the contract can proceed under incorrect assumptions, leading to potential loss of funds or other unexpected behaviors.
-   Unverified external calls can lead to incorrect updates to the contract state, making it vulnerable to exploits and logical inconsistencies.
-   Attackers can manipulate such vulnerabilities to execute malicious code or withdraw funds multiple times.


### Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/overview/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   For low-level functions like `call`, `delegatecall`, and `staticcall`, always check the return value and handle failures with `require(success, "message")`.
-   For ETH transfers, prefer `call{value}("")` with explicit success checks over `transfer()` or `send()` (see SCWE-079); `transfer()` has a 2300 gas stipend and can cause DoS when the recipient is a contract.
-   Limit interactions with untrusted contracts and ensure robust validation before performing critical operations.

# SCSTG-TEST-0011: Test Contract Interactions


### **Description**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#description "Permanent link")

Ensuring secure interactions and communications in smart contracts is crucial for protecting against unauthorized access, manipulation, and attacks. This includes ensuring that contracts interact securely with external contracts, manage oracle integrations safely, and use secure methods for cross-chain and bridge operations. A failure to adhere to best practices for these interactions can expose the contract to vulnerabilities such as reentrancy, front-running, or incorrect data feeds. This test focuses on validating that smart contracts perform secure interactions and communications, safeguarding the system from common attack vectors.

* * *


### **Test 1: Ensure Secure Contract Interactions**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#test-1-ensure-secure-contract-interactions "Permanent link")

#### **Vulnerable Code:**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#vulnerable-code "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.5.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#__codelineno-0-3)contract VulnerableContract {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#__codelineno-0-4)    address public trustedAddress; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#__codelineno-0-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#__codelineno-0-6)    constructor(address _trustedAddress) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#__codelineno-0-7)        trustedAddress = _trustedAddress;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#__codelineno-0-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#__codelineno-0-9)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#__codelineno-0-10)    function callExternalContract(address _to, uint256 _value) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#__codelineno-0-11)        _to.call{value: _value}(""); // Vulnerable to reentrancy or other attacks    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#__codelineno-0-12)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#__codelineno-0-13)}`

title: SCSTG-TEST-0011: Test Contract Interactions
heading: **How to Check**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#how-to-check "Permanent link")
text:
### **Why It’s Vulnerable**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#why-its-vulnerable "Permanent link")

-   The contract uses `.call` to make external calls, which is generally unsafe and susceptible to reentrancy attacks.
-   The function allows anyone to trigger the call and transfer funds, exposing the contract to potential attacks.

#### Fixed Code:[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#fixed-code "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#__codelineno-1-3)contract SecureContract {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#__codelineno-1-4)    address public trustedAddress; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#__codelineno-1-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#__codelineno-1-6)    constructor(address _trustedAddress) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#__codelineno-1-7)        trustedAddress = _trustedAddress;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#__codelineno-1-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#__codelineno-1-9)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#__codelineno-1-10)    function callExternalContract(address _to, uint256 _value) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#__codelineno-1-11)        require(_to != address(0), "Invalid address");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#__codelineno-1-12)        (bool success, ) = _to.call{value: _value}("");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#__codelineno-1-13)        require(success, "External call failed");    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#__codelineno-1-14)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#__codelineno-1-15)}`


### **How to Check**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMM/SCSTG-TEST-0011/#how-to-check "Permanent link")

-   **Code Review:** Look for external calls in the contract and ensure that they are using safe methods such as `transfer` or `send` where appropriate, or implementing reentrancy protection.
-   **Static Analysis:** Use static analysis tools like SolidityScan, MythX or Slither to detect unsafe calls in the code.
-   **Dynamic Testing:** Simulate a reentrancy attack by deploying a contract that calls the vulnerable contract and tries to drain funds.

title: Component-Specific Security
heading: **Component-Specific Security**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/overview/#component-specific-security "Permanent link")
text:
# Component-Specific Security

#### **Description**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/overview/#description "Permanent link")

Component-specific security focuses on the proper implementation and management of individual components in a smart contract ecosystem, such as tokens, NFTs, vaults, staking mechanisms, and liquidity pools. Each component has unique security considerations that must be addressed to prevent vulnerabilities and ensure smooth, secure operations within the broader system. These components often interact with each other, so it's critical to ensure that each is implemented correctly and adheres to established standards to avoid risks such as inconsistent balances, unintended behavior, and attacks.

#### **Example: ERC20 Token Security**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/overview/#example-erc20-token-security "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/overview/#__codelineno-0-1)// Example: Implementing ERC20 token with minting and transfers [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/overview/#__codelineno-0-2)contract MyToken is ERC20 {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/overview/#__codelineno-0-3)    uint256 public totalSupply; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/overview/#__codelineno-0-4)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/overview/#__codelineno-0-5)    function mint(address to, uint256 amount) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/overview/#__codelineno-0-6)        totalSupply += amount;  // Ensure total supply is updated securely        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/overview/#__codelineno-0-7)        _mint(to, amount);    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/overview/#__codelineno-0-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/overview/#__codelineno-0-9)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/overview/#__codelineno-0-10)    function transfer(address recipient, uint256 amount) public override returns (bool) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/overview/#__codelineno-0-11)        require(amount > 0, "Cannot transfer zero amount");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/overview/#__codelineno-0-12)        return super.transfer(recipient, amount);    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/overview/#__codelineno-0-13)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/overview/#__codelineno-0-14)}`

### **Component-Specific Security**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/overview/#component-specific-security "Permanent link")

#### **Impact**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/overview/#impact "Permanent link")

-   **Token Vulnerabilities**: Incorrect implementation of ERC20, ERC721, or ERC1155 tokens can lead to unexpected behavior, such as incorrect balances, inability to transfer tokens, or incompatible integrations with other dApps or services.
-   **NFT Security**: Poorly implemented NFTs can lead to issues with metadata integrity, unauthorized minting, or unauthorized transfers, impacting the uniqueness and value of NFTs.
-   **Vault Risks**: Issues related to asset management in vaults, such as stETH or wstETH, can cause delays in withdrawals or inconsistencies in the handling of token balances due to rebasing or other complex mechanisms.
-   **Liquid Staking Issues**: Vulnerabilities in staking mechanisms (e.g., sfrxETH/fraxETH) could lead to discrepancies in rewards or affect the overall staking rewards distribution.
-   **Liquidity Pool Exploits**: Automated market makers (AMMs) can be exploited if their logic is insecure, particularly regarding slippage, transaction fees, or impermanent loss calculations.
-   **Uniswap V4 Hook Vulnerabilities**: Incorrect integration or usage of Uniswap's TickMath and FullMath libraries can introduce overflow or underflow issues, leading to unpredictable behavior or contract failures.

#### **Remediation**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/overview/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Token Security**: Ensure compliance with token standards such as ERC20, ERC721, and ERC1155. Properly manage the total supply and token addresses. Avoid zero-amount transfers causing issues and ensure compatibility with other contracts or integrations.
-   **NFT Best Practices**: Implement strong standards for creating, managing, and transferring NFTs. Ensure metadata integrity and safeguard against unauthorized minting and transfers. Secure royalty payments and token burns to prevent exploitative behavior.
-   **Vault Management**: Address potential withdrawal overheads and ensure efficient handling of assets such as stETH and wstETH. Take care when converting between rebasing tokens to avoid discrepancies.
-   **Staking Mechanisms**: Regularly monitor and secure liquid staking mechanisms. Prevent discrepancies in reward transfers and ensure proper communication with users about potential changes, especially in the rate of tokens like sfrxETH.
-   **Liquidity Pool Security**: Secure the logic in automated market makers, especially for managing slippage and ensuring fair fee distributions. Ensure that the AMM is protected against known exploits and attacks.
-   **Uniswap V4 Integration**: Follow best practices for integrating Uniswap's TickMath and FullMath libraries, ensuring safe handling of arithmetic operations and proper validation to prevent overflow or underflow issues.

#### **Types of Vulnerabilities That Can Occur in This Category**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/overview/#types-of-vulnerabilities-that-can-occur-in-this-category "Permanent link")

-   **Token Minting Inconsistencies**: Incorrect updates to the totalSupply or failure to manage token addresses properly can cause inconsistencies and errors in token transactions.
-   **Unauthorized NFT Actions**: Lack of metadata integrity or vulnerabilities in transfer mechanisms can result in unauthorized minting, transfers, or sales of NFTs.
-   **Vault Management Flaws**: Issues like long withdrawal times or improper handling of rebasing assets can impact user experience and cause financial loss.
-   **Staking Discrepancies**: Vulnerabilities in staking reward mechanisms or incorrect handling of rate changes can undermine user confidence and token stability.
-   **Liquidity Pool Exploits**: Flaws in AMM contract logic, such as improper slippage management or failure to account for impermanent loss, can lead to loss of funds.
-   **Arithmetic Errors in Uniswap V4 Hooks**: Insecure arithmetic operations using Uniswap's libraries can result in overflow/underflow vulnerabilities, a

# SCSTG-TEST-0012: Test Token Implementations (ERC20, ERC721, ERC1155)


### **Description**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#description "Permanent link")

Component-Specific Security focuses on ensuring that each specific component of a decentralized application (dApp) or smart contract ecosystem is securely implemented. This includes a wide range of areas such as token standards (ERC20, ERC721, ERC1155), NFTs, vaults, liquidity pools, and other components. Properly securing these components is essential to avoid vulnerabilities that can lead to funds being stolen, lost, or misused. This test will focus on validating the security considerations for the components listed in the controls, ensuring that each one is implemented securely and with the appropriate mechanisms to protect users and assets.

* * *


### **Test: Ensure Proper Token Implementation (ERC20, ERC721, ERC1155)**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#test-ensure-proper-token-implementation-erc20-erc721-erc1155 "Permanent link")

#### \*\*Vulnerable Code: \*\*[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#vulnerable-code "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.5.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-0-3)contract SimpleERC20 {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-0-4)    mapping(address => uint256) public balanceOf;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-0-5)    mapping(address => mapping(address => uint256)) public allowance; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-0-6)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-0-7)    string public name = "Simple Token";    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-0-8)    string public symbol = "STK";    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-0-9)    uint8 public decimals = 18;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-0-10)    uint256 public totalSupply; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-0-11)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-0-12)    // Unchecked approve function (vulnerable to approval race condition)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-0-13)    function approve(address spender, uint256 amount) public returns (bool) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-0-14)        allowance[msg.sender][spender] = amount;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-0-15)        return true;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-0-16)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-0-17)}`

title: SCSTG-TEST-0012: Test Token Implementations (ERC20, ERC721, ERC1155)
heading: **How to Check**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#how-to-check "Permanent link")
text:
### **Why It’s Vulnerable**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#why-its-vulnerable "Permanent link")

-   The `approve` function does not include a check for the current allowance before setting a new one, which could allow for the "approval race condition." This can result in a vulnerability where an attacker could bypass the allowance mechanism and transfer more tokens than intended.
-   This issue is a well-known vulnerability in ERC20 token implementations.

#### Fixed Code:[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#fixed-code "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-1-3)contract SafeERC20 {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-1-4)    mapping(address => uint256) public balanceOf;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-1-5)    mapping(address => mapping(address => uint256)) public allowance; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-1-6)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-1-7)    string public name = "Safe Token";    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-1-8)    string public symbol = "STK";    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-1-9)    uint8 public decimals = 18;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-1-10)    uint256 public totalSupply; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-1-11)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-1-12)    // Secure approve function to prevent race condition    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-1-13)    function approve(address spender, uint256 amount) public returns (bool) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-1-14)        require(amount == 0 || allowance[msg.sender][spender] == 0, "Approve: non-zero allowance");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-1-15)        allowance[msg.sender][spender] = amount;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-1-16)        return true;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-1-17)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#__codelineno-1-18)}`


### **How to Check**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-COMP/SCSTG-TEST-0012/#how-to-check "Permanent link")

-   **Code Review:** Look for the `approve` function in token contracts and ensure that it includes the necessary checks to prevent the race condition. The secure approach is to first set the allowance to zero before updating it to a new value, or to require that it is zero if being reset.
-   **Static Analysis:** Use tools such as SolidityScan, MythX or Slither to check for the "approval race condition" and ensure the contract doesn't allow for this vulnerability.
-   **Dynamic Testing:** Test token transfer functionality with edge cases where the allowance is set to non-zero values before calling `approve`. Verify that it works correctly and no unauthorized transfers are possible.

title: Cryptographic Practices
heading: **Remediation**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/overview/#remediation "Permanent link")
text:
# Cryptographic Practices


### **Description**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/overview/#description "Permanent link")

Cryptographic practices in smart contracts ensure that sensitive operations, such as authentication, data integrity, and randomness, are protected from malicious manipulation. Secure key management, signature verification, and proper random number generation are essential to prevent vulnerabilities like unauthorized access, replay attacks, and exploitation of weaknesses in cryptographic operations.

Improper cryptographic practices can lead to severe consequences, including unauthorized transactions, predictable outcomes, and security breaches.


### **Example: Improper Signature Verification**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/overview/#example-improper-signature-verification "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/overview/#__codelineno-0-1)function verifySignature(address signer, bytes32 message, bytes memory signature) public pure returns (bool) {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/overview/#__codelineno-0-2)    bytes32 messageHash = keccak256(abi.encodePacked(message));    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/overview/#__codelineno-0-3)    address recoveredSigner = ecrecover(messageHash, uint8(signature[64]), bytes32(signature[0]), bytes32(signature[32]));    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/overview/#__codelineno-0-4)    return recoveredSigner == signer; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/overview/#__codelineno-0-5)}`

In this example, the `ecrecover` function is used without ensuring that the signature is valid, which may lead to vulnerabilities like signature malleability or invalid data recovery.


### **Impact**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/overview/#impact "Permanent link")

-   **Unauthorized Access**: Weak cryptographic practices can allow attackers to forge signatures or impersonate users, leading to unauthorized actions within the contract.
-   **Reentrancy Attacks**: If cryptographic functions are used to validate external calls, attackers could exploit weak or improperly implemented logic to re-enter the contract.
-   **Manipulation of Outcomes**: Predictable or weak random number generation could allow attackers to manipulate outcomes in systems relying on randomness, such as lotteries or gaming dApps.
-   **Replay Attacks**: Insufficient signature validation can result in replay attacks where signed messages are reused across different contexts, allowing attackers to perform unintended actions.


### **Remediation**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/overview/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Key Management**: Ensure that private keys are securely stored, never hardcoded in contracts, and use hardware solutions for key management.
-   **Signature Verification**: Implement proper checks for signature validity, including handling signature malleability by using nonces or hashed messages.
-   **Randomness**: Use secure sources of entropy, such as Chainlink VRF (Verifiable Random Function), to ensure the randomness cannot be manipulated.
-   **Compliance with Standards**: Ensure compliance with cryptographic standards like EIP-712 to prevent signature malleability and other vulnerabilities.

# SCSTG-TEST-0013: Secure Signature Verification


### **Description**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#description "Permanent link")

Cryptographic practices are essential in ensuring the confidentiality, integrity, and authenticity of interactions within decentralized systems. Weaknesses in cryptographic implementations, key management, or signature verification can lead to vulnerabilities such as unauthorized access, data manipulation, or attacks that compromise the security of transactions. This test focuses on verifying secure cryptographic practices, including key management, signature verification, and secure random number generation in smart contracts.

* * *


### **Test 1: Verify Secure Signature Verification**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#test-1-verify-secure-signature-verification "Permanent link")

#### Vulnerable Code:[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#vulnerable-code "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#__codelineno-0-3)contract SignatureVerification {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#__codelineno-0-4)    function verifySignature(address _signer, bytes32 _message, bytes memory _signature) public pure returns (bool) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#__codelineno-0-5)        // Directly using ecrecover, without checking for message format, leads to potential attack vectors        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#__codelineno-0-6)        address recovered = ecrecover(_message, uint8(_signature[0]), bytes32(_signature[1]), bytes32(_signature[2]));        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#__codelineno-0-7)        return recovered == _signer;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#__codelineno-0-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#__codelineno-0-9)}`

title: SCSTG-TEST-0013: Secure Signature Verification
heading: **Why It’s Vulnerable**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#why-its-vulnerable_1 "Permanent link")
text:
### **Why It’s Vulnerable**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#why-its-vulnerable "Permanent link")

-   The contract uses `ecrecover` directly without verifying the message structure.
-   Attackers could use a replay attack by reusing the signature from another message to authenticate different transactions.
-   The lack of proper checks makes the contract vulnerable to attacks where the attacker can forge or replay signatures.

#### Fixed Code:[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#fixed-code "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#__codelineno-1-3)contract SecureSignatureVerification {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#__codelineno-1-4)    // Use of EIP-712 for standard signature verification with specific message formats    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#__codelineno-1-5)    function verifySignature(address _signer, bytes32 _message, bytes memory _signature) public pure returns (bool) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#__codelineno-1-6)        bytes32 messageHash = keccak256(abi.encodePacked("\x19Ethereum Signed Message:\n32", _message));        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#__codelineno-1-7)        address recovered = ecrecover(messageHash, uint8(_signature[0]), bytes32(_signature[1]), bytes32(_signature[2]));        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#__codelineno-1-8)        return recovered == _signer;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#__codelineno-1-9)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#__codelineno-1-10)}`


### **How to Check**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#how-to-check "Permanent link")

-   **Code Review:** Verify that signatures are being properly validated using standards like EIP-712, and that the contract uses `ecrecover` securely. Ensure that messages are hashed and prefixed correctly before recovery.
-   **Dynamic Testing:** Test with replayed or malformed signatures to verify that the contract rejects such transactions.

* * *

#### Vulnerable Code:[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#vulnerable-code_1 "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#__codelineno-2-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#__codelineno-2-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#__codelineno-2-3)contract RandomNumberGenerator {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#__codelineno-2-4)    uint256 public randomValue; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#__codelineno-2-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#__codelineno-2-6)    function generateRandomNumber() public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#__codelineno-2-7)        randomValue = uint256(keccak256(abi.encodePacked(block.timestamp, block.difficulty)));    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#__codelineno-2-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#__codelineno-2-9)}`

title: SCSTG-TEST-0013: Secure Signature Verification
heading: **Why It’s Vulnerable**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#why-its-vulnerable_1 "Permanent link")
text:
### **Why It’s Vulnerable**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCSTG-TEST-0013/#why-its-vulnerable_1 "Permanent link")

-   The contract uses block properties like `block.timestamp` and `block.difficulty` (post-merge: `block.prevrandao`) to generate random numbers, which can be manipulated by validators.
-   This weak random number generation can lead to predictable values, making the contract vulnerable to attacks such as manipulation of lottery or gambling outcomes.

title: Gas Usage, Efficiency, and Limitations
heading: Gas Usage, Efficiency, and Limitations
text:
# Gas Usage, Efficiency, and Limitations

#### **Description**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/overview/#description "Permanent link")

Gas usage optimization in smart contracts is crucial for maintaining cost-effective, efficient, and scalable decentralized applications (dApps) on the Ethereum network. Gas represents the computational cost of executing operations in smart contracts, and minimizing gas consumption ensures that transactions are processed smoothly without hitting gas limits or incurring unnecessary costs. Understanding how to optimize gas usage and effectively design contracts is essential for reducing overhead, ensuring transaction reliability, and preventing network congestion.

#### **Example: Code Without Gas Optimization**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/overview/#example-code-without-gas-optimization "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/overview/#__codelineno-0-1)// Example: Non-optimized contract with expensive operations [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/overview/#__codelineno-0-2)function transfer(address recipient, uint256 amount) public {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/overview/#__codelineno-0-3)    require(balanceOf[msg.sender] >= amount, "Insufficient balance"); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/overview/#__codelineno-0-4)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/overview/#__codelineno-0-5)    balanceOf[msg.sender] -= amount;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/overview/#__codelineno-0-6)    balanceOf[recipient] += amount; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/overview/#__codelineno-0-7)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/overview/#__codelineno-0-8)    // Potentially costly operations (not optimized)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/overview/#__codelineno-0-9)    emit Transfer(msg.sender, recipient, amount); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/overview/#__codelineno-0-10)}`

#### **Impact**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/overview/#impact "Permanent link")

-   **High Gas Costs**: Inefficient smart contracts lead to higher gas costs for users, resulting in increased transaction fees and potentially deterring interaction with the contract.
-   **Transaction Failures**: Exceeding gas limits or inefficient use of gas can cause transactions to fail, resulting in reverted transactions and user dissatisfaction.
-   **Network Congestion**: Unoptimized contracts can cause network congestion, especially during high traffic periods, leading to delays and higher fees.
-   **Scalability Limitations**: As gas costs increase, the ability of the contract to handle a large number of transactions or users without hitting the gas limit is severely impacted.

#### **Remediation**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/overview/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Gas Usage Optimization**: Use efficient algorithms and reduce the number of computations performed on-chain. Avoid unnecessary state changes, and combine multiple operations where possible. Optimize loops, storage reads/writes, and event emissions to reduce costs.
-   **Gas Estimation Tools**: Use tools like eth\_gasPrice and gasStation to estimate gas prices and set appropriate gas limits for transactions. Implement gas estimation functions within the contract to predict and optimize gas usage.
-   **Layer 2 Solutions**: Consider integrating Layer 2 scaling solutions such as rollups or state channels to offload computation and reduce gas costs while improving transaction throughput. Validate the security and reliability of the chosen Layer 2 solutions to ensure seamless integration.

# SCSTG-TEST-0014: Test Gas Usage in Loops


### **Description**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/SCSTG-TEST-0014/#description "Permanent link")

Efficient gas usage is critical in smart contract development to ensure transactions are cost-effective and do not exceed block gas limits. Poorly optimized contracts can result in high transaction costs, failed transactions, and potential denial of service (DoS) attacks. Optimizing gas usage helps ensure that smart contracts are scalable, cost-effective, and maintain the overall security of decentralized applications (dApps). This test focuses on ensuring that gas usage is properly optimized, and contracts are designed to operate efficiently within the constraints of Ethereum's gas limits.

* * *

title: SCSTG-TEST-0014: Test Gas Usage in Loops
heading: **Test 1: Validate Gas Usage in Loops**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/SCSTG-TEST-0014/#test-1-validate-gas-usage-in-loops "Permanent link")
text:
### **Test 1: Validate Gas Usage in Loops**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/SCSTG-TEST-0014/#test-1-validate-gas-usage-in-loops "Permanent link")

#### **Vulnerable Code**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/SCSTG-TEST-0014/#vulnerable-code "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/SCSTG-TEST-0014/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/SCSTG-TEST-0014/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/SCSTG-TEST-0014/#__codelineno-0-3)contract GasInefficient {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/SCSTG-TEST-0014/#__codelineno-0-4)    uint256[] public data; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/SCSTG-TEST-0014/#__codelineno-0-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/SCSTG-TEST-0014/#__codelineno-0-6)    function addData(uint256[] memory newData) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/SCSTG-TEST-0014/#__codelineno-0-7)        for (uint i = 0; i < newData.length; i++) {            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/SCSTG-TEST-0014/#__codelineno-0-8)            data.push(newData[i]);  // Inefficient loop causing high gas costs        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/SCSTG-TEST-0014/#__codelineno-0-9)        }    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/SCSTG-TEST-0014/#__codelineno-0-10)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/SCSTG-TEST-0014/#__codelineno-0-11)}`

#### **Why It’s Vulnerable**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/SCSTG-TEST-0014/#why-its-vulnerable "Permanent link")

-   This contract uses a loop to iterate over an input array and push data into a dynamic array.
-   The gas cost increases linearly with the size of the input array. For large datasets, this can lead to excessive gas usage, potentially causing the transaction to exceed the block gas limit.
-   Smart contracts with inefficient loops that grow dynamically can become unmanageable when interacting with large datasets.

#### Fixed Code:[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/SCSTG-TEST-0014/#fixed-code "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/SCSTG-TEST-0014/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/SCSTG-TEST-0014/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/SCSTG-TEST-0014/#__codelineno-1-3)contract OptimizedGas {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/SCSTG-TEST-0014/#__codelineno-1-4)    uint256[] public data; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/SCSTG-TEST-0014/#__codelineno-1-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/SCSTG-TEST-0014/#__codelineno-1-6)    function addData(uint256[] memory newData) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/SCSTG-TEST-0014/#__codelineno-1-7)        uint256 length = newData.length;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/SCSTG-TEST-0014/#__codelineno-1-8)        for (uint i = 0; i < length; i++) {            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/SCSTG-TEST-0014/#__codelineno-1-9)            data.push(newData[i]);  // Optimized by storing array length outside the loop        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/SCSTG-TEST-0014/#__codelineno-1-10)        }    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/SCSTG-TEST-0014/#__codelineno-1-11)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/SCSTG-TEST-0014/#__codelineno-1-12)}`

#### **How to Check**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-DEFI/SCSTG-TEST-0014/#how-to-check "Permanent link")

-   **Code Review:** Ensure that loops and functions which deal with dynamic data structures are optimized for gas usage. Look for unnecessary state changes or excessive iterations within a single transaction.
-   **Gas Estimation:** Use tools like eth-gas-reporter or Remix IDE to estimate gas usage before and after optimizations.
-   **Dynamic Testing:** Test the contract with various input sizes and check that it performs within reasonable gas limits, ensuring it doesn't exceed the block gas limit.

title: Business Logic and Economic Security
heading: **Remediation**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-GOV/overview/#remediation "Permanent link")
text:
# Business Logic and Economic Security


### **Description**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-GOV/overview/#description "Permanent link")

Business logic and economic security in smart contracts ensure that the contract's operational rules and the associated economic incentives are properly designed to avoid exploitation and inefficiencies. This includes defining incentive structures, ensuring the stability of token values, preventing reentrancy attacks, and making sure that the tokenomics aligns with the expected behavior of the system. Contracts must be designed to avoid logical flaws, ensure that token rewards and penalties are correctly implemented, and prevent attacks that could undermine the contract's economic model.


### **Example: Improper Incentive Structure**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-GOV/overview/#example-improper-incentive-structure "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-GOV/overview/#__codelineno-0-1)// Push-based withdrawal process (vulnerable) [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-GOV/overview/#__codelineno-0-2)function withdraw(uint256 amount) public {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-GOV/overview/#__codelineno-0-3)    require(balance[msg.sender] >= amount, "Insufficient balance");    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-GOV/overview/#__codelineno-0-4)    (bool ok, ) = msg.sender.call{value: amount}("");    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-GOV/overview/#__codelineno-0-5)    require(ok, "Transfer failed"); // Push-based transfer (prefer pull-based; see SCWE-079)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-GOV/overview/#__codelineno-0-6)    balance[msg.sender] -= amount; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-GOV/overview/#__codelineno-0-7)}`

In the example above, a push-based withdrawal system may allow for unexpected behaviors, such as reentrancy attacks or failure to properly track balances due to uncontrolled fund transfers. A better approach would be to use a pull-based system.


### **Impact**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-GOV/overview/#impact "Permanent link")

-   **Incentive Misalignment**: Incorrect economic models can lead to unbalanced incentives, where users may be encouraged to behave in ways that harm the ecosystem or undermine contract objectives.
-   **Volatility and Losses**: Fluctuating token values, such as the conversion rates between assets like cbETH and ETH, can result in user losses if not properly handled. Similarly, staking rewards, such as with rETH, can create unpredictable value changes that impact users.
-   **Reentrancy Attacks**: Poor handling of transaction flow and state changes can allow attackers to re-enter the contract during a transaction, causing unintended consequences like double withdrawals.
-   **Token Vulnerabilities**: Incorrect tokenomics, such as faulty fee application or flawed reward systems, can cause users to lose funds or receive incorrect rewards.
-   **Double-Spending and Fraud**: Weak mechanisms like duplicate Merkle proofs can expose the system to double-spending attacks and other fraud mechanisms.

title: Business Logic and Economic Security
heading: **Remediation**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-GOV/overview/#remediation "Permanent link")
text:
### **Remediation**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCSTG/tests/SCSVS-GOV/overview/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Incentive Structures**: Implement a pull-based withdrawal system rather than push-based transfers to allow for proper tracking and reduce the risk of reentrancy attacks. Ensure that all economic incentives are clearly defined and aligned with desired behaviors.
-   **Tokenomics and Reward Systems**: Ensure that all token behaviors, including rebase mechanisms and reward claims, are properly handled. Prevent unexpected behaviors in tokens and validate that all claimable addresses are included in hashing processes to prevent unauthorized claims.
-   **Fluctuation Management**: Develop systems that can account for fluctuations in asset values (e.g., cbETH to ETH, rETH staking rewards) and adjust accordingly to mitigate risks for users.
-   **Transaction Flow Security**: Use patterns like check-effect-interaction to prevent reentrancy attacks, ensuring that state changes occur before external calls. Apply the NonReentrant modifier where applicable to prevent unintended recursive calls.
-   **Function Integrity**: Ensure that functions are designed to handle edge cases, such as same sender/recipient scenarios, and that they are not callable multiple times unnecessarily, avoiding potential inconsistencies or logic flaws.
