*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-005: Insecure Upgradeable Proxy Design

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-668: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/668.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/668.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#description "Permanent link")

Insecure upgradeable proxy designs occur when a smart contract implements an upgradeable proxy pattern without properly securing or validating upgrades. This may allow unauthorized actors to change the contract’s logic, possibly introducing malicious behavior. It often happens when the upgrade functionality lacks proper access controls or when there is no timelock to delay the upgrade, giving malicious actors an opportunity to exploit the contract.

This vulnerability can lead to critical failures, including the redirection of contract calls to malicious logic or unauthorized updates that compromise the integrity of the contract.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Access Control:** Ensure only trusted parties (e.g., contract owners, multisig wallets) can perform upgrades.
-   **Timelock Mechanism:** Implement a timelock to delay upgrades and provide transparency.
-   **Transparent Proxy Pattern:** Use patterns that prevent unauthorized contract logic changes, such as the Transparent Proxy Pattern.
-   **Audit Proxy Logic Regularly:** Conduct regular audits to ensure that the upgrade mechanism is secure and follows best practices.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#examples "Permanent link")

title: SCWE-005: Insecure Upgradeable Proxy Design
heading: Fixed Proxy Contract with Secure Upgrade Mechanism[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#fixed-proxy-contract-with-secure-upgrade-mechanism "Permanent link")
text:
### Vulnerable Proxy Contract[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#vulnerable-proxy-contract "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.4.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-0-3)contract VulnerableProxy {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-0-4)    address public implementation;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-0-5)    address public owner; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-0-6)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-0-7)    function setImplementation(address _implementation) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-0-8)        require(msg.sender == owner, "Only owner can set implementation");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-0-9)        implementation = _implementation;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-0-10)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-0-11)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-0-12)    function () public payable {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-0-13)        address _impl = implementation;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-0-14)        require(_impl != address(0), "Implementation address is zero");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-0-15)        assembly {            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-0-16)            let result := delegatecall(gas, _impl, add(msg.data, 0x20), mload(msg.data), 0, 0)            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-0-17)            let size := returndatasize            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-0-18)            let ptr := mload(0x40)            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-0-19)            return(ptr, size)        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-0-20)        }    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-0-21)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-0-22)}`

In this example, the `VulnerableProxy` contract allows the owner to update the implementation contract. If the owner is compromised, they can point the proxy to a malicious implementation, allowing the attacker to control the contract's logic.

title: SCWE-005: Insecure Upgradeable Proxy Design
heading: Fixed Proxy Contract with Secure Upgrade Mechanism[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#fixed-proxy-contract-with-secure-upgrade-mechanism "Permanent link")
text:
### Fixed Proxy Contract with Secure Upgrade Mechanism[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#fixed-proxy-contract-with-secure-upgrade-mechanism "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.4.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-3)contract SecureProxy {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-4)    address public implementation;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-5)    address public owner;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-6)    uint public lastUpgradeTime;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-7)    uint public upgradeDelay = 1 days;  // 24 hours delay before upgrade [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-8)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-9)    modifier onlyOwner() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-10)        require(msg.sender == owner, "Only owner can perform this action");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-11)        _;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-12)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-13)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-14)    modifier upgradeable() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-15)        require(block.timestamp >= lastUpgradeTime + upgradeDelay, "Upgrade not allowed yet");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-16)        _;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-17)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-18)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-19)    function setImplementation(address _implementation) public onlyOwner upgradeable {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-20)        implementation = _implementation;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-21)        lastUpgradeTime = block.timestamp; // Update the last upgrade time    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-22)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-23)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-24)    function () public payable {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-25)        address _impl = implementation;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-26)        require(_impl != address(0), "Implementation address is zero");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-27)        assembly {            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-28)            let result := delegatecall(gas, _impl, add(msg.data, 0x20), mload(msg.data), 0, 0)            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-29)            let size := returndatasize            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-30)            let ptr := mload(0x40)            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-31)            return(ptr, size)        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-32)        }    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-33)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-005/#__codelineno-1-34)}`

In the fixed `SecureProxy` contract, the following changes have been made:

# SCWE-006: Inconsistent Inheritance Hierarchy

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-006/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-710: Improper Adherence to Coding Standards [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/710.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/710.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-006/#description "Permanent link")

Inconsistent inheritance hierarchies occur when a contract inherits from multiple contracts or libraries in an inconsistent or contradictory way. This leads to unexpected behavior or errors due to conflicting function implementations, state variables, or access controls. A proper and consistent inheritance structure is essential for clear logic and predictable contract execution.

Some common issues in inheritance hierarchies include: - Ambiguous function overrides. - Conflicting variable definitions. - Misuse of multiple inheritance, which can lead to the diamond problem.

Inconsistent inheritance can significantly compromise a contract’s functionality and security, especially when multiple contracts or libraries with similar function names are used.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-006/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Clear Inheritance Structure:** Ensure that the inheritance hierarchy is logically structured and does not have overlapping functionalities or conflicting state variables.
-   **Use Explicit Overrides:** Clearly override functions when necessary to avoid ambiguity, and ensure there is no unintentional function masking.
-   **Favor Single Inheritance or Controlled Multiple Inheritance:** Avoid overly complex inheritance structures; if multiple inheritance is necessary, consider using design patterns like the Diamond Problem Resolver (i.e., using interfaces or abstract contracts).
-   **Regular Audits:** Periodically audit the inheritance structure to identify any inconsistencies early on.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-006/#examples "Permanent link")

``[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-006/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.4.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-006/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-006/#__codelineno-0-3)contract ParentA {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-006/#__codelineno-0-4)    uint public value; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-006/#__codelineno-0-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-006/#__codelineno-0-6)    function setValue(uint _value) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-006/#__codelineno-0-7)        value = _value;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-006/#__codelineno-0-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-006/#__codelineno-0-9)} [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-006/#__codelineno-0-10)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-006/#__codelineno-0-11)contract ParentB {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-006/#__codelineno-0-12)    uint public value; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-006/#__codelineno-0-13)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-006/#__codelineno-0-14)    function setValue(uint _value) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-006/#__codelineno-0-15)        value = _value * 2;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-006/#__codelineno-0-16)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-006/#__codelineno-0-17)} [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-006/#__codelineno-0-18)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-006/#__codelineno-0-19)contract Child is ParentA, ParentB {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-006/#__codelineno-0-20)    function setValue(uint _value) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-006/#__codelineno-0-21)        // Ambiguity: which `setValue` should be called?        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-006/#__codelineno-0-22)        ParentA.setValue(_value);    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-006/#__codelineno-0-23)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-006/#__codelineno-0-24)}``

In the above example, the `Child` contract inherits from both `ParentA` and `ParentB`. Both parent contracts define the `setValue` function. There is no clear indication of which function should be called, leading to ambiguity and potential bugs or undesired behavior.

# SCWE-051: Improper Use of CREATE2 for Contract Deployment

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   **CWE-706: Use of Incorrectly-Resolved Name or Reference**
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/706.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/706.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#description "Permanent link")

The `CREATE2` opcode allows for deterministic contract deployment, meaning the contract's address can be precomputed before deployment. However, improper handling of the salt parameter, constructor arguments, or contract bytecode can lead to vulnerabilities such as address predictability, re-deployment attacks, and malicious contract substitution. If an attacker can influence the salt or code, they may deploy a contract at a known address before the legitimate one, leading to security risks.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#remediation "Permanent link")

To prevent misuse of `CREATE2`:
\- Use unpredictable and unique salt values (e.g., incorporating nonces, sender addresses, or randomness).
\- Ensure the deployed contract logic remains consistent to prevent re-deployment attacks.
\- Hash important contract parameters into the salt to prevent unintended address collisions.


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#__codelineno-0-3)contract Factory {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#__codelineno-0-4)    function deploy(bytes32 salt, bytes memory bytecode) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#__codelineno-0-5)        address deployed;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#__codelineno-0-6)        assembly {            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#__codelineno-0-7)            deployed := create2(0, add(bytecode, 0x20), mload(bytecode), salt)        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#__codelineno-0-8)        }    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#__codelineno-0-9)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#__codelineno-0-10)}`

**Why is this vulnerable?**

-   If `salt` is predictable (e.g., user-supplied or a static value), an attacker can precompute and front-run the deployment.
-   The same contract address can be re-used by deploying different bytecode, leading to logic changes at a fixed address.
-   No validation ensures that the deployed contract is safe or expected.

title: SCWE-051: Improper Use of CREATE2 for Contract Deployment
heading: Fixed Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#fixed-contract-example "Permanent link")
text:
### Fixed Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#fixed-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#__codelineno-1-3)contract SecureFactory {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#__codelineno-1-4)    function deploy(bytes32 salt, bytes memory bytecode) public returns (address) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#__codelineno-1-5)        require(bytecode.length > 0, "Bytecode cannot be empty"); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#__codelineno-1-6)        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#__codelineno-1-7)        // Ensure the salt includes sender information to prevent front-running        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#__codelineno-1-8)        bytes32 secureSalt = keccak256(abi.encodePacked(msg.sender, salt)); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#__codelineno-1-9)        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#__codelineno-1-10)        address deployed;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#__codelineno-1-11)        assembly {            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#__codelineno-1-12)            deployed := create2(0, add(bytecode, 0x20), mload(bytecode), secureSalt)        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#__codelineno-1-13)        } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#__codelineno-1-14)        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#__codelineno-1-15)        require(deployed != address(0), "Deployment failed");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#__codelineno-1-16)        return deployed;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#__codelineno-1-17)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-051/#__codelineno-1-18)}`

**Why is this safe?** - Uses `keccak256(abi.encodePacked(msg.sender, salt))` to make the salt unique per sender. - Ensures the contract bytecode is non-empty before deploying. - Validates that the deployed contract is nonzero, ensuring a successful deployment.

**By securing CREATE2 deployments, developers can prevent predictable contract addresses, front-running risks, and contract replacement vulnerabilities.**

# SCWE-052: Transaction Order Dependence

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-052/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/400.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/400.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-052/#description "Permanent link")

Transaction Order Dependence (TOD) occurs when the outcome of a contract's execution depends on the order of transactions. Attackers can exploit this issue by submitting transactions in a specific order, manipulating the contract's state and gaining an unfair advantage, such as front-running or back-running other transactions. This can lead to unexpected behavior and resource consumption.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-052/#remediation "Permanent link")

To mitigate TOD vulnerabilities, ensure that the contract's logic does not depend on transaction order. Use techniques like commit-reveal schemes or randomization to prevent attackers from predicting the transaction order and exploiting it.


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-052/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-052/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-052/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-052/#__codelineno-0-3)contract TODExample {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-052/#__codelineno-0-4)    address public winner; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-052/#__codelineno-0-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-052/#__codelineno-0-6)    function bid() public payable {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-052/#__codelineno-0-7)        require(msg.value > 1 ether, "Bid too low");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-052/#__codelineno-0-8)        winner = msg.sender;  // Dependent on transaction order    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-052/#__codelineno-0-9)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-052/#__codelineno-0-10)}`


### Fixed Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-052/#fixed-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-052/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-052/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-052/#__codelineno-1-3)contract FixedTODExample {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-052/#__codelineno-1-4)    address public winner;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-052/#__codelineno-1-5)    uint public highestBid; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-052/#__codelineno-1-6)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-052/#__codelineno-1-7)    function bid() public payable {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-052/#__codelineno-1-8)        require(msg.value > highestBid, "Bid too low");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-052/#__codelineno-1-9)        highestBid = msg.value;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-052/#__codelineno-1-10)        winner = msg.sender;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-052/#__codelineno-1-11)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-052/#__codelineno-1-12)}`

# SCWE-064: Incorrect Inheritance Order

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-064/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-1001: Variable Shadowing
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1001.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1001.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-064/#description "Permanent link")

Incorrect inheritance order in Solidity can lead to unintended behavior, especially when multiple base contracts define similar variables or functions. Solidity’s linearization of the inheritance order can result in one contract unintentionally overriding or shadowing variables or functions defined in a parent contract, leading to confusion, errors, and potential vulnerabilities.

In Solidity, the order of inheritance matters. If the inheritance hierarchy is not properly structured, the wrong version of a variable or function may be called, causing bugs or security issues.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-064/#remediation "Permanent link")

To mitigate this vulnerability, carefully review and order the inheritance structure. Ensure that parent contracts are inherited in a logical sequence and that any variables or functions are not unintentionally shadowed or overridden. Consider following a clear and consistent inheritance pattern.


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-064/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

# SCWE-070: Incorrect Constructor Name

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-070/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-1001: Variable Shadowing
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1001.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1001.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-070/#description "Permanent link")

In Solidity, the constructor is a special function used to initialize a contract's state variables when it is deployed. If a constructor is incorrectly named, it will not function as expected, leading to issues such as failing to initialize state variables or triggering unexpected behavior. The constructor must have the exact name of the contract and no return type.

If the constructor name is not correct, it will not be executed as intended, and the contract may not behave as expected, potentially leaving it in an uninitialized or inconsistent state.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-070/#remediation "Permanent link")

Ensure that the constructor has the correct name, which must match the contract name and contain no return type. In newer versions of Solidity (0.4.22 and later), the constructor keyword is used instead of the contract name for constructor functions.


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-070/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-070/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.4.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-070/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-070/#__codelineno-0-3)contract Example {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-070/#__codelineno-0-4)    uint public value; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-070/#__codelineno-0-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-070/#__codelineno-0-6)    // In Solidity <0.4.22, constructor had to match contract name. In 0.5+, this is a regular function, not a constructor.    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-070/#__codelineno-0-7)    function Example() public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-070/#__codelineno-0-8)        value = 10;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-070/#__codelineno-0-9)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-070/#__codelineno-0-10)}`


### Fixed Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-070/#fixed-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-070/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-070/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-070/#__codelineno-1-3)contract Example {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-070/#__codelineno-1-4)    uint public value; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-070/#__codelineno-1-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-070/#__codelineno-1-6)    // Correct constructor definition (Solidity >=0.4.22)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-070/#__codelineno-1-7)    constructor() {  // Use "constructor" instead of the contract name        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-070/#__codelineno-1-8)        value = 10;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-070/#__codelineno-1-9)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-070/#__codelineno-1-10)}`

# SCWE-071: Uninitialized Storage Pointer

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-071/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-457: Use of Uninitialized Variable
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/457.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/457.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-071/#description "Permanent link")

An uninitialized storage pointer in Solidity refers to a variable that has been declared but not assigned a value before being used. This can result in unpredictable behavior, as the variable might point to unintended locations in the contract's storage, potentially exposing sensitive data or allowing attackers to exploit the uninitialized pointer. This is a critical issue because Solidity does not automatically initialize storage variables, leaving them with default values that may be unsafe.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-071/#remediation "Permanent link")

Always initialize storage pointers to avoid potential vulnerabilities. Ensure that all variables, especially storage pointers, are properly assigned a value before being used. This prevents accessing uninitialized or garbage data from the contract’s storage.


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-071/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-071/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-071/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-071/#__codelineno-0-3)contract Example {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-071/#__codelineno-0-4)    uint[] public data; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-071/#__codelineno-0-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-071/#__codelineno-0-6)    // Uninitialized storage pointer, could lead to unexpected behavior    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-071/#__codelineno-0-7)    function addData(uint _value) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-071/#__codelineno-0-8)        data.push(_value);        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-071/#__codelineno-0-9)        uint[] storage uninitializedPointer;  // Pointer is uninitialized        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-071/#__codelineno-0-10)        uninitializedPointer.push(10);  // Accessing uninitialized storage pointer    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-071/#__codelineno-0-11)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-071/#__codelineno-0-12)}`

**Why is this vulnerable?** - `uninitializedPointer` is a storage pointer but is not assigned a reference to valid storage. - Writing to `uninitializedPointer.push(10);` could overwrite unintended storage locations.

**Potential outcomes:** - Corrupting storage layout (e.g., overwriting contract variables). - Unexpected behaviors due to storage reallocation.

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-071/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-071/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-071/#__codelineno-1-3)contract Example {       [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-071/#__codelineno-1-4)      uint[] public data; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-071/#__codelineno-1-5)      [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-071/#__codelineno-1-6)      function addData(uint _value) public {          [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-071/#__codelineno-1-7)          data.push(_value);          [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-071/#__codelineno-1-8)          uint[] storage initializedPointer = data;  // ✅ Properly initialized storage pointer          [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-071/#__codelineno-1-9)          initializedPointer.push(10);  // ✅ Safely interacts with the intended storage      [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-071/#__codelineno-1-10)      }  [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-071/#__codelineno-1-11)  }`

**Why is this safe?** - `initializedPointer` explicitly references `data`, ensuring that it does not point to an arbitrary storage slot. - Prevents unintended overwrites of contract state. - Ensures expected behavior and protects contract integrity.

# SCWE-080: Incorrect Type Conversion

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-080/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   **CWE-704: Incorrect Type Conversion or Cast**
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/704.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/704.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-080/#description "Permanent link")

Incorrect type conversion occurs when a value is cast or implicitly converted between incompatible types, potentially leading to precision loss, unexpected behavior, or security vulnerabilities. Solidity allows certain implicit conversions (e.g., from `uint256` to `uint8`), which can lead to silent truncation of data. Additionally, casting between types like `address` and `uint` can lead to unexpected security risks.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-080/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Avoid unsafe downcasts from larger to smaller types unless explicitly required.
-   Always validate the range before converting between numerical types.
-   Use explicit conversion functions where applicable, ensuring proper handling of edge cases.


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-080/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-080/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-080/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-080/#__codelineno-0-3)contract Example {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-080/#__codelineno-0-4)    function unsafeDowncast(uint256 value) public pure returns (uint8) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-080/#__codelineno-0-5)        return uint8(value);  // ❌ Truncates value if > 255    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-080/#__codelineno-0-6)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-080/#__codelineno-0-7)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-080/#__codelineno-0-8)    function unsafeAddressToUint(address addr) public pure returns (uint256) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-080/#__codelineno-0-9)        return uint256(uint160(addr));  // ❌ May lead to unexpected behaviors    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-080/#__codelineno-0-10)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-080/#__codelineno-0-11)}`

**Why is this vulnerable?**

-   `uint8(value)` will silently truncate values above 255, leading to unintended loss of data.
-   `uint256(uint160(addr))` might be used incorrectly in arithmetic operations, potentially allowing address manipulation.

title: SCWE-080: Incorrect Type Conversion
heading: Fixed Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-080/#fixed-contract-example "Permanent link")
text:
### Fixed Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-080/#fixed-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-080/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-080/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-080/#__codelineno-1-3)contract SecureExample {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-080/#__codelineno-1-4)    function safeDowncast(uint256 value) public pure returns (uint8) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-080/#__codelineno-1-5)        require(value <= type(uint8).max, "Value exceeds uint8 range");  // ✅ Ensure valid range        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-080/#__codelineno-1-6)        return uint8(value);    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-080/#__codelineno-1-7)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-080/#__codelineno-1-8)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-080/#__codelineno-1-9)    function safeAddressToUint(address addr) public pure returns (uint160) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-080/#__codelineno-1-10)        return uint160(addr);  // ✅ Restrict conversion to valid 160-bit range    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-080/#__codelineno-1-11)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-080/#__codelineno-1-12)}`

**Why is this safe?**

-   Ensures that values do not exceed the allowed range before downcasting.
-   Restricts type conversion to avoid security risks from improper arithmetic operations.
-   Prevents silent data loss that could lead to unintended contract behavior.

**By enforcing safe type conversions, developers can ensure contract logic remains reliable and free from unexpected truncation issues.**

# SCWE-098: Initialization Front-Running in Upgradeable Contracts

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-098/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-284: Improper Access Control
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/284.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/284.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-098/#description "Permanent link")

Proxy-based contracts ship without constructors; if the initializer is callable by anyone, an attacker can front-run deployment and seize ownership, set trusted roles, or lock upgrades. This permanently compromises the implementation behind the proxy.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-098/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Protect initializer functions with access control and `initializer`/`reinitializer` guards.
-   Invoke initialization atomically during deployment or via a deploy-time call data payload.
-   Use `disableInitializers()` on the implementation contract to prevent accidental takeover.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-098/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-098/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-098/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-098/#__codelineno-0-2)import "@openzeppelin/contracts-upgradeable/proxy/utils/Initializable.sol"; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-098/#__codelineno-0-3)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-098/#__codelineno-0-4)contract UpgradeableVault is Initializable {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-098/#__codelineno-0-5)    address public owner; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-098/#__codelineno-0-6)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-098/#__codelineno-0-7)    function initialize(address _owner) public initializer {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-098/#__codelineno-0-8)        owner = _owner; // anyone can front-run and become owner    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-098/#__codelineno-0-9)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-098/#__codelineno-0-10)}`


### Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-098/#fixed "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-098/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-098/#__codelineno-1-2)import "@openzeppelin/contracts-upgradeable/proxy/utils/Initializable.sol"; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-098/#__codelineno-1-3)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-098/#__codelineno-1-4)contract UpgradeableVault is Initializable {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-098/#__codelineno-1-5)    address public owner; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-098/#__codelineno-1-6)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-098/#__codelineno-1-7)    function initialize(address _owner, address deployer) public initializer {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-098/#__codelineno-1-8)        require(msg.sender == deployer, "only deployer");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-098/#__codelineno-1-9)        owner = _owner;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-098/#__codelineno-1-10)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-098/#__codelineno-1-11)}`

Deployer (or factory) deploys the proxy and calls `initialize(owner, address(this))` in the same transaction — no window for front-running.

# SCWE-099: Storage Layout Collision on Upgrade

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-099/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-664: Improper Control of a Resource Through its Lifetime
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/664.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/664.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-099/#description "Permanent link")

Upgradeable contracts rely on stable storage slots. Reordering, removing, or inserting state variables (or changing inheritance order) between versions causes storage collisions when the proxy reuses the same slots, corrupting balances, roles, or configuration.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-099/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Freeze variable ordering; only append new variables.
-   Reserve gaps (`uint256[50] private __gap;`) to allow future expansion.
-   Use automated storage layout diffing and follow upgrade-safe patterns (e.g., OZ Upgradeable tooling).


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-099/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-099/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-099/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-099/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-099/#__codelineno-0-3)contract V1 {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-099/#__codelineno-0-4)    address public owner;   // slot 0    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-099/#__codelineno-0-5)    uint256 public balance; // slot 1 [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-099/#__codelineno-0-6)} [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-099/#__codelineno-0-7)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-099/#__codelineno-0-8)contract V2 is V1 {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-099/#__codelineno-0-9)    uint256 public balance; // reuses slot 1, corrupts state    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-099/#__codelineno-0-10)    address public treasury; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-099/#__codelineno-0-11)}`


### Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-099/#fixed "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-099/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-099/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-099/#__codelineno-1-3)contract V1 {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-099/#__codelineno-1-4)    address public owner;   // slot 0    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-099/#__codelineno-1-5)    uint256 public balance; // slot 1    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-099/#__codelineno-1-6)    uint256[48] private __gap; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-099/#__codelineno-1-7)} [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-099/#__codelineno-1-8)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-099/#__codelineno-1-9)contract V2 is V1 {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-099/#__codelineno-1-10)    uint256 public treasuryFee; // slot 2 (after gap) [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-099/#__codelineno-1-11)}`

# SCWE-117: Proxy Implementation Selfdestruct Exposure

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-117/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-284: Improper Access Control
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/284.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/284.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-117/#description "Permanent link")

If the proxy’s implementation contract exposes `selfdestruct` (or `SELFDESTRUCT` reachable through a function), an attacker or careless admin can destroy the implementation. The proxy then points to a non-existent code address, bricking upgrades or locking funds.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-117/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Remove or disable `selfdestruct` in implementations; use `disableInitializers()` patterns.
-   Gate any destruct-like functionality behind timelock + multisig and migration plans.
-   Monitor implementation addresses and block upgrades that reduce code size to zero.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-117/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-117/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

### Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-117/#fixed "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-117/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-117/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-117/#__codelineno-1-3)contract Impl {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-117/#__codelineno-1-4)    // no selfdestruct path; migrations use new proxy with state copy [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-117/#__codelineno-1-5)}`

# SCWE-118: Unauthenticated Beacon Upgrade

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-118/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/306.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/306.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-118/#description "Permanent link")

Beacon proxies rely on a beacon address that determines implementation. If the beacon upgrade function lacks proper access control or timelock, an attacker can point all proxies to malicious code, taking over state and funds.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-118/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Restrict beacon upgrades to multisig+timelock and emit events on change.
-   Validate new implementation bytecode (e.g., initializer disabled, interfaces intact).
-   Monitor beacon address changes on-chain with alerts.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-118/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-118/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-118/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-118/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-118/#__codelineno-1-3)contract Beacon {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-118/#__codelineno-1-4)    address public impl;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-118/#__codelineno-1-5)    address public admin;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-118/#__codelineno-1-6)    function upgradeTo(address newImpl) external {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-118/#__codelineno-1-7)        require(msg.sender == admin, "not admin");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-118/#__codelineno-1-8)        impl = newImpl;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-118/#__codelineno-1-9)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-118/#__codelineno-1-10)}`

# SCWE-119: Shared Proxy Admin and Logic Owner Key

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-119/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-284: Improper Access Control
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/284.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/284.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-119/#description "Permanent link")

Using the same key to control both the proxy admin (upgrade rights) and logic contract owner concentrates power. A single key compromise allows hostile upgrades and privileged function abuse with no separation of duties.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-119/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Separate roles: proxy admin under multisig+timelock; logic owner under different multisig.
-   Use role-based access (e.g., OZ AccessControl) and distinct keys for operational vs. upgrade actions.
-   Document and monitor role boundaries; rotate keys periodically.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-119/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-119/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

# SCWE-145: Unvalidated Constructor Parameters

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-145/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-20: Improper Input Validation
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-145/#description "Permanent link")

Constructors that accept critical parameters (owner, oracle, fee recipient, token addresses) without validation can deploy a contract in a broken or insecure state. Zero addresses, invalid values, or inconsistent configuration (e.g., fee > 100%) may be impossible to fix after deployment if there is no setter or upgrade path.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-145/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Validate all constructor parameters: zero address checks, range checks (e.g., fee <= 100%), and consistency checks.
-   Use `require` or custom errors to revert deployment with a clear message when validation fails.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-145/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-145/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-145/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-145/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-145/#__codelineno-0-3)contract Staking {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-145/#__codelineno-0-4)    address public owner;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-145/#__codelineno-0-5)    address public rewardToken;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-145/#__codelineno-0-6)    uint256 public feeBps; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-145/#__codelineno-0-7)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-145/#__codelineno-0-8)    constructor(address _owner, address _rewardToken, uint256 _feeBps) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-145/#__codelineno-0-9)        owner = _owner;           // No validation        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-145/#__codelineno-0-10)        rewardToken = _rewardToken;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-145/#__codelineno-0-11)        feeBps = _feeBps;         // Could be > 10000    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-145/#__codelineno-0-12)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-145/#__codelineno-0-13)}`


### Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-145/#fixed "Permanent link")

title: SCWE-150: Storage Slot Collision When Upgrading Implementation
heading: Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-150/#fixed "Permanent link")
text:
*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-150: Storage Slot Collision When Upgrading Implementation

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-150/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-682: Incorrect Calculation
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/682.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/682.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-150/#description "Permanent link")

When upgrading a proxy's implementation, the new implementation's storage layout must be compatible with the proxy's storage. Appending variables in the implementation without accounting for the proxy's own storage (e.g., admin, implementation address) can cause slot collisions. Similarly, inherited contracts that add state variables can overwrite slots used by the base or proxy. SCWE-099 covers same-contract layout; this addresses cross-contract layout (proxy + implementation, inheritance chain).


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-150/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Use a single storage contract or follow a consistent storage layout convention (e.g., EIP-1967).
-   Reserve gaps (`uint256[50] private __gap`) in base contracts for future expansion.
-   Run storage layout diff tools before upgrading.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-150/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-150/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-150/#__codelineno-0-1)// Proxy [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-150/#__codelineno-0-2)contract Proxy {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-150/#__codelineno-0-3)    address public implementation;  // slot 0    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-150/#__codelineno-0-4)    address public admin;           // slot 1 [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-150/#__codelineno-0-5)} [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-150/#__codelineno-0-6)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-150/#__codelineno-0-7)// Implementation V2 - assumes it "owns" slots from 0 [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-150/#__codelineno-0-8)contract ImplV2 {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-150/#__codelineno-0-9)    address public owner;      // slot 0 - COLLIDES with proxy's implementation    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-150/#__codelineno-0-10)    uint256 public newValue;   // slot 1 - COLLIDES with proxy's admin [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-150/#__codelineno-0-11)}`


### Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-150/#fixed "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-150/#__codelineno-1-1)contract ImplV2 {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-150/#__codelineno-1-2)    // Storage in implementation must not overlap proxy slots    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-150/#__codelineno-1-3)    // Use EIP-1967 or append after reserved slots    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-150/#__codelineno-1-4)    bytes32 private constant IMPLEMENTATION_SLOT = 0x360894...;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-150/#__codelineno-1-5)    // Implementation state starts after proxy slots    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-150/#__codelineno-1-6)    uint256 public newValue; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-ARCH/SCWE-150/#__codelineno-1-7)}`

*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-016: Insufficient Authorization Checks

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-862: Missing Authorization [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/862.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/862.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#description "Permanent link")

Insufficient authorization occurs when the contract does not verify whether a user has the appropriate permissions to perform specific actions. This vulnerability arises when there are missing or improperly implemented authorization checks, allowing unauthorized users to access functions they should not have access to.

Common causes of insufficient authorization include: - Missing access control modifiers or incorrect configuration. - Failure to validate roles before granting access to sensitive functions. - Poor handling of user permissions, which could lead to privilege escalation.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Implement role-based access control (RBAC):** Define roles such as `admin`, `user`, etc., and assign permissions accordingly to ensure only authorized users can call restricted functions.
-   **Use access control modifiers:** Protect sensitive functions with appropriate modifiers (e.g., `onlyOwner`, `onlyAdmin`) to restrict access.
-   **Principle of least privilege:** Ensure each user only has access to the minimal set of actions they need to perform their role.
-   **Thorough testing:** Test for authorization vulnerabilities to ensure all restricted functions are properly secured.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#examples "Permanent link")


### Insufficient Authorization Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#insufficient-authorization-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#__codelineno-0-3)contract InsufficientAuthorization {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#__codelineno-0-4)    uint public balance; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#__codelineno-0-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#__codelineno-0-6)    function withdraw(uint amount) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#__codelineno-0-7)        // No checks for user roles, any address can withdraw funds        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#__codelineno-0-8)        balance -= amount;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#__codelineno-0-9)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#__codelineno-0-10)}`

### Fixed Authorization Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#fixed-authorization-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#__codelineno-1-3)contract FixedAuthorization {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#__codelineno-1-4)    uint public balance;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#__codelineno-1-5)    address public owner; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#__codelineno-1-6)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#__codelineno-1-7)    constructor() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#__codelineno-1-8)        owner = msg.sender;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#__codelineno-1-9)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#__codelineno-1-10)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#__codelineno-1-11)    modifier onlyOwner() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#__codelineno-1-12)        require(msg.sender == owner, "Not authorized");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#__codelineno-1-13)        _;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#__codelineno-1-14)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#__codelineno-1-15)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#__codelineno-1-16)    function withdraw(uint amount) public onlyOwner {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#__codelineno-1-17)        balance -= amount;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#__codelineno-1-18)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-016/#__codelineno-1-19)}`

In the fixed example, the `onlyOwner` modifier ensures that only the contract owner can withdraw funds, thus preventing unauthorized users from performing sensitive operations like withdrawing assets.

# SCWE-017: Privileged Role Mismanagement

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-017/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-269: Improper Privilege Management
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/269.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/269.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-017/#description "Permanent link")

Privileged role mismanagement occurs when a smart contract incorrectly assigns roles or permissions, granting excessive privileges to certain users. This can lead to users obtaining permissions beyond what is necessary for their intended function, creating a potential for privilege escalation or unauthorized actions. In the context of smart contracts, improper privilege management can lead to critical vulnerabilities such as unauthorized contract changes, malicious interactions, or loss of funds.

Common causes include: - Insufficient checks for users attempting to access privileged functions. - Roles being dynamically assigned without validation. - Inadequate access control mechanisms for sensitive contract functions.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-017/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Role-based access control (RBAC):** Implement strict role checks using modifiers to ensure that users can only perform actions that correspond to their assigned roles.
-   **Principle of least privilege:** Limit the privileges of each role to the bare minimum needed to perform their task.
-   **Use of trusted or immutable sources:** Ensure that privileged roles cannot be arbitrarily changed by unauthorized users or during attacks.
-   **Periodic reviews and audits:** Regularly review roles and permissions to ensure they are correctly assigned and maintained.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-017/#examples "Permanent link")


### Privileged Role Mismanagement Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-017/#privileged-role-mismanagement-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-017/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-017/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-017/#__codelineno-0-3)contract PrivilegedRoleMismanagement {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-017/#__codelineno-0-4)    address public admin;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-017/#__codelineno-0-5)    uint public balance; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-017/#__codelineno-0-6)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-017/#__codelineno-0-7)    function setAdmin(address _admin) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-017/#__codelineno-0-8)        admin = _admin;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-017/#__codelineno-0-9)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-017/#__codelineno-0-10)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-017/#__codelineno-0-11)    function withdraw(uint amount) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-017/#__codelineno-0-12)        require(msg.sender == admin, "Only admin can withdraw");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-017/#__codelineno-0-13)        balance -= amount;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-017/#__codelineno-0-14)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-017/#__codelineno-0-15)}`

In the above example, there is no check for the address assigning the `admin` role, and it can be changed by anyone, including malicious actors.

   [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-017/#__codelineno-1-18)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-017/#__codelineno-1-19)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-017/#__codelineno-1-20)    function withdraw(uint amount) public onlyOwner {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-017/#__codelineno-1-21)        balance -= amount; title: SCWE-018: Use of tx.origin for Authorization
heading: Fixed Contract (Using msg.sender for Authorization)[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#fixed-contract-using-msgsender-for-authorization "Permanent link")
text:
*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-018: Use of tx.origin for Authorization

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   **CWE-346**: Origin Validation Error
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/346.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/346.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#description "Permanent link")

The use of `tx.origin` for authorization is a security vulnerability in which a smart contract checks the origin of the transaction to determine if a user is authorized to perform an action. This approach is flawed because `tx.origin` can be exploited by an attacker through a chain of transactions, allowing unauthorized users to interact with the contract. An attacker could trick the contract into performing an action on behalf of the victim by utilizing another contract in the transaction chain.

**Key Issues**: - Allows unauthorized transactions by using the `tx.origin` variable instead of `msg.sender`. - Vulnerable to phishing and reentrancy attacks, where attackers can use contracts to impersonate the victim. - Mismanagement of roles and improper transaction flow handling.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Use `msg.sender` instead of `tx.origin`**: Always rely on `msg.sender` for authentication and authorization, as it correctly represents the immediate sender of the current call.
-   **Strict validation checks**: Ensure that authorization checks are done on the direct sender of the transaction, i.e., `msg.sender`, and not the originator.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable Contract (Using `tx.origin` for Authorization)[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#vulnerable-contract-using-txorigin-for-authorization "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#__codelineno-0-3)contract Vulnerable {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#__codelineno-0-4)    address public owner; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#__codelineno-0-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#__codelineno-0-6)    constructor() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#__codelineno-0-7)        owner = msg.sender;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#__codelineno-0-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#__codelineno-0-9)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#__codelineno-0-10)    function restrictedAction() public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#__codelineno-0-11)        require(tx.origin == owner, "Only the owner can perform this action");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#__codelineno-0-12)        // Action code here    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#__codelineno-0-13)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#__codelineno-0-14)}`

In the vulnerable contract, the authorization check uses `tx.origin` to validate the caller. This is a problem because if the contract is called via another contract, `tx.origin` will return the original transaction sender (not the immediate caller), which opens up the contract to attacks such as phishing. The attacker can create a contract that interacts with the vulnerable contract on behalf of the victim.

title: SCWE-018: Use of tx.origin for Authorization
heading: Fixed Contract (Using msg.sender for Authorization)[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#fixed-contract-using-msgsender-for-authorization "Permanent link")
text:
### Fixed Contract (Using msg.sender for Authorization)[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#fixed-contract-using-msgsender-for-authorization "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#__codelineno-1-3)contract Secure {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#__codelineno-1-4)    address public owner; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#__codelineno-1-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#__codelineno-1-6)    constructor() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#__codelineno-1-7)        owner = msg.sender;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#__codelineno-1-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#__codelineno-1-9)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#__codelineno-1-10)    function restrictedAction() public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#__codelineno-1-11)        require(msg.sender == owner, "Only the owner can perform this action");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#__codelineno-1-12)        // Action code here    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#__codelineno-1-13)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-018/#__codelineno-1-14)}`

In the fixed contract, `msg.sender` is used instead of `tx.origin`. This ensures that the contract checks the immediate sender of the call, which prevents attacks where malicious contracts impersonate the victim.
