*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-019: Insecure Signature Verification

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/347.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/347.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#description "Permanent link")

Insecure signature verification occurs when a contract improperly verifies a cryptographic signature or fails to securely validate signatures, allowing attackers to forge or manipulate them. This vulnerability can allow unauthorized transactions or the bypassing of important security mechanisms, potentially leading to fraud, unauthorized access, or other attacks.

Common causes of insecure signature verification include: - Not validating the signer's address. - Using weak or outdated cryptographic libraries. - Failing to check signature validity before processing actions. - Incorrectly handling the signature format.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Verify signatures properly:** Always verify that the signature matches the intended signer by using the `ecrecover` function for Ethereum addresses and comparing the result to the expected signer address.
-   **Use strong cryptographic methods:** Ensure the use of robust cryptographic techniques and libraries. Avoid using outdated or weak algorithms.
-   **Use secure signature formats:** Make sure that signature formats are validated properly (e.g., ensure proper handling of `v`, `r`, `s` values in Ethereum signatures).
-   **Implement checks before acting on the signature:** Always perform checks for valid signature and relevant parameters before executing any logic that could be influenced by the signature.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#examples "Permanent link")

title: SCWE-019: Insecure Signature Verification
heading: Fixed Signature Verification[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#fixed-signature-verification "Permanent link")
text:
### Insecure Signature Verification[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#insecure-signature-verification "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-0-3)contract InsecureSignatureExample {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-0-4)    address public owner; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-0-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-0-6)    constructor() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-0-7)        owner = msg.sender;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-0-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-0-9)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-0-10)    // Insecure signature verification: does not properly validate the signature    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-0-11)    function executeTransaction(bytes32 hash, uint8 v, bytes32 r, bytes32 s) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-0-12)        address signer = ecrecover(hash, v, r, s);  // Signature verification        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-0-13)        if (signer == owner) {            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-0-14)            // Execute some sensitive action        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-0-15)        }    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-0-16)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-0-17)}`

In the insecure version, the contract checks if the signature corresponds to the owner but does not properly validate or handle potential issues with the signature, such as its format or correctness.


### Fixed Signature Verification[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#fixed-signature-verification "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-1-3)contract SecureSignatureExample {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-1-4)    address public owner; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-1-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-1-6)    constructor() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-1-7)        owner = msg.sender;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-1-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-1-9)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-1-10)    // Secure signature verification: properly checks signature and signer    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-1-11)    function executeTransaction(bytes32 hash, uint8 v, bytes32 r, bytes32 s) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-1-12)        address signer = ecrecover(hash, v, r, s);        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-1-13)        require(signer == owner, "Invalid signature");  // Ensure valid signature before proceeding        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-1-14)        // Execute some sensitive action    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-1-15)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-019/#__codelineno-1-16)}`

In the fixed version, we use the `require()` function to ensure the signature matches the owner's address, thereby improving security by preventing unauthorized access or actions.

# SCWE-020: Absence of Time-Locked Functions

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-840: Business Logic Errors [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/840.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/840.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#description "Permanent link")

Absence of time-locked functions occurs when smart contracts do not implement mechanisms to delay certain critical functions or actions based on time conditions. This can result in the contract allowing actions that should be restricted or postponed for a certain period, such as emergency fund withdrawals or sensitive administrative actions. Without time-locking mechanisms, malicious actors or faulty logic could trigger these actions at the wrong time, leading to undesired outcomes.

Time-locking is commonly used in scenarios like: - Delaying admin or owner functions to prevent immediate misuse. - Ensuring withdrawal or fund transfer happens only after a predefined delay. - Enabling emergency actions only after a certain time or under specific conditions.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Implement time-locked functions:** Ensure that critical functions, especially those related to fund transfers or administrative actions, are protected by a time lock, delaying their execution until an appropriate time has passed.
-   **Use block timestamps:** Leverage block timestamps or block numbers to control the execution of functions.
-   **Limit emergency access:** If implementing emergency mechanisms, ensure that there are time delays before they can be invoked, to reduce the chance of misuse.
-   **Review time-based logic regularly:** Verify the correctness of time-based logic to ensure that the system behaves as intended.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#examples "Permanent link")

title: SCWE-020: Absence of Time-Locked Functions
heading: Time-Locked Function Implementation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#time-locked-function-implementation "Permanent link")
text:
### Absence of Time-Locked Function[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#absence-of-time-locked-function "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-0-3)contract NoTimeLock {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-0-4)    address public owner;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-0-5)    uint public funds; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-0-6)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-0-7)    constructor() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-0-8)        owner = msg.sender;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-0-9)        funds = 1000;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-0-10)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-0-11)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-0-12)    // Critical function without time-lock    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-0-13)    function withdrawFunds(uint amount) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-0-14)        require(msg.sender == owner, "Not the owner");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-0-15)        funds -= amount;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-0-16)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-0-17)}`

In this example, the contract lacks any time-lock mechanism, allowing the owner to withdraw funds at any time, which could be dangerous if mishandled.

text:
### Time-Locked Function Implementation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#time-locked-function-implementation "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-1-3)contract TimeLockExample {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-1-4)    address public owner;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-1-5)    uint public funds;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-1-6)    uint public lastWithdrawalTime;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-1-7)    uint public withdrawalDelay = 1 weeks; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-1-8)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-1-9)    constructor() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-1-10)        owner = msg.sender;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-1-11)        funds = 1000;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-1-12)        lastWithdrawalTime = block.timestamp;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-1-13)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-1-14)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-1-15)    // Critical function with time-lock    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-1-16)    function withdrawFunds(uint amount) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-1-17)        require(msg.sender == owner, "Not the owner");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-1-18)        require(block.timestamp >= lastWithdrawalTime + withdrawalDelay, "Time lock not expired"); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-1-19)        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-1-20)        lastWithdrawalTime = block.timestamp;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-1-21)        funds -= amount;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-1-22)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-020/#__codelineno-1-23)}`

In the fixed version, a time-lock mechanism is implemented, ensuring that the owner can only withdraw funds after a certain delay (e.g., one week). This provides an added layer of security, particularly in cases where emergency withdrawals or administrative actions are necessary but should not be immediate.

text:
*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-038: Insecure Use of Selfdestruct

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-038/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-732: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
    [CWE-732 Link](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/732.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-038/#description "Permanent link")

Insecure use of selfdestruct refers to vulnerabilities that arise when the `selfdestruct` function is used without proper safeguards. This can lead to: - Unauthorized destruction of the contract. - Loss of funds or data. - Exploitation of vulnerabilities in contract logic.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-038/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Restrict access:** Ensure only authorized addresses can call `selfdestruct`. Note: `selfdestruct` is deprecated per EIP-6049 (Solidity 0.8.24+); prefer migration patterns where possible.
-   **Implement circuit breakers:** Add mechanisms to halt operations in case of suspicious activity.
-   **Test thoroughly:** Conduct extensive testing to ensure `selfdestruct` is used securely.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-038/#examples "Permanent link")

-   **Insecure Selfdestruct Usage**

    `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-038/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-038/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-038/#__codelineno-0-3)contract InsecureSelfdestruct {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-038/#__codelineno-0-4)    function destroy() public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-038/#__codelineno-0-5)        selfdestruct(payable(msg.sender)); // No access control    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-038/#__codelineno-0-6)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-038/#__codelineno-0-7)}`

-   **Secure Selfdestruct Usage**

# SCWE-045: Insecure Use of Modifiers

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-732: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
    [CWE-732 Link](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/732.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#description "Permanent link")

Insecure use of modifiers refers to vulnerabilities that arise when modifiers are used improperly. This can lead to: - Unauthorized actions by malicious actors. - Loss of funds or data. - Exploitation of vulnerabilities in contract logic.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Restrict access:** Ensure only authorized addresses can use the modifier.
-   **Validate inputs:** Ensure all inputs to the modifier are properly validated.
-   **Test thoroughly:** Conduct extensive testing to ensure modifiers are secure.

title: SCWE-045: Insecure Use of Modifiers
heading: Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#examples "Permanent link")
text:
## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#examples "Permanent link")

-   **Insecure Modifier Usage (With Storage Bug)**

    `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-0-3)contract InsecureModifier {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-0-4)    address public admin; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-0-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-0-6)    constructor(address _admin) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-0-7)        admin = _admin; // ❌ Storage bug: Allows setting admin to zero address.    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-0-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-0-9)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-0-10)    modifier onlyAdmin() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-0-11)        require(admin == address(0), "Unauthorized"); // ❌ Wrong condition, only works if admin is zero!        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-0-12)        _;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-0-13)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-0-14)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-0-15)    function updateAdmin(address newAdmin) public onlyAdmin {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-0-16)        admin = newAdmin; // ❌ Can set admin to zero address, breaking access control.    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-0-17)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-0-18)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-0-19)    function updateBalance(uint newBalance) public onlyAdmin {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-0-20)        // Update balance    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-0-21)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-0-22)}`


**Why is this Insecure?** - Wrong Condition in `onlyAdmin()` - `require(admin == address(0), "Unauthorized");` only allows function execution when admin is zero. - This means no valid admin can ever execute admin functions! - If admin is ever non-zero, all `onlyAdmin` functions become unusable.

-   Loss of Control

    -   If admin is accidentally set to `address(0)`, anyone can now execute admin functions, breaking security
-   **Secure Modifier Usage**

    `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-1-3)contract SecureModifier {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-1-4)    address public admin; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-1-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-1-6)    constructor(address _admin) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-1-7)        require(_admin != address(0), "Invalid admin address"); // ✅ Proper validation        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-1-8)        admin = _admin;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-1-9)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-1-10)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-1-11)    modifier onlyAdmin() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-1-12)        require(msg.sender == admin, "Unauthorized"); // ✅ Correctly restricts access        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-1-13)        _;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-1-14)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-04

title: SCWE-045: Insecure Use of Modifiers
heading: Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#examples "Permanent link")
text:
5/#__codelineno-1-15)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-1-16)    function updateAdmin(address newAdmin) public onlyAdmin {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-1-17)        require(newAdmin != address(0), "New admin cannot be zero address"); // ✅ Prevents admin loss        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-1-18)        admin = newAdmin;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-1-19)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-1-20)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-1-21)    function updateBalance(uint newBalance) public onlyAdmin {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-1-22)        // Update balance securely    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-1-23)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-045/#__codelineno-1-24)}`


**Why is this Secure?** - Proper access control in `onlyAdmin()` - `require(msg.sender == admin, "Unauthorized");` ensures only the correct admin can execute admin functions. - Prevents privilege escalation - `updateAdmin()` prevents setting `admin = address(0)`, avoiding unintended loss of access.

# SCWE-049: Unprotected Ether Withdrawal

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-049/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-732: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/732.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/732.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-049/#description "Permanent link")

Unprotected Ether withdrawal occurs when a smart contract allows withdrawal of Ether (ETH) without sufficient access control or proper authorization mechanisms. This vulnerability exposes the contract to unauthorized or malicious users, enabling them to drain funds without any checks on the withdrawal request.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-049/#remediation "Permanent link")

To prevent this vulnerability, implement strong access control mechanisms like the `onlyOwner` modifier or a more flexible role-based access control (RBAC) system. Ensure that only authorized users (e.g., the contract owner or specific users) can initiate Ether withdrawals. Always verify user permissions before allowing access to critical contract functions.


## Impact[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-049/#impact "Permanent link")

An attacker can exploit this vulnerability to withdraw Ether from the contract, leading to potential financial loss. This could result in a total loss of funds if no protective measures are in place, exposing the contract and its users to significant risks.


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-049/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-049/#__codelineno-0-1)contract EtherWallet {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-049/#__codelineno-0-2)    address public owner; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-049/#__codelineno-0-3)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-049/#__codelineno-0-4)    constructor() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-049/#__codelineno-0-5)        owner = msg.sender;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-049/#__codelineno-0-6)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-049/#__codelineno-0-7)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-049/#__codelineno-0-8)    function withdraw(uint amount) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-049/#__codelineno-0-9)        (bool ok, ) = msg.sender.call{value: amount}("");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-049/#__codelineno-0-10)        require(ok, "Transfer failed");  // No access control    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-049/#__codelineno-0-11)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-049/#__codelineno-0-12)}`

# SCWE-050: Unprotected SELFDESTRUCT Instruction

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-050/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-732: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/732.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/732.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-050/#description "Permanent link")

The `SELFDESTRUCT` instruction in Ethereum allows a contract to destroy itself and send its remaining Ether balance to a specified address. If this instruction is not properly protected with access controls, an attacker could trigger it, causing the contract to self-destruct and possibly transferring all the funds to an unauthorized address. This can result in the total loss of funds or disruption of contract functionality.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-050/#remediation "Permanent link")

To mitigate this vulnerability, it is crucial to protect the `SELFDESTRUCT` instruction with proper access control mechanisms. Only authorized users, such as the contract owner or admin, should be allowed to call the `SELFDESTRUCT` function. Consider using modifiers like `onlyOwner` or a role-based access control system to enforce permission checks before allowing this critical operation. **Note:** `selfdestruct` is deprecated per EIP-6049 (Solidity 0.8.24+); prefer migration patterns where possible.


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-050/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-050/#__codelineno-0-1)contract Destructible {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-050/#__codelineno-0-2)    address public owner; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-050/#__codelineno-0-3)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-050/#__codelineno-0-4)    constructor() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-050/#__codelineno-0-5)        owner = msg.sender;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-050/#__codelineno-0-6)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-050/#__codelineno-0-7)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-050/#__codelineno-0-8)    // Unprotected SELFDESTRUCT allowing anyone to call it    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-050/#__codelineno-0-9)    function destruct() public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-050/#__codelineno-0-10)        selfdestruct(payable(msg.sender));  // No access control    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-050/#__codelineno-0-11)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-050/#__codelineno-0-12)}`

# SCWE-105: Permit Signature Replay via Missing Domain Separator or Nonce

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-105/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/347.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/347.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-105/#description "Permanent link")

Improper EIP-2612 permit implementations that omit chain-specific domain separators, do not increment nonces, or ignore expiration allow signatures to be replayed across chains or multiple times. Attackers can repeatedly approve spending or re-use permits on forked networks.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-105/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Build EIP-712 domain separators including `name`, `version`, `chainId`, and `verifyingContract`.
-   Maintain per-owner nonces and increment on every successful permit.
-   Enforce deadlines and reject expired signatures.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-105/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-105/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-105/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-105/#__codelineno-0-2)contract Token {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-105/#__codelineno-0-3)    mapping(address => uint256) public nonces; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-105/#__codelineno-0-4)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-105/#__codelineno-0-5)    function permit(address owner, address spender, uint256 value, bytes calldata sig) external {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-105/#__codelineno-0-6)        // missing chainId/domain checks, nonce not incremented        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-105/#__codelineno-0-7)        address signer = ecrecover(/* simplified */);        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-105/#__codelineno-0-8)        require(signer == owner, "bad sig");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-105/#__codelineno-0-9)        // allowance set here...    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-105/#__codelineno-0-10)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-105/#__codelineno-0-11)}`

*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-106: Unauthenticated Meta-Transactions

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-106/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/347.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/347.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-106/#description "Permanent link")

Meta-transaction forwarders that relay calls without verifying the signer, nonce, chain, or expiry let relayers execute arbitrary actions on behalf of victims. Missing replay protection allows the same signed request to be executed multiple times.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-106/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Verify EIP-712 typed data signatures against the declared signer.
-   Track and increment per-signer nonces; enforce deadlines and chainId.
-   Restrict trusted forwarders and sanitize `msg.sender`/`msg.data` assumptions in downstream calls.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-106/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-106/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-106/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-106/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-106/#__codelineno-0-3)contract Forwarder {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-106/#__codelineno-0-4)    function relay(address target, bytes calldata data) external {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-106/#__codelineno-0-5)        (bool ok, ) = target.call(data); // no signature or nonce check        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-106/#__codelineno-0-6)        require(ok, "call failed");    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-106/#__codelineno-0-7)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-106/#__codelineno-0-8)}`


### Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-106/#fixed "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-106/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-106/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-106/#__codelineno-1-3)contract Forwarder {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-106/#__codelineno-1-4)    mapping(address => uint256) public nonces; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-106/#__codelineno-1-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-106/#__codelineno-1-6)    function relay(address target, bytes calldata data, uint256 nonce, uint256 deadline, bytes calldata sig) external {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-106/#__codelineno-1-7)        require(block.timestamp <= deadline, "expired");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-106/#__codelineno-1-8)        bytes32 digest = keccak256(abi.encode(target, data, nonce, block.chainid, deadline));        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-106/#__codelineno-1-9)        address signer = ECDSA.recover(digest, sig);        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-106/#__codelineno-1-10)        require(nonce == nonces[signer]++, "bad nonce");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-106/#__codelineno-1-11)        (bool ok, ) = target.call(data);        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-106/#__codelineno-1-12)        require(ok, "call failed");    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-106/#__codelineno-1-13)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-106/#__codelineno-1-14)}`

*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-129: Single EOA Admin Without Rotation

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-129/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-284: Improper Access Control
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/284.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/284.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-129/#description "Permanent link")

Relying on a single externally owned account (EOA) as contract admin creates a single point of failure. Key compromise, loss, or coercion can lead to irreversible upgrades, pauses, or fund drains with no recovery.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-129/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Use multisig (>=2-of-3) with hardware keys and timelocks for admin roles.
-   Document and test key rotation and recovery procedures.
-   Limit admin powers by role (upgrade vs. ops) and enforce separation of duties.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-129/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-129/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-129/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-129/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-129/#__codelineno-0-3)contract Gov {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-129/#__codelineno-0-4)    address public admin; // single EOA — key loss or compromise = no recovery [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-129/#__codelineno-0-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-129/#__codelineno-0-6)    modifier onlyAdmin() { require(msg.sender == admin, "not admin"); _; }    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-129/#__codelineno-0-7)    function upgrade(address impl) external onlyAdmin { /* ... */ } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-129/#__codelineno-0-8)}`


### Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-129/#fixed "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-129/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-129/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-129/#__codelineno-1-3)contract Gov {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-129/#__codelineno-1-4)    IMultisig public admin;     // 2-of-3 multisig with hardware keys    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-129/#__codelineno-1-5)    ITimelock public timelock;  // 48h delay for upgrades [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-129/#__codelineno-1-6)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-129/#__codelineno-1-7)    function proposeUpgrade(address impl) external {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-129/#__codelineno-1-8)        require(admin.isOwner(msg.sender), "not owner");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-129/#__codelineno-1-9)        timelock.schedule(impl);    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-129/#__codelineno-1-10)    }    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-129/#__codelineno-1-11)    function executeUpgrade() external {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-129/#__codelineno-1-12)        timelock.execute(); // only after delay; supports key rotation    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-129/#__codelineno-1-13)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-129/#__codelineno-1-14)}`

title: SCWE-139: Single-Step Ownership Transfer Without Confirmation
heading: Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-139/#fixed "Permanent link")

*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-139: Single-Step Ownership Transfer Without Confirmation

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-139/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-670: Always-Incorrect Control Flow Implementation
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/670.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/670.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-139/#description "Permanent link")

A single-step `transferOwnership(newOwner)` immediately assigns ownership to the new address. If the wrong address is used (typo, burn address `address(0)`, or a contract that cannot receive ownership), the contract can be permanently locked—no one can perform owner-only actions or correct the mistake. A two-step process (propose → accept) allows the intended recipient to confirm and prevents accidental loss of control.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-139/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Implement a two-step ownership transfer: `transferOwnershipPending(newOwner)` sets a pending owner, and `acceptOwnership()` (callable only by the pending owner) completes the transfer.
-   Validate that `newOwner != address(0)` and consider rejecting contract addresses if the owner must be an EOA for operational reasons.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-139/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-139/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-139/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-139/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-139/#__codelineno-0-3)contract Ownable {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-139/#__codelineno-0-4)    address public owner; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-139/#__codelineno-0-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-139/#__codelineno-0-6)    constructor() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-139/#__codelineno-0-7)        owner = msg.sender;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-139/#__codelineno-0-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-139/#__codelineno-0-9)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-139/#__codelineno-0-10)    function transferOwnership(address newOwner) external {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-139/#__codelineno-0-11)        require(msg.sender == owner, "Not owner");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-139/#__codelineno-0-12)        owner = newOwner;  // Single step: typo or address(0) permanently locks contract    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-139/#__codelineno-0-13)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-139/#__codelineno-0-14)}`

title: SCWE-147: Permit or Meta-Transaction Signatures Without Expiration
heading: Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-147/#fixed "Permanent link")
text:
*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-147: Permit or Meta-Transaction Signatures Without Expiration

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-147/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/347.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/347.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-147/#description "Permanent link")

Permit (EIP-2612) and meta-transaction signatures that omit a `deadline` or `expiry` parameter can be replayed indefinitely once obtained. An attacker who captures a valid signature (e.g., via phishing or a compromised frontend) can submit it at any future time. SCWE-105 covers domain separator and nonce; this weakness specifically addresses the absence of expiration.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-147/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Include a `deadline` (or `expiry`) in the signed message and enforce `require(block.timestamp <= deadline, "Expired")` when processing the signature.
-   Use EIP-712 structured data with a deadline field.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-147/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-147/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-147/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-147/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-147/#__codelineno-0-3)contract MetaTx {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-147/#__codelineno-0-4)    function execute(address signer, bytes32 hash, uint8 v, bytes32 r, bytes32 s) external {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-147/#__codelineno-0-5)        require(ecrecover(hash, v, r, s) == signer, "Bad sig");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-147/#__codelineno-0-6)        // No deadline: signature valid forever        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-147/#__codelineno-0-7)        _execute(signer);    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-147/#__codelineno-0-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-147/#__codelineno-0-9)}`


### Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-147/#fixed "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-147/#__codelineno-1-1)function execute(address signer, uint256 deadline, bytes32 hash, uint8 v, bytes32 r, bytes32 s) external {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-147/#__codelineno-1-2)    require(block.timestamp <= deadline, "Expired");    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-147/#__codelineno-1-3)    require(ecrecover(hash, v, r, s) == signer, "Bad sig");    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-147/#__codelineno-1-4)    _execute(signer); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-147/#__codelineno-1-5)}`

**Note:** The `hash` must be computed from EIP-712 structured data that includes the `deadline` field so the signature cannot be replayed after expiry.

*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-155: Single Point of Failure in Administrative Key Management

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-284: Improper Access Control
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/284.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/284.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#description "Permanent link")

Contracts that rely on a single administrative key (EOA or contract) without multisig, timelock, or key rotation create a single point of failure. Compromise of that key (phishing, malware, physical theft) gives full control; loss of the key (e.g., no backup) can permanently lock critical functions. SCWE-129 covers single EOA admin; this weakness focuses on the *risk* of single-key design and the absence of mitigations.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Use multisig wallets (e.g., Gnosis Safe) for administrative actions.
-   Implement timelocks for sensitive operations (SCWE-020).
-   Plan for key rotation or recovery mechanisms.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-0-3)contract Treasury {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-0-4)    address public owner; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-0-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-0-6)    function withdraw(uint256 amount) external {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-0-7)        require(msg.sender == owner, "Not owner");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-0-8)        (bool ok, ) = owner.call{value: amount}("");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-0-9)        require(ok, "Transfer failed");    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-0-10)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-0-11)}`

**Risk:** Single `owner` key; no multisig, no timelock. Compromise or loss permanently affects the treasury.

title: SCWE-155: Single Point of Failure in Administrative Key Management
heading: Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#fixed "Permanent link")
text:
### Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#fixed "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-1-1)contract Treasury {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-1-2)    address public owner;  // In production: use multisig (e.g., Gnosis Safe)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-1-3)    uint256 public constant TIMELOCK = 2 days;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-1-4)    uint256 public pendingAmount;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-1-5)    uint256 public unlockTime; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-1-6)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-1-7)    function proposeWithdraw(uint256 amount) external {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-1-8)        require(msg.sender == owner, "Not owner");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-1-9)        pendingAmount = amount;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-1-10)        unlockTime = block.timestamp + TIMELOCK;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-1-11)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-1-12)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-1-13)    function executeWithdraw() external {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-1-14)        require(msg.sender == owner, "Not owner");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-1-15)        require(block.timestamp >= unlockTime, "Timelock");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-1-16)        uint256 amount = pendingAmount;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-1-17)        pendingAmount = 0;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-1-18)        (bool ok, ) = owner.call{value: amount}("");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-1-19)        require(ok, "Transfer failed");    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-1-20)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-AUTH/SCWE-155/#__codelineno-1-21)}`

**Fix:** Timelock adds a delay so large withdrawals can be contested. Use a multisig for `owner` in production.

# SCWE-024: Weak Randomness Sources

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-024/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-336: Predictable Random Number Generator
    [CWE-336 Link](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/336.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-024/#description "Permanent link")

Weak randomness sources refer to the use of predictable or insecure sources of randomness, such as block timestamps or block hashes. This can lead to: - Exploitation of the contract's logic. - Loss of funds or data. - Reduced trust in the contract's security.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-024/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Use secure randomness:** Leverage secure randomness sources like Chainlink VRF.
-   **Avoid block variables:** Do not rely on block timestamps or hashes for randomness.
-   **Test thoroughly:** Conduct extensive testing to ensure randomness is secure.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-024/#examples "Permanent link")

-   **Weak Randomness**

    `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-024/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-024/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-024/#__codelineno-0-3)contract WeakRandomness {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-024/#__codelineno-0-4)    function generateRandomNumber() public view returns (uint) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-024/#__codelineno-0-5)        return uint(keccak256(abi.encodePacked(block.timestamp, block.difficulty))); // Insecure: post-merge use block.prevrandao; both are insecure for value-at-stake randomness    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-024/#__codelineno-0-6)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-024/#__codelineno-0-7)}`

-   **Secure Randomness** \`\`\`solidity pragma solidity ^0.8.0;


import "@chainlink/contracts/src/v0.8/VRFConsumerBase.sol"; // Note: Chainlink VRF V1 is deprecated; use VRF V2 (VRFConsumerBaseV2) in production

contract SecureRandomness is VRFConsumerBase { bytes32 internal keyHash; uint256 internal fee; uint256 public randomResult;

    ` constructor(address vrfCoordinator, address linkToken, bytes32 _keyHash, uint256 _fee)         VRFConsumerBase(vrfCoordinator, linkToken) {         keyHash = _keyHash;         fee = _fee;     }      function getRandomNumber() public returns (bytes32 requestId) {         require(LINK.balanceOf(address(this)) >= fee, "Not enough LINK");         return requestRandomness(keyHash, fee);     }      function fulfillRandomness(bytes32 requestId, uint256 randomness) internal override {         randomResult = randomness;     } } ``` `

* * *

text:
*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-031: Insecure use of Block Variables

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   **CWE-682: Incorrect Calculation**
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/682.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/682.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#description "Permanent link")

In blockchain networks like Ethereum, block variables `(block.timestamp, block.number, block.difficulty` / `block.prevrandao` post-merge, etc.) provide information about the current state of the blockchain. However, these values are not fully deterministic and can be manipulated by validators (or miners on PoW chains), leading to vulnerabilities in smart contracts.

Block timestamps are not guaranteed to be accurate or consistent, and validators (or miners on PoW chains) can influence them within a certain range. This can cause issues when contracts depend on precise timing for critical functionality, such as token distribution, access control, or other time-sensitive events.

Potential issues that arise from insecure timestamp usage include:

-   Timestamp Manipulation: Validators (or miners on PoW) can slightly alter `block.timestamp` to influence time-sensitive logic (e.g., auctions, token distributions, staking rewards).
-   Predictable Randomness: Using `block.number` or `block.difficulty` as a source of randomness allows attackers to predict and manipulate outcomes.
-   Exploitable Access Control: Contracts that rely on block timestamps for permissions or actions may be bypassed if timestamps are adjusted.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Avoid timestamp-based conditions**: Where possible, use block numbers instead of timestamps. Block numbers are more reliable and less subject to manipulation.
-   **Use Oracles**: For time-sensitive contracts, consider using trusted oracles to provide external time data.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#examples "Permanent link")

title: SCWE-031: Insecure use of Block Variables
heading: Fixed Block Timestamp Usage[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#fixed-block-timestamp-usage "Permanent link")
text:
### Insecure Block Timestamp Usage- Timestamp-Based Deadlines[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#insecure-block-timestamp-usage-timestamp-based-deadlines "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.4.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-0-3)contract TimestampExample {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-0-4)    uint public deadline; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-0-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-0-6)    function setDeadline(uint _deadline) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-0-7)        deadline = _deadline;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-0-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-0-9)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-0-10)    function checkDeadline() public view returns (string) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-0-11)        if (block.timestamp > deadline) {            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-0-12)            return "Deadline passed";        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-0-13)        } else {            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-0-14)            return "Deadline not passed";        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-0-15)        }    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-0-16)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-0-17)}`

In the above example, `block.timestamp` is used to compare with the deadline. This creates a potential vulnerability as validators (or miners on PoW) can manipulate the block timestamp within a predefined window (~15 seconds).

title: SCWE-031: Insecure use of Block Variables
heading: Insecure Lottery Using block.timestamp[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#insecure-lottery-using-blocktimestamp "Permanent link")
text:
### Fixed Block Timestamp Usage[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#fixed-block-timestamp-usage "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.4.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-1-3)contract SafeTimestampExample {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-1-4)    uint public deadline;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-1-5)    uint public blockNumber; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-1-6)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-1-7)    function setDeadline(uint _deadline) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-1-8)        deadline = _deadline;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-1-9)        blockNumber = block.number;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-1-10)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-1-11)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-1-12)    function checkDeadline() public view returns (string) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-1-13)        if (block.number > blockNumber + 1000) { // Assuming a reasonable number of blocks for a deadline            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-1-14)            return "Deadline passed";        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-1-15)        } else {            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-1-16)            return "Deadline not passed";        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-1-17)        }    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-1-18)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-1-19)}`

In this fixed version, the contract uses `block.number` instead of `block.timestamp`. This makes the contract less susceptible to timestamp manipulation, as block numbers are more reliable and consistent.

title: SCWE-031: Insecure use of Block Variables
heading: Secure Alternative (Commit-Reveal)[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#secure-alternative-commit-reveal "Permanent link")
text:
### Insecure Lottery Using block.timestamp[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#insecure-lottery-using-blocktimestamp "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-2-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-2-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-2-3)contract InsecureLottery {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-2-4)    address[] public players; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-2-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-2-6)    function enter() public payable {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-2-7)        require(msg.value > 0.01 ether, "Minimum ETH required"); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-2-8)        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-2-9)        players.push(msg.sender);    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-2-10)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-2-11)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-2-12)    function pickWinner() public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-2-13)        uint index = uint(block.timestamp) % players.length; // Insecure: Predictable outcome        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-2-14)        (bool ok, ) = payable(players[index]).call{value: address(this).balance}("");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-2-15)        require(ok, "Transfer failed");    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-2-16)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-2-17)}`

Issue: - Predictability: Since `block.timestamp` is manipulable within a small range, validators (or miners on PoW chains) can influence the winner selection. - Attack Vector: A validator (or miner on PoW) could reorder transactions to ensure a specific outcome

title: SCWE-031: Insecure use of Block Variables
heading: Secure Alternative (Commit-Reveal)[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#secure-alternative-commit-reveal "Permanent link")
text:
### Secure Alternative (Commit-Reveal)[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#secure-alternative-commit-reveal "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-3-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-3-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-3-3)contract SecureLottery {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-3-4)    mapping(address => bytes32) public commits;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-3-5)    mapping(address => bytes32) public revealed;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-3-6)    address[] public players; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-3-7)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-3-8)    function commit(bytes32 hash) external payable {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-3-9)        require(msg.value > 0.01 ether, "Minimum ETH required");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-3-10)        require(commits[msg.sender] == bytes32(0), "Already committed");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-3-11)        commits[msg.sender] = hash;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-3-12)        players.push(msg.sender);    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-3-13)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-3-14)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-3-15)    function reveal(bytes32 secret) external {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-3-16)        require(keccak256(abi.encodePacked(secret)) == commits[msg.sender], "Invalid reveal");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-3-17)        revealed[msg.sender] = secret;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-3-18)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-3-19)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-3-20)    function pickWinner() external {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-3-21)        bytes32 combined = bytes32(0);        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-3-22)        for (uint i = 0; i < players.length; i++) {            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-3-23)            require(revealed[players[i]] != bytes32(0), "All must reveal");            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-3-24)            combined = keccak256(abi.encodePacked(combined, revealed[players[i]]));        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-3-25)        }        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-3-26)        uint index = uint(combined) % players.length;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-3-27)        (bool ok, ) = payable(players[index]).call{value: address(this).balance}("");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-3-28)        require(ok, "Transfer failed");    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-3-29)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-031/#__codelineno-3-30)}`

Fixes: - Uses commit-reveal: each player commits a hash, then reveals; combined secrets determine the winner. - `block.prevrandao` and `block.timestamp` are **not safe** for value-at-stake randomness — use VRF (e.g., Chainlink) or commit-reveal.

title: SCWE-065: Block Values as a Proxy for Time
heading: Fixed Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#fixed-contract-example "Permanent link")
text:
*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-065: Block Values as a Proxy for Time

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-20: Improper Input Validation
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#description "Permanent link")

Using block values (such as `block.timestamp`, `block.number`, or `block.difficulty` / `block.prevrandao` post-merge) as a proxy for time in Ethereum smart contracts can be problematic. Block values are determined by validators (or miners on PoW chains) and can be manipulated within certain limits, making them unreliable for time-sensitive logic. Relying on these values for critical decisions like deadlines or expiration dates can result in unexpected behaviors, such as manipulations by validators (or miners on PoW chains) or unintended contract states.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#remediation "Permanent link")

To mitigate this vulnerability, account for the manipulation bounds of block values. `block.timestamp` can vary by ~15 seconds per block; design deadlines and time checks with this tolerance in mind. Time oracles are uncommon; the standard approach is to use `block.timestamp` with appropriate buffers. Where precision is critical, consider commit-reveal or multi-block confirmation.


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#__codelineno-0-1)contract TimeSensitive {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#__codelineno-0-2)    uint public deadline; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#__codelineno-0-3)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#__codelineno-0-4)    constructor(uint _deadline) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#__codelineno-0-5)        deadline = _deadline;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#__codelineno-0-6)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#__codelineno-0-7)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#__codelineno-0-8)    function hasExpired() public view returns (bool) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#__codelineno-0-9)        return block.timestamp > deadline;  // Relies on block.timestamp    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#__codelineno-0-10)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#__codelineno-0-11)}`

title: SCWE-065: Block Values as a Proxy for Time
heading: Fixed Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#fixed-contract-example "Permanent link")
text:
### Fixed Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#fixed-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#__codelineno-1-3)contract TimeSensitive {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#__codelineno-1-4)    uint public constant DEADLINE_BUFFER = 15; // seconds — accounts for block.timestamp manipulation    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#__codelineno-1-5)    uint public deadline; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#__codelineno-1-6)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#__codelineno-1-7)    constructor(uint _deadline) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#__codelineno-1-8)        // Set deadline with buffer so expiry is robust to ~15s timestamp variance        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#__codelineno-1-9)        deadline = _deadline + DEADLINE_BUFFER;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#__codelineno-1-10)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#__codelineno-1-11)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#__codelineno-1-12)    function hasExpired() public view returns (bool) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#__codelineno-1-13)        return block.timestamp > deadline;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#__codelineno-1-14)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-065/#__codelineno-1-15)}`

**Mitigation:** Add a buffer when setting deadlines to account for the ~15 second manipulation window of `block.timestamp`. Avoid relying on sub-minute precision.

title: SCWE-073: Message Call with Hardcoded Gas Amount
heading: Fixed Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-073/#fixed-contract-example "Permanent link")
text:
*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-073: Message Call with Hardcoded Gas Amount

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-073/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/400.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/400.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-073/#description "Permanent link")

In Solidity, calling external contracts with a hardcoded gas value can lead to various issues, such as running out of gas or allowing a malicious contract to manipulate gas consumption. Hardcoding the gas amount is inflexible and may lead to resource exhaustion or cause the transaction to fail when the gas limit is insufficient for the operation.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-073/#remediation "Permanent link")

Instead of hardcoding gas values, it is better to allow the gas to be automatically determined or adjust the gas dynamically depending on the needs of the transaction. This ensures that the transaction can complete successfully while avoiding unnecessary resource consumption.


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-073/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-073/#__codelineno-0-1)contract Example {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-073/#__codelineno-0-2)    address public target; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-073/#__codelineno-0-3)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-073/#__codelineno-0-4)    function callTarget() public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-073/#__codelineno-0-5)        // Hardcoding the gas value for the message call        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-073/#__codelineno-0-6)        target.call{gas: 100000}("");  // Vulnerable to resource consumption issues    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-073/#__codelineno-0-7)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-073/#__codelineno-0-8)}`


### Fixed Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-073/#fixed-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-073/#__codelineno-1-1)contract Example {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-073/#__codelineno-1-2)    address public target; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-073/#__codelineno-1-3)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-073/#__codelineno-1-4)    function callTarget() public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-073/#__codelineno-1-5)        // Let Solidity handle gas consumption dynamically        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-073/#__codelineno-1-6)        target.call("");  // Gas amount handled by the EVM dynamically    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-073/#__codelineno-1-7)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-073/#__codelineno-1-8)}`

title: SCWE-127: EIP-1559 Basefee Assumptions
