*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-127: EIP-1559 Basefee Assumptions

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-127/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-841: Improper Enforcement of Behavioral Workflow
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/841.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/841.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-127/#description "Permanent link")

Hardcoding gas price/basefee assumptions (e.g., fixed `gasprice` limits or expecting refunds) can break on EIP-1559 chains. Contracts that require exact `block.basefee` ranges or reimburse fixed gas can become stuck or exploitable via gas griefing.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-127/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Avoid relying on specific basefee values; parameterize and allow updates via governance with delays.
-   Use robust gas estimation and caps on external calls; avoid refund-dependent logic.
-   Simulate on mainnet forks with varying basefee to validate liveness.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-127/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-127/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-127/#__codelineno-0-1)require(tx.gasprice <= 30 gwei, "gas too high"); // fails as basefee rises`


### Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-127/#fixed "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-127/#__codelineno-1-1)uint256 maxGasPrice = governanceMaxGasPrice; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-127/#__codelineno-1-2)require(tx.gasprice <= maxGasPrice, "gas too high"); // upgradable with delays`

title: SCWE-153: Reliance on block.prevrandao for High-Value Randomness
heading: Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-153/#fixed "Permanent link")
text:
*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-153: Reliance on block.prevrandao for High-Value Randomness

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-153/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/330.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/330.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-153/#description "Permanent link")

Post-merge (Ethereum PoS), `block.difficulty` was replaced by `block.prevrandao`. Both are manipulable by validators: they can influence the value within protocol rules. Using `block.prevrandao` (or `block.difficulty`) for high-value randomness—lotteries, airdrops, winner selection—allows validators or sophisticated actors to predict or bias outcomes. SCWE-024 and SCWE-084 cover blockhash/timestamp; this weakness specifically addresses `block.prevrandao`.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-153/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Do not use `block.prevrandao` or `block.difficulty` for value-at-stake randomness.
-   Use Chainlink VRF, commit-reveal schemes, or other verifiable randomness sources.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-153/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-153/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-153/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-153/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-153/#__codelineno-0-3)contract Lottery {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-153/#__codelineno-0-4)    address[] public participants; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-153/#__codelineno-0-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-153/#__codelineno-0-6)    function pickWinner() external view returns (uint256) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-153/#__codelineno-0-7)        return uint256(keccak256(abi.encodePacked(block.prevrandao, block.timestamp))) % participants.length;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-153/#__codelineno-0-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-153/#__codelineno-0-9)}`

**Why vulnerable:** `block.prevrandao` is manipulable by validators; they can influence the value to bias the outcome.


### Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BLOCK/SCWE-153/#fixed "Permanent link")

Use Chainlink VRF V2 or a commit-reveal scheme where participants commit hashes before the random value is known. See SCWE-024 for a Chainlink VRF example.

*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-032: Dependency on Block Gas Limit

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-032/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
    [CWE-400 Link](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/400.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-032/#description "Permanent link")

Dependency on block gas limit refers to the reliance on the Ethereum block gas limit for contract operations, which can lead to: - Failed transactions if gas limits are exceeded. - Exploitation of vulnerabilities in gas-intensive operations. - Loss of funds or data.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-032/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Optimize gas usage:** Minimize gas consumption in contract operations.
-   **Avoid unbounded loops:** Ensure loops have a fixed upper limit.
-   **Test thoroughly:** Conduct extensive testing to ensure operations stay within gas limits.

title: SCWE-032: Dependency on Block Gas Limit
heading: Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-032/#examples "Permanent link")
text:
## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-032/#examples "Permanent link")

-   **Gas-Intensive Operation- Storing Large Dynamic Data**

    `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-032/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-032/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-032/#__codelineno-0-3)contract GasIntensive {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-032/#__codelineno-0-4)    uint[] public largeArray; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-032/#__codelineno-0-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-032/#__codelineno-0-6)    function appendData(uint[] memory data) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-032/#__codelineno-0-7)        for (uint i = 0; i < data.length; i++) {            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-032/#__codelineno-0-8)            largeArray.push(data[i]); // Storing a large dataset in a single transaction        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-032/#__codelineno-0-9)        }    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-032/#__codelineno-0-10)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-032/#__codelineno-0-11)}`

-   This contract appends large arrays in a single transaction, which fails when the block gas limit is exceeded.
-   Attackers could exploit this by forcing high gas consumption and causing DoS attacks (e.g., filling storage inefficiently).

-   **Optimized Gas Usage- Chunk Processing & Gas Efficiency**

    `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-032/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-032/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-032/#__codelineno-1-3)contract GasOptimized {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-032/#__codelineno-1-4)    uint[] public largeArray; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-032/#__codelineno-1-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-032/#__codelineno-1-6)    function appendData(uint[] memory data, uint start, uint end) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-032/#__codelineno-1-7)        require(end <= data.length, "Invalid range");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-032/#__codelineno-1-8)        for (uint i = start; i < end; i++) {            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-032/#__codelineno-1-9)            largeArray.push(data[i]); // Process in controlled batches        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-032/#__codelineno-1-10)        }    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-032/#__codelineno-1-11)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-032/#__codelineno-1-12)}`


Why is this better? - The start and end parameters allow batch processing instead of handling everything in a single call. - Prevents hitting the block gas limit by splitting work across multiple transactions.

# SCWE-033: Chain Split Risks

## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-033/#description "Permanent link")

Chain split risks refer to vulnerabilities that arise when a blockchain splits into multiple chains, such as during a hard fork. This can lead to: - Confusion or inconsistencies in contract logic. - Loss of funds or data. - Exploitation of vulnerabilities in cross-chain operations.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-033/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Handle chain splits:** Implement logic to handle potential chain splits.
-   **Use chain identifiers:** Include chain identifiers in cross-chain communications.
-   **Test thoroughly:** Conduct extensive testing to ensure contract logic is robust.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-033/#examples "Permanent link")

-   **Vulnerable to Chain Splits**

    `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-033/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-033/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-033/#__codelineno-0-3)contract ChainSplitVulnerable {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-033/#__codelineno-0-4)    function processTransaction(bytes memory data) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-033/#__codelineno-0-5)        // Process transaction without chain split handling    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-033/#__codelineno-0-6)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-033/#__codelineno-0-7)}`

-   **Protected Against Chain Splits**

    `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-033/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-033/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-033/#__codelineno-1-3)contract ChainSplitProtected {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-033/#__codelineno-1-4)    uint public chainId; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-033/#__codelineno-1-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-033/#__codelineno-1-6)    constructor(uint _chainId) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-033/#__codelineno-1-7)        chainId = _chainId;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-033/#__codelineno-1-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-033/#__codelineno-1-9)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-033/#__codelineno-1-10)    function processTransaction(bytes memory data, uint transactionChainId) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-033/#__codelineno-1-11)        require(transactionChainId == chainId, "Invalid chain ID");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-033/#__codelineno-1-12)        // Process transaction    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-033/#__codelineno-1-13)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-033/#__codelineno-1-14)}`

# SCWE-034: Insecure Cross-Chain Messaging

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-20: Improper Input Validation
    [CWE-20 Link](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#description "Permanent link")

Insecure cross-chain messaging refers to vulnerabilities that arise when communicating between different blockchains. This can lead to: - Unauthorized actions by malicious actors. - Loss of funds or data. - Exploitation of vulnerabilities in cross-chain logic.

-   Economic inconsistencies due to unvalidated msg.value in message handlers.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Validate messages:** Ensure all cross-chain messages are properly validated.
-   **Use secure protocols:** Leverage secure cross-chain communication protocols.
-   **Test thoroughly:** Conduct extensive testing to ensure cross-chain logic is secure.

-   **Validate msg.value:** Decode expected value from the message payload or protocol parameters and require that `msg.value` matches (or meets) this expectation; revert on mismatch.

## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#examples "Permanent link")

-   **Insecure Cross-Chain Messaging**

    `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-0-3)contract InsecureCrossChain {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-0-4)    event MessageProcessed(bytes message); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-0-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-0-6)    function processMessage(bytes memory message) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-0-7)        // ❌ No validation of the sender (anyone can call this function!)        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-0-8)        // ❌ No signature verification (attackers can inject fake messages!)        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-0-9)        // 🚨 No relayer authorization        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-0-10)        // 🚨 No replay protection        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-0-11)        emit MessageProcessed(message);    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-0-12)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-0-13)}`

    🔴 Issue: The function accepts messages without validation, allowing unauthorized transactions.

Unauthorized Relayers (Anyone Can Call!) - Issue: The function allows any msg.sender to call processMessage(), meaning an attacker can send arbitrary messages. - Impact: Attackers can forge transactions, trigger unintended actions, or drain funds if the function is connected to cross-chain asset transfers.

No Signature Verification (Fake Messages) - Issue: The contract doesn’t verify the authenticity of the message. - Impact: Attackers can inject fake messages and trick the contract into executing unauthorized actions.

Replay Attacks - Issue: The contract doesn’t track processed messages. - Impact: The same message can be replayed multiple times, leading to repeated execution of sensitive operations.

-   **Secure Cross-Chain Messaging**

    `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-1-3)contract SecureCrossChain {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-1-4)    mapping(address => bool) public trustedRelayers;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-1-5)    mapping(bytes32 => bool) public processedMessages; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-1-6)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-1-7)    event MessageProcessed(bytes32 indexed messageHash, address indexed sender);    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-1-8)    event RelayerUpdated(address relayer, bool status); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-1-9)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-1-10)    address public owner; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-1-11)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-1-12)    modifier onlyOwner() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-1-13)        require(msg.sender == owner, "Not the owner");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-1-14)        _;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-1-15)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-1-16)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-1-17)    constructor(address[] memory initialRelayers) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-1-18)        owner = msg.s

       [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-1-36)        address signer = ecrecover(messageHash, v, r, s);        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-1-37)        require(signer != address(0), "Invalid signature"); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-1-38)        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-1-39)        require(!processedMessages[messageHash], "Message already processed");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-1-40)        processedMessages[messageHash] = true; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-1-41)        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-1-42)        emit MessageProcessed(messageHash, signer); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-1-43)        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-1-44)        // ✅ Securely process the message    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-1-45)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-034/#__codelineno-1-46)}`


Fix: Implements signature verification, relayer validation, and replay protection. Why is this better? ✅ Verifies Signatures Properly: Uses ecrecover() with Ethereum Signed Message hashing. ✅ Admin Can Manage Relayers: Allows dynamic relayer updates via setRelayer(). ✅ Prevents Replay Attacks: Tracks processed messages in processedMessages mapping. ✅ Ensures Message Authenticity: Only validly signed messages are accepted.

*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-087: Missing Payload Size Validation in Cross-Chain Messaging (Denial of Service/Stuck Funds)

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-087/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-1284: Improper Validation of Specified Quantity in Input
    [CWE-1284 Link](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1284.html)
-   CWE-20: Improper Input Validation
    [CWE-20 Link](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-087/#description "Permanent link")

This weakness arises when smart contracts performing cross-chain messaging fail to validate the size of payloads before emitting or sending them. In protocols using relayer-based messaging (e.g., LayerZero, Wormhole), data is typically encoded and emitted as a payload on the source chain, then relayed and decoded on the destination chain. If the encoded payload exceeds the maximum allowed size (often 10,000 bytes or similar, depending on the bridge/messaging protocol), the message transmission or decoding can revert—often because the large payload causes out-of-gas consumption during processing or fails explicit size checks. In lock-mint architectures, this can lead to permanent loss of user funds due to inability to unlock or mint assets on the destination chain.


## Impact[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-087/#impact "Permanent link")

-   **Denial of Service:** Oversized payloads will revert during cross-chain transmission, preventing legitimate state updates or token minting/unlocking on the destination chain.
-   **Stuck or Lost Funds:** In bridges using lock-and-mint or burn-and-mint designs, users’ assets may be locked on the source chain with no way to release or claim them on the destination due to repeated transaction failure.
-   **Operational Risk:** Malicious or unintentional submission of oversized payloads can be used to disrupt bridge operations, preventing protocol liveness or causing critical business logic to be inaccessible.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-087/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Enforce maximum payload size validation on both source and destination chains.
-   Perform defensive coding around payload encoding and decoding to catch out-of-gas or out-of-bound errors.
-   Consider fallback or reversion handling strategies to safely refund or unlock funds when such failures occur.

*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-094: Insufficient Gas Limit Validation in LayerZero Message Sending

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-094/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-20: Improper Input Validation
    [CWE-20 Link](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-094/#description "Permanent link")

This weakness arises when a smart contract using LayerZero for cross-chain communication fails to validate the minimum gas limit in the adapter parameters. Attackers (or misconfigured clients) can specify an adapter params gas value that is too low for the destination chain execution. As a result, message processing reverts before reaching business logic or error-handling, and the message is recorded as a failed payload on the destination chain. Accumulating failed payloads can disrupt protocol liveness by blocking the cross-chain communication pathway until manual intervention is performed.


## Impact[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-094/#impact "Permanent link")

-   **Denial of Service:** Destination chain message execution reverts due to insufficient gas, preventing critical state changes or callbacks.
-   **Message Backlog/Failed Payloads:** Messages accumulate in failed payload storage/queues, increasing operational burden.
-   **Operational Risk:** Requires manual retries, clearing, or rescue flows to restore liveness; prolonged outages can impact user operations (e.g., bridging, synchronization, DeFi actions).


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-094/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Validate minimum gas limit:** Decode LayerZero adapter parameters and enforce a protocol-defined minimum gas limit per message type.
-   **Use safe defaults:** Provide default adapter params with adequate gas and reject user-supplied values below the threshold.
-   **Granular minima:** If different message types have varying complexity, define per-endpoint or per-function minimum gas values.
-   **Robust failure handling:** Implement operational procedures and tooling to safely retry or clear failed payloads without compromising security.

title: SCWE-096: Missing Token Burn During Cross-Chain NFT Withdrawal

*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-096: Missing Token Burn During Cross-Chain NFT Withdrawal

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-345: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity
    [CWE-345 Link](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/345.html)
-   CWE-664: Improper Control of a Resource Through Its Lifetime
    [CWE-664 Link](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/664.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#description "Permanent link")

This weakness occurs when a cross-chain bridge allows withdrawals from Chain B to Chain A without properly burning or locking the corresponding token on the source chain (Chain B) before initiating the cross-chain transaction.

As a result, the same token can exist simultaneously on both chains, enabling a double-spend scenario where malicious actors can sell, transfer, or use the same token on multiple chains.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#remediation "Permanent link")

1.  Burn the NFT

    -   Call the `burn(tokenId)` function on the L2 NFT contract before sending the cross-chain withdrawal request.
    -   This ensures that the NFT no longer exists on L2 and cannot be reused, transferred, or sold.
2.  Alternatively, Lock the NFT (if burning isn’t possible)

    -   If NFTs are not meant to be permanently destroyed, implement a lock mechanism to freeze the token on L2 until the cross-chain withdrawal is completed successfully.
3.  Update Cross-Chain Workflow

    -   Enforce the burn/lock operation as part of the withdrawal process.
    -   Revert the entire transaction if the burn/lock fails.

-   **Vulnerable Code (Not Burning Token Before Sending Cross Chain Message)**

    `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-0-1)// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-0-2)pragma solidity ^0.8.20; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-0-3)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-0-4)contract SourceChainNFTGateway {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-0-5)    mapping(address => mapping(uint256 => address)) public ownerOf; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-0-6)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-0-7)    function withdrawNFT(address l2Token, uint256 tokenId) external {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-0-8)        require(ownerOf[l2Token][tokenId] == msg.sender, "Not the owner"); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-0-9)        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-0-10)        // ❌ Send cross-chain message to Destination Chain (omitted for simplicity)        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-0-11)        // NFT is still available on Source Chain → double-spend possible    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-0-12)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-0-13)}`

-   **Safe Code (Burning Token Before Sending Cross Chain Message)**

    `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-1-1)// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-1-2)pragma solidity ^0.8.20; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-1-3)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-1-4)interface IL2NFT {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-1-5)    function burn(uint256 tokenId) external; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-1-6)} [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-1-7)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-1-8)contract SourceChainNFTGateway {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-1-9)    mapping(address => mapping(uint256 => address)) public ownerOf; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-1-10)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-1-11)    function withdrawNFT(address l2Token, uint256 tokenId) external {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-1-12)        require(ownerOf[l2Token][tokenId] == msg.sender, "Not the owner"); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-1-13)        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-1-14)        // ✅ Burn the NFT on Source Chain to prevent double-spend        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-1-15)        IL2NFT(l2Token).burn(tokenId); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-1-16)        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-1-17)        // Send cross-chain message to Destination Chain (omitted for simplicity)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-1-18)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-096/#__codelineno-1-19)}`

title: SCWE-132: Mismatched Token Decimals in Bridge Mint/Burn
heading: Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-132/#fixed "Permanent link")
text:
*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-132: Mismatched Token Decimals in Bridge Mint/Burn

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-132/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-682: Incorrect Calculation
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/682.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/682.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-132/#description "Permanent link")

Bridging tokens with differing decimals without normalization can over- or under-mint wrapped assets. Attackers can exploit decimal confusion to siphon value or lock funds when withdrawing back to the origin chain.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-132/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Normalize amounts to a canonical precision before mint/burn.
-   Store per-token decimal config and validate consistency during bridge operations.
-   Add tests for round-trip conversions across chains with varying decimals.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-132/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-132/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-132/#__codelineno-0-1)// assumes 18 decimals on both sides; origin token has 6 [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-132/#__codelineno-0-2)_mint(user, amount);`


### Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-132/#fixed "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-132/#__codelineno-1-1)uint8 srcDec = 6; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-132/#__codelineno-1-2)uint8 dstDec = 18; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-132/#__codelineno-1-3)uint256 normalized = amount * 10**(dstDec - srcDec); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-132/#__codelineno-1-4)_mint(user, normalized);`

*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-133: Missing Replay Nonce per Bridge Lane

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-133/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-294: Authentication Bypass by Capture-replay
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/294.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/294.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-133/#description "Permanent link")

Bridge receivers that do not track nonces per source chain/sender allow the same message to be replayed, causing duplicate mints or withdrawals. Forked chains can also replay historical messages if lanes are not isolated.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-133/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Maintain monotonically increasing nonces per (sourceChain, sourceSender).
-   Reject messages with reused or out-of-order nonces.
-   Bind nonces into signed payloads or proofs to prevent tampering.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-133/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-133/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-133/#__codelineno-0-1)function receive(bytes calldata payload) external {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-133/#__codelineno-0-2)    _execute(payload); // no nonce tracking [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-133/#__codelineno-0-3)}`


### Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-133/#fixed "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-133/#__codelineno-1-1)mapping(uint256 => mapping(address => uint256)) public nonce; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-133/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-133/#__codelineno-1-3)function receive(uint256 srcChain, address src, uint256 n, bytes calldata payload) external {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-133/#__codelineno-1-4)    require(n == nonce[srcChain][src]++, "replay");    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-133/#__codelineno-1-5)    _execute(payload); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-BRIDGE/SCWE-133/#__codelineno-1-6)}`

# SCWE-007: Presence of Unused Variables

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-007/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-563: Assignment to Variable with No Effect [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/563.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/563.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-007/#description "Permanent link")

The presence of unused variables in smart contracts refers to variables that are declared but never utilized in the contract logic. These variables consume storage or memory space unnecessarily, potentially wasting gas when deployed or executed. This situation often arises due to incomplete code, forgotten variables, or code that was intended for future use but never implemented. The presence of such variables increases the attack surface by making it harder to understand the contract and opens up potential vulnerabilities.

Some common risks include: - Wasted gas due to storage and memory consumption. - Increased complexity and difficulty in understanding contract behavior. - Potential confusion for auditors or future developers working on the contract.

Unused variables can also hide logic errors or indicate that parts of the contract are not functioning as intended.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-007/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Remove Unused Variables:** Ensure that any variables that are not required for the contract’s functionality are removed.
-   **Code Review and Refactoring:** Regularly review and refactor the code to eliminate dead or unnecessary variables.
-   **Automated Static Analysis Tools:** Use static analysis tools to detect unused variables and other unnecessary code patterns.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-007/#examples "Permanent link")


### Contract with Unused Variables[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-007/#contract-with-unused-variables "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-007/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.4.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-007/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-007/#__codelineno-0-3)contract UnusedVariables {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-007/#__codelineno-0-4)    uint public balance;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-007/#__codelineno-0-5)    uint public unusedVariable; // This variable is not used anywhere [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-007/#__codelineno-0-6)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-007/#__codelineno-0-7)    function deposit(uint amount) public payable {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-007/#__codelineno-0-8)        require(msg.value == amount, "ETH amount mismatch");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-007/#__codelineno-0-9)        balance += amount;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-007/#__codelineno-0-10)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-007/#__codelineno-0-11)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-007/#__codelineno-0-12)    function withdraw(uint amount) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-007/#__codelineno-0-13)        balance -= amount;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-007/#__codelineno-0-14)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-007/#__codelineno-0-15)}`

In the example above, the `unusedVariable` is declared but never used within the contract. This is a waste of storage space and can confuse anyone reading or auditing the code.

title: SCWE-008: Hardcoded Constants

*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-008: Hardcoded Constants

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-008/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-547: Use of Hard-coded, Security-relevant Constants [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/547.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/547.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-008/#description "Permanent link")

Hardcoded constants refer to values that are embedded directly into the code and cannot be easily changed without modifying the code itself. These constants may include critical parameters, addresses, or settings that could be subject to change based on external factors or evolving needs. Hardcoding these values in the code introduces several issues:

-   **Lack of flexibility**: Once the contract is deployed, these hardcoded values cannot be changed without deploying a new version, leading to inefficiency and reduced adaptability.
-   **Security risks**: Hardcoded values may expose sensitive information or create vulnerabilities if they are not properly protected.
-   **Upgrade challenges**: Contracts with hardcoded constants cannot easily evolve to support new functionality or parameters without requiring costly redeployment.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-008/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Use variables instead of constants**: Instead of hardcoding values, define them as variables that can be updated through administrative actions.
-   **Implement upgradeable contract patterns**: Use proxy contracts or other patterns that support upgrades to allow flexibility in modifying constants.
-   **External configuration**: Use off-chain storage for configuration values that can be updated without needing to deploy new contract versions.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-008/#examples "Permanent link")


### Contract with Hardcoded Constants[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-008/#contract-with-hardcoded-constants "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-008/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-008/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-008/#__codelineno-0-3)contract HardcodedConstants {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-008/#__codelineno-0-4)    address public owner = 0x1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef12345678; // Hardcoded address    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-008/#__codelineno-0-5)    uint public maxSupply = 1000000; // Hardcoded supply limit [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-008/#__codelineno-0-6)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-008/#__codelineno-0-7)    function setOwner(address newOwner) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-008/#__codelineno-0-8)        owner = newOwner;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-008/#__codelineno-0-9)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-008/#__codelineno-0-10)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-008/#__codelineno-0-11)    function setMaxSupply(uint newMaxSupply) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-008/#__codelineno-0-12)        maxSupply = newMaxSupply;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-008/#__codelineno-0-13)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-008/#__codelineno-0-14)}`

In this example, the `owner` address and `maxSupply` are hardcoded values that cannot be changed without redeploying the contract. This reduces flexibility and creates potential security risks.

# SCWE-009: Deprecated Variable and Function Usage

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-009/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-477: Use of Obsolete Function [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/477.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/477.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-009/#description "Permanent link")

The use of deprecated variables and functions refers to employing code elements that are no longer recommended for use, either due to obsolescence, security concerns, or the introduction of better alternatives. Using such elements can cause issues, including reduced compatibility, poor maintainability, and security vulnerabilities. Specific concerns related to deprecated usage are:

-   **Security risks**: Deprecated functions may have known vulnerabilities or might not be patched.
-   **Compatibility issues**: Newer compiler versions and environments may not support deprecated code.
-   **Maintenance difficulties**: Continuing to use deprecated code increases the complexity of codebase management and prevents clean upgrades.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-009/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Replace deprecated functions**: Always use the recommended and supported alternatives in the latest compiler versions.
-   **Update dependencies**: If relying on libraries that use deprecated elements, upgrade to versions that support current standards.
-   **Monitor for deprecation warnings**: Stay informed about deprecated functions in the Solidity language or external libraries and refactor the code when necessary.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-009/#examples "Permanent link")


### Contract with Deprecated Function Usage[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-009/#contract-with-deprecated-function-usage "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-009/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.4.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-009/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-009/#__codelineno-0-3)contract DeprecatedUsage {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-009/#__codelineno-0-4)    address public owner;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-009/#__codelineno-0-5)    uint public balance; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-009/#__codelineno-0-6)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-009/#__codelineno-0-7)    // Deprecated function, example using older Solidity versions    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-009/#__codelineno-0-8)    function sendTransaction(address recipient, uint amount) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-009/#__codelineno-0-9)        recipient.transfer(amount);    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-009/#__codelineno-0-10)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-009/#__codelineno-0-11)}`

In this example, the `transfer` function in Solidity's older versions is deprecated. Continuing to use such functions can cause issues with future compiler versions.

### Improved Contract without Deprecated Usage[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-009/#improved-contract-without-deprecated-usage "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-009/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-009/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-009/#__codelineno-1-3)contract UpdatedUsage {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-009/#__codelineno-1-4)    address public owner;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-009/#__codelineno-1-5)    uint public balance; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-009/#__codelineno-1-6)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-009/#__codelineno-1-7)    // Replaced with call{value} — avoids 2300 gas limit of transfer/send    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-009/#__codelineno-1-8)    function sendTransaction(address recipient, uint amount) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-009/#__codelineno-1-9)        (bool success, ) = payable(recipient).call{value: amount}("");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-009/#__codelineno-1-10)        require(success, "Transfer failed");    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-009/#__codelineno-1-11)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-009/#__codelineno-1-12)}`

# SCWE-010: Shadowing Variables and Functions

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   **CWE-1109: Use of Same Variable for Multiple Purposes**
    [CWE-1109](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1109.html)
    Description: This weakness occurs when a variable is used for multiple purposes in a way that causes confusion, bugs, or unintentional side effects. In the context of smart contracts, shadowing variables leads to such misuse, as it causes ambiguity between different scopes.


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#description "Permanent link")

Shadowing variables or functions is a scenario where a local variable or function shares the same name as one in a larger or outer scope. This can cause ambiguity and lead to unexpected behavior or bugs, as the inner variable or function hides the outer one. This problem is especially tricky in Solidity due to its inheritance model, where a child contract might unintentionally override parent contract variables or functions.


### Key issues:[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#key-issues "Permanent link")

-   **Ambiguity**: The developer might not be aware that a variable or function is being hidden.
-   **Unintentional logic errors**: It may lead to the wrong variable being accessed, or the wrong function being called.
-   **Difficulty in debugging**: Shadowing makes the code harder to understand and trace, especially in complex contracts or when inheritance is involved.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Use unique and descriptive names**: Always use unique names for variables and functions to avoid shadowing. Use clear, descriptive names for contract variables and functions.
-   **Avoid redeclaring variables in nested scopes**: Ensure that variables or functions in inner scopes don’t conflict with those in outer scopes.
-   **Static analysis tools**: Use static analysis tools to detect and warn about shadowing issues.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#examples "Permanent link")

text:
### Example of Shadowing Variables and Functions[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#example-of-shadowing-variables-and-functions "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-0-3)contract ShadowingExample {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-0-4)    uint public balance; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-0-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-0-6)    // This function shadows the 'balance' variable    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-0-7)    function deposit(uint balance) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-0-8)        // Local variable 'balance' now shadows the contract's balance variable        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-0-9)        balance += balance;  // This operation affects the local 'balance', not the contract's state variable    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-0-10)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-0-11)} [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-0-12)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-0-13)contract Test {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-0-14)    ShadowingExample example; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-0-15)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-0-16)    constructor() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-0-17)        example = new ShadowingExample();    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-0-18)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-0-19)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-0-20)    function testDeposit() public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-0-21)        example.deposit(100);  // Calling the deposit function on the example contract    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-0-22)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-0-23)}`

In the above example, the parameter `balance` in the `deposit` function shadows the contract’s state variable `balance`. This causes confusion, and the operation `balance += balance`; modifies the local variable instead of the contract state variable, leading to unexpected behavior.

[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-1-14)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-1-15)    constructor() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-1-16)        example = new ShadowingExample();    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-1-17)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-1-18)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-1-19)    function testDeposit() public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-1-20)        example.deposit(100);  // Calling the deposit function on the example contract    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-1-21)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-010/#__codelineno-1-22)}`

# SCWE-011: Insecure ABI Encoding and Decoding

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-011/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-116: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/116.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/116.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-011/#description "Permanent link")

Insecure ABI encoding and decoding occur when a smart contract improperly handles data serialization and deserialization, leading to vulnerabilities such as data corruption, type confusion, or reentrancy attacks. Solidity provides ABI encoding functions like `abi.encode()`, `abi.encodePacked()`, and `abi.decode()`, but improper usage can cause unexpected behavior.

Common issues with insecure ABI handling: - **Collision Risks in `abi.encodePacked()`**: Multiple concatenated parameters can lead to ambiguous encoding, making it vulnerable to hash collisions. - **Unchecked Decoding**: Improper use of `abi.decode()` can result in unintended memory corruption or type confusion. - **Lack of Input Validation**: Encoding user inputs without verification can introduce security flaws. - **Mismatched Data Types**: Decoding an incorrectly encoded data structure can lead to invalid memory access.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-011/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Use `abi.encode()` Instead of `abi.encodePacked()` for Hashing**: Prevent collision risks by ensuring unique encoding.
-   **Validate Data Before Decoding**: Ensure the encoded data conforms to the expected structure before decoding.
-   **Match Encoding and Decoding Types**: Always use the correct type structure when decoding to avoid unintended behavior.
-   **Avoid Direct ABI Decoding of External Calls**: Use strict validation mechanisms when handling data from external contracts.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-011/#examples "Permanent link")


### Example of Insecure ABI Encoding:[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-011/#example-of-insecure-abi-encoding "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-011/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-011/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-011/#__codelineno-0-3)contract InsecureABI {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-011/#__codelineno-0-4)    function hashValues(string memory str, uint256 num) public pure returns (bytes32) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-011/#__codelineno-0-5)        return keccak256(abi.encodePacked(str, num)); // Collision risk    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-011/#__codelineno-0-6)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-011/#__codelineno-0-7)}`

-   In this example, `abi.encodePacked()` creates a collision risk because different input combinations can produce the same hash.

title: SCWE-011: Insecure ABI Encoding and Decoding
heading: Refactored to Secure ABI Encoding:[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-011/#refactored-to-secure-abi-encoding "Permanent link")
text:
### Refactored to Secure ABI Encoding:[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-011/#refactored-to-secure-abi-encoding "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-011/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-011/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-011/#__codelineno-1-3)contract SecureABI {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-011/#__codelineno-1-4)    function hashValues(string memory str, uint256 num) public pure returns (bytes32) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-011/#__codelineno-1-5)        return keccak256(abi.encode(str, num)); // Unique encoding, no collision    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-011/#__codelineno-1-6)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-011/#__codelineno-1-7)}`

-   In this improved version, `abi.encode()` ensures a unique encoding structure, preventing hash collision attacks.

# SCWE-013: Unauthorized Parameter Changes

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-013/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-233: Improper Handling of Parameters [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/233.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/233.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-013/#description "Permanent link")

Unauthorized parameter changes occur when privileged smart contract parameters—such as fees, governance rules, withdrawal limits, or security configurations—can be modified by a single entity or an unauthorized user. This can lead to **unexpected behavior, security risks, or financial loss** if an attacker gains access to the privileged account.

Key risks associated with unauthorized parameter changes: - **Single Point of Control**: A centralized owner can unilaterally alter critical parameters, leading to governance concerns. - **Malicious Modifications**: Attackers who exploit an access control flaw may change key parameters, resulting in stolen funds or manipulated contract logic. - **Lack of Transparency**: Hidden or undocumented parameter changes can mislead users and investors, reducing trust. - **Impact on DeFi Protocols**: Unauthorized changes to liquidity pool fees, interest rates, or reward mechanisms can disrupt incentives and harm protocol users.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-013/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Use Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)**: Assign granular roles and restrict who can modify key parameters.
-   **Multisig Approval for Parameter Changes**: Require governance approval (e.g., Gnosis Safe) before making critical updates.
-   **Timelocks for Parameter Changes**: Introduce time delays on modifications to allow community review and prevent instant malicious changes.
-   **On-Chain Governance for DAOs**: Utilize decentralized governance mechanisms where stakeholders vote on parameter updates.
-   **Emit Events for Transparency**: Log all parameter changes on-chain to ensure visibility and auditability.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-013/#examples "Permanent link")

-   In this example, the owner can unilaterally change the fee rate, which poses a security risk.

### Refactored to Require Multisig and Timelocks[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-013/#refactored-to-require-multisig-and-timelocks "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-013/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-013/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-013/#__codelineno-1-3)interface ITimelock {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-013/#__codelineno-1-4)    function queueTransaction(address target, uint256 value, bytes calldata data, uint256 eta) external;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-013/#__codelineno-1-5)    function executeTransaction(address target, uint256 value, bytes calldata data, uint256 eta) external; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-013/#__codelineno-1-6)} [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-013/#__codelineno-1-7)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-013/#__codelineno-1-8)contract SecureGovernance {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-013/#__codelineno-1-9)    ITimelock public timelock;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-013/#__codelineno-1-10)    uint256 public feeRate; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-013/#__codelineno-1-11)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-013/#__codelineno-1-12)    constructor(address _timelock) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-013/#__codelineno-1-13)        timelock = ITimelock(_timelock);        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-013/#__codelineno-1-14)        feeRate = 5; // Default fee rate    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-013/#__codelineno-1-15)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-013/#__codelineno-1-16)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-013/#__codelineno-1-17)    function updateFeeRate(uint256 newRate) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-013/#__codelineno-1-18)        bytes memory data = abi.encodeWithSignature("setFeeRate(uint256)", newRate);        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-013/#__codelineno-1-19)        timelock.queueTransaction(address(this), 0, data, block.timestamp + 2 days); // ✅ Adds delay before execution    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-013/#__codelineno-1-20)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-013/#__codelineno-1-21)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-013/#__codelineno-1-22)    function setFeeRate(uint256 newRate) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-013/#__codelineno-1-23)        require(msg.sender == address(timelock), "Only timelock can execute");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-013/#__codelineno-1-24)        feeRate = newRate;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-013/#__codelineno-1-25)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-013/#__codelineno-1-26)}`

This improved version: - Uses a Timelock contract to delay parameter changes, preventing instant unauthorized updates. - Restricts execution to an approved governance mechanism, preventing a single actor from making direct changes.

# SCWE-014: Lack of Emergency Stop Mechanism

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   **CWE-693**: Protection Mechanism Failure
    [CWE-693](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/693.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#description "Permanent link")

A Lack of Emergency Stop Mechanism refers to the absence of a built-in feature in a smart contract that allows for halting or pausing critical operations during emergencies. This mechanism is essential for mitigating risks like a discovered vulnerability, unexpected behavior, or a malicious attack. Without this safeguard, the contract may continue executing malicious actions or suffer irreversible damage. The ability to stop critical functions provides an important recovery measure in scenarios where an exploit is detected or control needs to be regained.

Key risks: - Continuous execution of harmful or malicious actions without control. - Difficulty in recovering from unexpected failures. - Increased vulnerability to hacks or exploitation.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Implement a pausable contract pattern**: Use the `Pausable` contract from the OpenZeppelin library to implement a mechanism that allows authorized users (e.g., the owner or a governance entity) to pause and unpause certain critical contract functions.
-   **Limit emergency stop to critical functions**: Ensure that only critical functions can be paused to minimize the impact on the rest of the system's operation.
-   **Implement role-based access control**: Use a role-based mechanism to control who has the ability to pause or unpause functions, reducing the risk of unauthorized access.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#examples "Permanent link")


### Lack of Emergency Stop Mechanism Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#lack-of-emergency-stop-mechanism-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-0-3)contract NoEmergencyStop {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-0-4)    address public owner;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-0-5)    uint public criticalValue; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-0-6)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-0-7)    constructor() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-0-8)        owner = msg.sender;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-0-9)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-0-10)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-0-11)    // This function is critical and lacks an emergency stop mechanism    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-0-12)    function updateCriticalValue(uint newValue) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-0-13)        require(msg.sender == owner, "Only the owner can update this value");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-0-14)        criticalValue = newValue;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-0-15)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-0-16)}`

In the `NoEmergencyStop` contract, there is no way to stop or pause critical operations, which makes it vulnerable to continued exploitation if an issue arises.

title: SCWE-014: Lack of Emergency Stop Mechanism
heading: Fixed: Emergency Stop Mechanism Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#fixed-emergency-stop-mechanism-example "Permanent link")
text:
### Fixed: Emergency Stop Mechanism Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#fixed-emergency-stop-mechanism-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-1-3)import "@openzeppelin/contracts/security/Pausable.sol"; // OZ 5.x: utils/Pausable.sol [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-1-4)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-1-5)contract EmergencyStopExample is Pausable {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-1-6)    address public owner;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-1-7)    uint public criticalValue; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-1-8)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-1-9)    constructor() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-1-10)        owner = msg.sender;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-1-11)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-1-12)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-1-13)    // Critical function that can be paused in case of emergency    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-1-14)    function updateCriticalValue(uint newValue) public whenNotPaused {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-1-15)        require(msg.sender == owner, "Only the owner can update this value");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-1-16)        criticalValue = newValue;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-1-17)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-1-18)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-1-19)    // Emergency stop function to pause the contract    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-1-20)    function emergencyStop() public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-1-21)        require(msg.sender == owner, "Only the owner can stop the contract");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-1-22)        _pause();  // Pauses the contract    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-1-23)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-1-24)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-1-25)    // Emergency restart function to unpause the contract    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-1-26)    function resumeOperations() public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-1-27)        require(msg.sender == owner, "Only the owner can resume the contract");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-1-28)        _unpause();  // Resumes the contract    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-1-29)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-014/#__codelineno-1-30)}`

The `EmergencyStopExample` contract implements the `Pausable` pattern, which allows the contract owner to pause and unpause critical functions using the `emergencyStop` and `resumeOperations` functions. This ensures that if a vulnerability is discovered or a critical issue occurs, the contract can be halted temporarily to prevent further damage.

heading: Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-039/#examples "Permanent link")
text:
*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-039: Insecure Use of Inline Assembly

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-039/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-704: Incorrect Type Conversion or Cast
    [CWE-704 Link](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/704.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-039/#description "Permanent link")

Insecure use of inline assembly refers to vulnerabilities that arise when low-level assembly code is used improperly. This can lead to: - Incorrect type conversions or casts. - Exploitation of vulnerabilities in low-level operations. - Loss of funds or data.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-039/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Avoid inline assembly:** Use high-level Solidity code whenever possible.
-   **Validate inputs:** Ensure all inputs to assembly code are properly validated.
-   **Test thoroughly:** Conduct extensive testing to ensure assembly code is secure.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-039/#examples "Permanent link")

-   **Insecure Inline Assembly- Unsafe Type Casting Leads to Exploitable Overflow**

    `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-039/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-039/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-039/#__codelineno-0-3)contract InsecureAssembly {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-039/#__codelineno-0-4)    function unsafeCast(uint256 value) public pure returns (uint8) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-039/#__codelineno-0-5)        uint8 result;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-039/#__codelineno-0-6)        assembly {            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-039/#__codelineno-0-7)            result := value // Unsafe cast, truncating high bits        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-039/#__codelineno-0-8)        }        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-039/#__codelineno-0-9)        return result;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-039/#__codelineno-0-10)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-039/#__codelineno-0-11)}`

    ⚠️ Why is this Vulnerable?
-   Casting a large uint256 into uint8 without bounds checking causes integer truncation.
-   If value = 257, it becomes 1 (256 is lost).
-   Attackers can bypass security checks if truncation affects authentication or balance checks.

-   **Secure Alternative — High-Level Code with Bounds Checking**

    `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-039/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-039/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-039/#__codelineno-1-3)contract SecureAssembly {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-039/#__codelineno-1-4)    function safeCast(uint256 value) public pure returns (uint8) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-039/#__codelineno-1-5)        require(value <= type(uint8).max, "Value too large"); // Prevent truncation        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-039/#__codelineno-1-6)        return uint8(value);    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-039/#__codelineno-1-7)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-039/#__codelineno-1-8)}`

    Fixes:

-   Bounds checking (require) prevents unintended truncation.
-   Prefer high-level Solidity over assembly when possible; if assembly is required, validate inputs first.

* * *
