## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-040/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   **CWE-805: Buffer Access with Incorrect Length Value**
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/805.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/805.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-040/#description "Permanent link")

Incorrect storage packing in Solidity occurs when storage variables are not efficiently packed within a single storage slot, leading to unnecessary gas consumption. Solidity automatically stores variables in 32-byte (256-bit) slots, and inefficient ordering of data types can lead to wasted space. Contracts that fail to optimize storage packing may incur higher gas costs during deployments and transactions.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-040/#remediation "Permanent link")

To optimize storage packing:
\- Group smaller data types together (e.g., `uint8`, `bool`) to fit within a single 32-byte slot.
\- Avoid leaving gaps between variables of different sizes.
\- Order state variables efficiently to minimize wasted storage slots.


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-040/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-040/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-040/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-040/#__codelineno-0-3)contract InefficientStorage {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-040/#__codelineno-0-4)    uint256 a;  // Occupies full 32-byte slot    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-040/#__codelineno-0-5)    bool b;     // Occupies another 32-byte slot (wasteful)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-040/#__codelineno-0-6)    uint8 c;    // Uses a new 32-byte slot instead of sharing    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-040/#__codelineno-0-7)    uint256 d;  // Uses its own slot, leading to extra gas costs [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-040/#__codelineno-0-8)}`

**Why is this vulnerable?** - Each variable unnecessarily occupies a separate storage slot, increasing gas costs. - The `bool` and `uint8` could be packed into the same 32-byte slot, reducing wasted storage space.


### Fixed Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-040/#fixed-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-040/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-040/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-040/#__codelineno-1-3)contract OptimizedStorage {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-040/#__codelineno-1-4)    uint256 a;   // Occupies one full 32-byte slot    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-040/#__codelineno-1-5)    uint256 d;   // Placed next to 'a' to use another full slot    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-040/#__codelineno-1-6)    bool b;      // Packed within the same slot as 'c'    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-040/#__codelineno-1-7)    uint8 c;     // Fits within the same slot as 'b' [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-040/#__codelineno-1-8)}`

**Why is this safe?** - `bool` and `uint8` share the same storage slot, reducing unnecessary storage use. - `uint256` variables are placed together to minimize fragmentation. - Optimized storage layout leads to lower gas costs for contract execution.

**By correctly ordering state variables and utilizing Solidity’s storage packing rules, developers can significantly reduce gas fees and improve contract efficiency.**

# SCWE-041: Unsafe Downcasting

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-041/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   **CWE-681: Incorrect Conversion between Numeric Types**
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/681.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/681.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-041/#description "Permanent link")

Unsafe downcasting occurs when a larger integer type is implicitly or explicitly converted to a smaller type, leading to precision loss, unintended value changes, or integer overflows. Solidity does not automatically check for overflow when performing explicit type conversions, making it possible to unintentionally truncate values.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-041/#remediation "Permanent link")

To prevent unsafe downcasting:
\- Always validate that the value fits within the target data type before casting.
\- Use safe mathematical libraries like OpenZeppelin's `SafeCast` to ensure proper conversions.
\- Avoid unnecessary downcasting unless explicitly needed for gas optimization.


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-041/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-041/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-041/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-041/#__codelineno-0-3)contract UnsafeDowncasting {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-041/#__codelineno-0-4)    function truncateValue(uint256 largeNumber) public pure returns (uint8) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-041/#__codelineno-0-5)        return uint8(largeNumber);  // ⚠️ Potential data loss if largeNumber > 255    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-041/#__codelineno-0-6)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-041/#__codelineno-0-7)}`

**Why is this vulnerable?** - If `largeNumber > 255`, the higher bits will be truncated, resulting in unexpected values. - No validation ensures that `largeNumber` fits within `uint8`, leading to silent failures.


### Fixed Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-041/#fixed-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-041/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-041/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-041/#__codelineno-1-3)import "@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/math/SafeCast.sol"; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-041/#__codelineno-1-4)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-041/#__codelineno-1-5)contract SafeDowncasting {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-041/#__codelineno-1-6)    using SafeCast for uint256; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-041/#__codelineno-1-7)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-041/#__codelineno-1-8)    function safeTruncateValue(uint256 largeNumber) public pure returns (uint8) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-041/#__codelineno-1-9)        return largeNumber.toUint8();  // ✅ Ensures safe conversion    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-041/#__codelineno-1-10)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-041/#__codelineno-1-11)}`

**Why is this safe?**

-   Uses OpenZeppelin’s `SafeCast` library to enforce safe downcasting.
-   If `largeNumber` exceeds `uint8` limits, the transaction will revert instead of silently truncating.
-   Prevents unexpected behavior and potential security vulnerabilities.

**By properly handling type conversions, developers can avoid integer truncation issues and maintain data integrity in smart contracts.**

# SCWE-046: Reentrancy Attacks

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-046/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-367: Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/367.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/367.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-046/#description "Permanent link")

Reentrancy attacks occur when a contract allows untrusted external calls during execution without properly updating state variables or implementing protections. This enables attackers to repeatedly call functions and manipulate the contract’s state before execution completes. Common issues include:

-   Making external calls before updating state variables.
-   Lack of mechanisms to prevent repeated or recursive calls.
-   Improper handling of external interactions.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-046/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Update state first:** Modify critical state variables before any external calls.
-   **Implement reentrancy guards:** Use tools like `nonReentrant` modifiers to block recursive calls.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-046/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable Contract Example (Reentrancy)[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-046/#vulnerable-contract-example-reentrancy "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-046/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-046/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-046/#__codelineno-0-3)contract Vulnerable {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-046/#__codelineno-0-4)    mapping(address => uint) public balances; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-046/#__codelineno-0-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-046/#__codelineno-0-6)    function withdraw(uint _amount) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-046/#__codelineno-0-7)        require(balances[msg.sender] >= _amount);        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-046/#__codelineno-0-8)        (bool success, ) = msg.sender.call{value: _amount}(""); // Vulnerable: external call before state update (reentrancy)        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-046/#__codelineno-0-9)        require(success, "Transfer failed");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-046/#__codelineno-0-10)        balances[msg.sender] -= _amount;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-046/#__codelineno-0-11)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-046/#__codelineno-0-12)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-046/#__codelineno-0-13)    function deposit() public payable {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-046/#__codelineno-0-14)        balances[msg.sender] += msg.value;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-046/#__codelineno-0-15)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-046/#__codelineno-0-16)}`

# SCWE-047: Integer Overflows and Underflows

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-190: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/190.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/190.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#description "Permanent link")

Integer overflows and underflows occur when arithmetic operations exceed the bounds of the integer data type, causing the value to "wrap around" to an unexpected number.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Use Solidity 0.8.0 or later:** Leverage the compiler’s built-in overflow and underflow checks.
-   **Apply SafeMath libraries:** Use libraries like OpenZeppelin’s `SafeMath` for versions before 0.8.0.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.4.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#__codelineno-0-3)contract Vulnerable {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#__codelineno-0-4)    uint8 public totalSupply; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#__codelineno-0-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#__codelineno-0-6)    function addTokens(uint8 _value) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#__codelineno-0-7)        totalSupply += _value; // May overflow    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#__codelineno-0-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#__codelineno-0-9)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#__codelineno-0-10)    function subtractTokens(uint8 _value) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#__codelineno-0-11)        totalSupply -= _value; // May underflow    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#__codelineno-0-12)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#__codelineno-0-13)}`


### Fixed Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#fixed-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#__codelineno-1-3)contract Secure {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#__codelineno-1-4)    uint8 public totalSupply; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#__codelineno-1-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#__codelineno-1-6)    function addTokens(uint8 _value) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#__codelineno-1-7)        totalSupply += _value; // Built-in overflow check in 0.8+    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#__codelineno-1-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#__codelineno-1-9)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#__codelineno-1-10)    function subtractTokens(uint8 _value) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#__codelineno-1-11)        totalSupply -= _value; // Built-in underflow check in 0.8+    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#__codelineno-1-12)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-047/#__codelineno-1-13)}`

# SCWE-048: Unchecked Call Return Value

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-048/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-252: Unchecked Return Value [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/252.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/252.html)
-   CWE-390: Detection of Error Condition Without Action [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/390.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/390.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-048/#description "Permanent link")

Unchecked call return value vulnerabilities occur when a contract fails to validate the success or failure of low-level calls, such as `call`, `delegatecall`, and `staticcall`. Ignoring the return values of these calls can result in undetected errors, allowing malicious or unintended actions to succeed silently.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-048/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Check return values:** Always verify the success of low-level calls.
-   **Use higher-level abstractions:** Prefer method calls or, if you are confident that 2300 gas are sufficient for the recipient to handle the transfer, `transfer` over `call`, as they revert on failure.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-048/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-048/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-048/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-048/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-048/#__codelineno-0-3)contract UncheckedCall {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-048/#__codelineno-0-4)    function sendEther(address _recipient) public payable {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-048/#__codelineno-0-5)        _recipient.call{value: msg.value}(""); // Unchecked call, no error handling    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-048/#__codelineno-0-6)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-048/#__codelineno-0-7)}`


### Fixed Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-048/#fixed-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-048/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-048/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-048/#__codelineno-1-3)contract CheckedCall {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-048/#__codelineno-1-4)    function sendEther(address payable _recipient) public payable {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-048/#__codelineno-1-5)        (bool success, ) = _recipient.call{value: msg.value}("");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-048/#__codelineno-1-6)        require(success, "Transfer failed");    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-048/#__codelineno-1-7)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-048/#__codelineno-1-8)}`

Stable Version v1.0

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   **CWE-459: Incomplete Cleanup**
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/459.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/459.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#description "Permanent link")

In Solidity, mappings (`mapping(address => uint256)`) do not store key-value pairs in a way that allows them to be iterated over or deleted in a straightforward manner. Deleting a mapping variable does not remove its entries; it only resets the reference to the mapping, leaving stale data accessible if another variable references the same mapping. Improper deletion of mappings can lead to storage inconsistencies, potential access control issues, and unintended behavior.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Instead of using `delete mappingVariable;`, explicitly set each key’s value to zero where necessary.
-   Consider additional data structures (e.g., arrays or linked lists) to track mapping keys if deletion is required.
-   Ensure mapping deletions do not leave residual data that can be accessed unexpectedly.


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-0-3)contract Example {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-0-4)    mapping(address => uint256) public balances; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-0-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-0-6)    function addBalance(address user, uint256 amount) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-0-7)        balances[user] = amount;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-0-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-0-9)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-0-10)    function resetBalances() public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-0-11)        delete balances;  // ❌ This does not clear individual key-value pairs!    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-0-12)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-0-13)}`

**Why is this vulnerable?**

-   `delete balances;` only resets the storage reference but does not remove key-value pairs.
-   If another contract or function still references `balances`, the data remains accessible.
-   Unexpected behavior may arise where users assume balances have been erased but can still access the old data.

title: SCWE-053: Improper Deletion of Mappings

text:
### Fixed Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#fixed-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-1-3)contract SecureExample {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-1-4)    mapping(address => uint256) public balances;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-1-5)    address[] private users; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-1-6)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-1-7)    function addBalance(address user, uint256 amount) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-1-8)        if (balances[user] == 0) {            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-1-9)            users.push(user);        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-1-10)        }        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-1-11)        balances[user] = amount;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-1-12)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-1-13)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-1-14)    function resetBalances() public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-1-15)        for (uint256 i = 0; i < users.length; i++) {            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-1-16)            balances[users[i]] = 0;  // ✅ Explicitly clears each entry        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-1-17)        }        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-1-18)        delete users;  // ✅ Resets the tracking array    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-1-19)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-053/#__codelineno-1-20)}`

**Why is this safe?** - Tracks users in an array to allow explicit deletion of each mapping entry. - Ensures all key-value pairs are properly reset instead of just deleting the mapping reference. - Prevents residual data from being accessed unintentionally.

**By properly handling mapping deletions, developers can avoid unintended data persistence and ensure accurate contract state management.**

## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-060/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-703: Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/703.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/703.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-060/#description "Permanent link")

The use of floating pragmas (e.g., `^0.8.0`) in smart contract development can lead to unexpected issues when new versions of the Solidity compiler are released. Floating versions allow the contract to automatically use newer versions of the compiler within the specified range, which may introduce breaking changes, unexpected bugs, or security vulnerabilities. To avoid this, it is important to specify fixed versions to ensure the contract works reliably and consistently across different environments.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-060/#remediation "Permanent link")

To mitigate this vulnerability, always specify a fixed compiler version in the contract to avoid using floating pragmas. This ensures that the contract is compiled using a known and tested version of the compiler, preventing unexpected behavior from new, untested releases.


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-060/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-060/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0;  // Floating version allows for any 0.8.x version [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-060/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-060/#__codelineno-0-3)contract Vulnerable {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-060/#__codelineno-0-4)    uint public value; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-060/#__codelineno-0-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-060/#__codelineno-0-6)    function setValue(uint _value) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-060/#__codelineno-0-7)        value = _value;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-060/#__codelineno-0-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-060/#__codelineno-0-9)}`


### Fixed Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-060/#fixed-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-060/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity 0.8.4;  // Fixed version ensures no unexpected updates [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-060/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-060/#__codelineno-1-3)contract Fixed {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-060/#__codelineno-1-4)    uint public value; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-060/#__codelineno-1-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-060/#__codelineno-1-6)    function setValue(uint _value) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-060/#__codelineno-1-7)        value = _value;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-060/#__codelineno-1-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-060/#__codelineno-1-9)}`

## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-062/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-561: Dead Code
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/561.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/561.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-062/#description "Permanent link")

Code with no effects or Dead Code- refers to segments of a smart contract that are never executed or do not alter the contract's state or output. This can lead to unnecessary gas consumption, complicate the contract’s logic, and potentially confuse developers. Dead code often appears as leftover code from previous iterations or functions that are no longer in use but have not been removed. Removing such code improves contract efficiency and readability.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-062/#remediation "Permanent link")

To mitigate this vulnerability, ensure that all functions, variables, and logic in the smart contract have a purpose and contribute to the contract’s behavior. Unused code should be removed to reduce complexity, save gas, and improve maintainability.

# SCWE-066: Incorrect Handling of Bitwise Operations

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-066/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   **CWE-682: Incorrect Calculation**
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/682.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/682.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-066/#description "Permanent link")

Bitwise operations (e.g., `&`, `|`, `^`, `<<`, `>>`) can be efficient alternatives to arithmetic operations but are prone to errors if not used correctly. Misusing bitwise shifts can cause unintended value changes, integer overflows, or precision loss. Solidity lacks native overflow checks for bitwise shifts, making incorrect handling particularly dangerous in financial calculations or cryptographic functions.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-066/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Ensure bitwise shifts do not exceed the size of the data type (e.g., shifting a `uint8` left by 8+ bits).
-   Validate input ranges before performing shifts to prevent overflow or precision loss.
-   Avoid unnecessary bitwise operations in financial calculations unless explicitly needed.


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-066/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

``[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-066/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-066/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-066/#__codelineno-0-3)contract Example {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-066/#__codelineno-0-4)    function shiftLeft(uint8 input) public pure returns (uint8) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-066/#__codelineno-0-5)        return input << 8;  // ❌ Shifting beyond `uint8` capacity leads to zero    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-066/#__codelineno-0-6)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-066/#__codelineno-0-7)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-066/#__codelineno-0-8)    function bitwiseAnd(uint8 a, uint8 b) public pure returns (uint8) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-066/#__codelineno-0-9)        return a & b;  // ❌ Without proper validation, this could lead to unintended masking    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-066/#__codelineno-0-10)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-066/#__codelineno-0-11)}``

**Why is this vulnerable?**

-   `input << 8` shifts a `uint8` completely out of range, resulting in a value of `0`.
-   `a & b` can unintentionally mask critical bits if inputs are not properly validated.

### Fixed Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-066/#fixed-contract-example "Permanent link")

``[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-066/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-066/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-066/#__codelineno-1-3)contract SecureExample {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-066/#__codelineno-1-4)    function safeShiftLeft(uint8 input) public pure returns (uint8) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-066/#__codelineno-1-5)        require(input < 32, "Shift too large");  // ✅ Validate shift range        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-066/#__codelineno-1-6)        return input << 2;  // ✅ Safe shift within `uint8` bounds    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-066/#__codelineno-1-7)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-066/#__codelineno-1-8)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-066/#__codelineno-1-9)    function safeBitwiseAnd(uint8 a, uint8 b) public pure returns (uint8) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-066/#__codelineno-1-10)        require(a > 0 && b > 0, "Invalid input");  // ✅ Ensure inputs are meaningful        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-066/#__codelineno-1-11)        return a & b;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-066/#__codelineno-1-12)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-066/#__codelineno-1-13)}``

**Why is this safe?**

-   Restricts shift values to prevent unexpected overflows.
-   Ensures bitwise operations do not unintentionally modify values in an unintended way.
-   Protects contract logic from potential manipulation through poorly validated inputs.

**By correctly handling bitwise operations, developers can avoid unintended computation errors and ensure mathematical correctness in smart contracts.**

# SCWE-067: Assert Violation

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-067/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-754: Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-067/#description "Permanent link")

In Ethereum smart contracts, assertions (`assert`) are commonly used for internal consistency checks and to prevent erroneous states. However, if not used correctly, they can lead to unexpected behavior. When an `assert` statement fails, it reverts the entire transaction, and all changes made in the transaction are reverted. This can be problematic if it is used for conditions that can be expected during normal contract execution.

Using `assert` for conditions that can occur under normal circumstances (e.g., user inputs or contract logic) may cause unnecessary reverts and loss of gas. It’s important to reserve `assert` for critical errors, such as invariants and internal state checks that should never fail.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-067/#remediation "Permanent link")

To avoid unnecessary assertion failures, use `require` for input validation and conditions that can reasonably fail. `assert` should only be used for internal error detection and state validation that should never happen, as it signals a critical issue if violated.


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-067/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-067/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-067/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-067/#__codelineno-0-3)contract Vulnerable {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-067/#__codelineno-0-4)    uint public balance; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-067/#__codelineno-0-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-067/#__codelineno-0-6)    constructor() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-067/#__codelineno-0-7)        balance = 100;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-067/#__codelineno-0-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-067/#__codelineno-0-9)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-067/#__codelineno-0-10)    function withdraw(uint amount) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-067/#__codelineno-0-11)        assert(balance >= amount);  // Assert violation on user input        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-067/#__codelineno-0-12)        balance -= amount;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-067/#__codelineno-0-13)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-067/#__codelineno-0-14)}`

# SCWE-068: State Variable Default Visibility

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-068/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-704: Incorrect Type Conversion or Cast
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/704.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/704.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-068/#description "Permanent link")

In Solidity, state variables have a default visibility of `internal`, which means they can only be accessed within the contract or derived contracts (not by external callers). Omitting explicit visibility can lead to unintended behavior: for example, if a developer intends `private` but forgets to specify it, derived contracts can still access the variable; if they intend `public` but omit it, no getter is generated and external callers cannot read the value. Explicit visibility ensures the variable behaves as intended.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-068/#remediation "Permanent link")

Always explicitly specify the visibility of state variables. The possible visibility options are: - `public`: Accessible by anyone, both externally and internally. - `internal`: Accessible only within the contract or derived contracts (default). - `private`: Accessible only within the contract.


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-068/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-068/#__codelineno-0-1)contract Vulnerable {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-068/#__codelineno-0-2)    uint balance;  // Default internal; no getter — external callers cannot read it [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-068/#__codelineno-0-3)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-068/#__codelineno-0-4)    constructor() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-068/#__codelineno-0-5)        balance = 100;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-068/#__codelineno-0-6)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-068/#__codelineno-0-7)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-068/#__codelineno-0-8)    function updateBalance(uint amount) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-068/#__codelineno-0-9)        balance = amount;  // Intended public? Forgot visibility — no automatic getter    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-068/#__codelineno-0-10)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-068/#__codelineno-0-11)}`


### Fixed Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-068/#fixed-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-068/#__codelineno-1-1)contract Secure {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-068/#__codelineno-1-2)    uint private balance;  // Explicitly set visibility to private [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-068/#__codelineno-1-3)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-068/#__codelineno-1-4)    constructor() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-068/#__codelineno-1-5)        balance = 100;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-068/#__codelineno-1-6)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-068/#__codelineno-1-7)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-068/#__codelineno-1-8)    function updateBalance(uint amount) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-068/#__codelineno-1-9)        balance = amount;  // No external access to the variable    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-068/#__codelineno-1-10)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-068/#__codelineno-1-11)}`

# SCWE-069: Shadowing State Variables

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-069/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-1001: Variable Shadowing
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1001.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1001.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-069/#description "Permanent link")

Shadowing occurs when a state variable in a derived contract uses the same name as one in the base contract. This can lead to confusion and unexpected behavior, as the derived contract will hide the state variable from the base contract, potentially causing errors in contract logic or making it harder to maintain and audit the code.

It is essential to avoid naming state variables in derived contracts the same as those in base contracts to ensure that the intended state is correctly accessed and modified.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-069/#remediation "Permanent link")

To avoid state variable shadowing, use unique names for state variables in derived contracts or explicitly refer to the base contract variable using `super`. This will ensure that the correct state variable is accessed and manipulated as intended.


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-069/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-069/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-069/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-069/#__codelineno-0-3)contract Base {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-069/#__codelineno-0-4)    uint public balance; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-069/#__codelineno-0-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-069/#__codelineno-0-6)    constructor() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-069/#__codelineno-0-7)        balance = 100;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-069/#__codelineno-0-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-069/#__codelineno-0-9)} [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-069/#__codelineno-0-10)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-069/#__codelineno-0-11)contract Derived is Base {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-069/#__codelineno-0-12)    uint public balance;  // Shadows state variable from Base contract [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-069/#__codelineno-0-13)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-069/#__codelineno-0-14)    function updateBalance(uint amount) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-069/#__codelineno-0-15)        balance = amount;  // Refers to Derived's balance, not Base's balance    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-069/#__codelineno-0-16)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-069/#__codelineno-0-17)}`

# SCWE-072: Use of Deprecated Solidity Functions

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-072/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-676: Use of a Dangerous Function
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/676.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/676.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-072/#description "Permanent link")

Some Solidity functions and features have been deprecated over time due to security risks, inefficiencies, or better alternatives being introduced in newer versions of Solidity. Using deprecated functions can expose contracts to known vulnerabilities and potential attacks. Examples include `suicide()`, which was replaced by `selfdestruct()`, and `sha3()`, which was replaced by `keccak256()`.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-072/#remediation "Permanent link")

Always check the Solidity documentation to ensure that the functions you're using are not deprecated. If a function is deprecated, replace it with its recommended alternative to maintain the contract's security and ensure compatibility with future Solidity versions. **Note:** As of EIP-6049 (Solidity 0.8.24+), `selfdestruct` is deprecated and will be removed in a future EVM version.


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-072/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

``[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-072/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-072/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-072/#__codelineno-0-3)contract Example {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-072/#__codelineno-0-4)    function oldFunction() public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-072/#__codelineno-0-5)        // Using deprecated function `suicide`        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-072/#__codelineno-0-6)        suicide(msg.sender);  // Deprecated, should be replaced with `selfdestruct`    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-072/#__codelineno-0-7)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-072/#__codelineno-0-8)}``


### Fixed Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-072/#fixed-contract-example "Permanent link")

``[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-072/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-072/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-072/#__codelineno-1-3)contract Example {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-072/#__codelineno-1-4)    function oldFunction() public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-072/#__codelineno-1-5)        // Correctly using the recommended alternative `selfdestruct` (deprecated per EIP-6049; prefer migration patterns)        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-072/#__codelineno-1-6)        selfdestruct(payable(msg.sender));  // Replacing deprecated `suicide` with `selfdestruct`    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-072/#__codelineno-1-7)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-072/#__codelineno-1-8)}``

# SCWE-076: Right-To-Left-Override Control Character (U+202E)

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-076/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-451: User Interface (UI) Misrepresentation of Critical Information
    [CWE-451 Link](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/451.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-076/#description "Permanent link")

The Right-To-Left-Override (RTLO) control character (U+202E) can be used to manipulate the display order of text, creating misleading or deceptive visual representations in source code. Malicious actors can exploit this to: - Mask malicious logic or misrepresent code intent. - Introduce security-critical bugs that are difficult to detect visually. - Deceive auditors, developers, or end-users by obscuring real functionality.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-076/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Disallow U+202E in source code:** Ensure RTLO and similar Unicode direction control characters are explicitly banned in smart contracts.
-   **Static analysis tools:** Use static analysis to detect and prevent Unicode control characters in contract source code.
-   **Education and awareness:** Educate developers about the risks associated with Unicode control characters in smart contract development.

title: SCWE-076: Right-To-Left-Override Control Character (U+202E)

# SCWE-089: Vulnerable & Outdated Libraries

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-089/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-1104: Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components
    [CWE-1104 Link](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1104.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-089/#description "Permanent link")

Smart contracts that depend on outdated or vulnerable third‑party libraries inherit their security flaws. Attackers can exploit known issues in widely used libraries (e.g., reentrancy, integer overflow, or access control bypasses), especially if the library is no longer maintained or patched.
Common risks include:
\- Exploitation of known vulnerabilities in older OpenZeppelin versions or other dependencies.
\- Inheriting insecure logic or deprecated patterns from unmaintained libraries.
\- Increased attack surface due to indirect dependencies.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-089/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Version pinning:** Always specify exact, up‑to‑date versions of dependencies in `package.json`, `foundry.toml`, or `hardhat.config.js`.
-   **Regular audits:** Periodically review library versions for known vulnerabilities and upgrade accordingly.
-   **Vendor management:** Rely on reputable, actively maintained libraries (e.g., OpenZeppelin). Avoid custom forks unless fully audited.
-   **Automated scanning:** Use dependency scanners (e.g., `npm audit`, `snyk`, `slither-check-oz`) to detect outdated or vulnerable libraries.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-089/#examples "Permanent link")

[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-089/#__codelineno-0-7)}`

*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-090: Missing Slippage Protection in Automated Token Swaps

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-090/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-20: Improper Input Validation [CWE-20 Link](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-090/#description "Permanent link")

This weakness occurs when smart contracts execute token swaps through DEX routers (e.g., Uniswap, PancakeSwap, SushiSwap) with the amountOutMin parameter set to 0 or a hardcoded static value. This disables slippage protection and allows trades to execute regardless of adverse price movement. As a result, users or protocols may receive significantly fewer tokens than expected, especially under high volatility, front-running, or sandwich attack conditions.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-090/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Always validate amountOutMin based on live price quotes (e.g., using on-chain oracles or pre-trade estimates).
-   Allow users to configure slippage tolerance (0.5%, 1%, etc.), and enforce it in contract logic.
-   Never hardcode 0 or static values for amountOutMin.

# SCWE-091: Lack of Zero Value Check in Token Transfers

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-091/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-754: Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions
    [CWE-754 Link](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-091/#description "Permanent link")

This weakness occurs when smart contracts perform ERC20 token transfers without first validating that the transfer amount is greater than zero. While most ERC20 tokens allow zero‑value transfers, some implementations (e.g., LEND and others) revert when the amount is zero. This inconsistency can cause unexpected reverts in production, disrupt execution flow, and prevent critical contract logic from completing successfully.
Common risks include:
\- Unexpected revert when interacting with non‑standard ERC20 tokens that disallow zero‑value operations.
\- Potential denial‑of‑service conditions if an attacker or integration repeatedly triggers zero‑value transfers.
\- Broken integrations when protocols assume uniform ERC20 behavior across diverse tokens.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-091/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Validate transfer amounts:** Ensure `amount > 0` before calling `transfer`/`transferFrom`.
-   **Treat zero as a no‑op if acceptable:** Early‑return when `amount == 0` rather than calling token methods.
-   **Use robust token wrappers:** Centralize token operations (e.g., via OpenZeppelin `SafeERC20`) and standardize zero‑value handling.
-   **Integration testing:** Include zero‑value cases for all integrated tokens (especially known non‑standard tokens like LEND).
-   **Input sanitization:** Validate and sanitize externally supplied amounts prior to token interactions.

title: SCWE-092: Missing Disable Initializer in Constructor for Proxy Contracts
heading: Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#examples "Permanent link")
text:
*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-092: Missing Disable Initializer in Constructor for Proxy Contracts

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   **CWE-665**: [Improper Initialization](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/665.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#description "Permanent link")

This weakness occurs when upgradeable proxy contracts (e.g., UUPS or Transparent Proxy patterns) do not include a call to `_disableInitializers()` inside their constructor. Without this safeguard, malicious actors may invoke the `initialize()` function directly on the implementation contract. This can lead to takeover of admin roles, unauthorized ownership assignment, or malicious configuration of protocol-critical parameters.

This mistake is frequently observed in contracts built with OpenZeppelin Upgradeable libraries where developers forget to disable initializers in the implementation contract’s constructor.


## Impact[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#impact "Permanent link")

Failure to disable initializers in proxy contracts is a recurring and high-severity weakness. It enables attackers to:
\- Become the owner/admin of an uninitialized logic contract.
\- Hijack upgradeability or governance control.
\- Set malicious parameters (fees, treasury addresses, token supply logic, etc.).

This weakness has caused multiple security incidents in production DeFi and NFT projects where attackers initialized orphaned implementation contracts and drained funds.

Its importance stems from:
\- Widespread use of upgradeable contracts in DeFi and DAOs.
\- Frequent developer oversight when using proxy patterns.
\- High impact — loss of protocol ownership, funds, and governance control.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Always call `_disableInitializers()` in the constructor of implementation contracts.
-   Review all upgradeable contracts to ensure the implementation cannot be directly initialized.
-   Use OpenZeppelin’s recommended pattern and annotations (e.g., `@custom:oz-upgrades-unsafe-allow constructor`) when disabling initializers.

## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#examples "Permanent link")

-   **❌ Vulnerable Code**

    `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#__codelineno-0-1)// Implementation contract for a UUPS Proxy [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#__codelineno-0-2)pragma solidity ^0.8.20; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#__codelineno-0-3)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#__codelineno-0-4)import "@openzeppelin/contracts-upgradeable/proxy/utils/Initializable.sol"; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#__codelineno-0-5)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#__codelineno-0-6)contract Vault is Initializable {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#__codelineno-0-7)    address public owner; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#__codelineno-0-8)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#__codelineno-0-9)    function initialize(address _owner) public initializer {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#__codelineno-0-10)        owner = _owner;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#__codelineno-0-11)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#__codelineno-0-12)}`


⚠️ Issue:
\- The constructor does not call `_disableInitializers()`.
\- Attackers can directly call `initialize()` on the implementation contract (not through the proxy) and take over ownership.

-   **✅ Safe Code**

    `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#__codelineno-1-1)// Secure implementation contract for a UUPS Proxy [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#__codelineno-1-2)pragma solidity ^0.8.20; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#__codelineno-1-3)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#__codelineno-1-4)import "@openzeppelin/contracts-upgradeable/proxy/utils/Initializable.sol"; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#__codelineno-1-5)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#__codelineno-1-6)contract Vault is Initializable {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#__codelineno-1-7)    address public owner; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#__codelineno-1-8)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#__codelineno-1-9)    /// @custom:oz-upgrades-unsafe-allow constructor    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#__codelineno-1-10)    constructor() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#__codelineno-1-11)        _disableInitializers(); // Prevents initialize() from being called on implementation    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#__codelineno-1-12)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#__codelineno-1-13)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#__codelineno-1-14)    function initialize(address _owner) public initializer {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#__codelineno-1-15)        owner = _owner;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#__codelineno-1-16)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-092/#__codelineno-1-17)}`


✅ Fix:
\- Adding `_disableInitializers()` in the constructor ensures the logic (implementation) contract cannot be initialized directly.
\- Only the proxy can call `initialize()` safely during deployment.

# SCWE-093: Unnamed Function Parameters

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-093/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   **CWE-710**: [Improper Adherence to Coding Standards](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/710.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-093/#description "Permanent link")

This weakness occurs when functions declare parameters without names (only types). Unnamed parameters reduce code clarity and hinder maintainability, making it difficult for reviewers and future maintainers to understand the purpose and expected usage of each argument. In smart contracts, where correctness is critical, this ambiguity can result in misinterpretation, incorrect argument ordering in calls or refactors, and subtle logic errors.


## Impact[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-093/#impact "Permanent link")

Lack of clear parameter names can lead to: - Misuse of function arguments due to misunderstanding of their meaning.
\- Increased likelihood of logic bugs during refactoring and maintenance.
\- Higher audit and review overhead; reduced readability and self-documentation.
\- Potential security issues if parameters are confused (e.g., recipient vs. sender, amount vs. fee).


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-093/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Always provide descriptive names for all function parameters.
-   Choose meaningful, self-explanatory names consistent with a coding standard.
-   Supplement with NatSpec where helpful to document parameter intent and units.
-   Enforce naming conventions with linters and code review checklists.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-093/#examples "Permanent link")

-   **Vulnerable Code (Unnamed parameters reduce clarity)**

-   **✅ Safe Code (Named parameters improve readability)**

# SCWE-095: Missing Destination Address Size Check

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-095/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   **CWE-20**: [Improper Input Validation](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-095/#description "Permanent link")

This weakness occurs when a smart contract function accepts a `bytes32` parameter intended to represent an Ethereum address without validating its size. Ethereum addresses are 20 bytes, and using a `bytes32` type without proper checks can lead to incorrect address interpretation, potentially causing funds to be sent to unintended addresses.

This is especially risky in cross-chain, bridging, or interoperability contexts where address formats and padding conventions may vary. If the upper 12 bytes of the `bytes32` value are non-zero (or the value is otherwise malformed), naive casting to `address` can silently truncate or misinterpret the actual destination, leading to irreversible fund loss or misdirection.


## Impact[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-095/#impact "Permanent link")

Failure to validate `bytes32` inputs that represent addresses may enable: - Accidental misdirection of funds to unintended addresses due to truncation.
\- Loss of funds in production deployments, as ETH/token transfers are irreversible.
\- Exploitation by attackers who craft inputs with malicious upper bits to redirect value.
\- Integration fragility in cross-chain workflows where address encoding/padding differs.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-095/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Avoid using `bytes32` to represent addresses when possible; prefer the native `address` type.
-   If `bytes32` is required for protocol compatibility, validate that the upper 12 bytes are zero before casting: ensure `uint256(destination) >> 160 == 0`.
-   Centralize the validation and conversion logic in a dedicated helper to prevent inconsistent handling.
-   Add unit tests and fuzzing to verify that malformed `bytes32` values are rejected.

# SCWE-097: Missing Explicit Function Visibility

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-097/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-284: Improper Access Control
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/284.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/284.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-097/#description "Permanent link")

When a function’s visibility is omitted in Solidity, it defaults to `public`, allowing any caller to invoke logic that may have been intended to be internal or private. This expands the attack surface, enabling unauthorized state changes, fund movements, or reentrancy entry points.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-097/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Explicitly declare visibility (`private`, `internal`, `public`, `external`) on every function.
-   Use linters/static analysis to enforce visibility declarations.
-   Restrict privileged logic with proper access modifiers and role checks.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-097/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-097/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-097/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-097/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-097/#__codelineno-0-3)contract Vault {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-097/#__codelineno-0-4)    uint256 public balance; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-097/#__codelineno-0-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-097/#__codelineno-0-6)    function withdraw(uint256 amount) { // defaults to public        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-097/#__codelineno-0-7)        balance -= amount;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-097/#__codelineno-0-8)        payable(msg.sender).transfer(amount);    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-097/#__codelineno-0-9)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-097/#__codelineno-0-10)}`


### Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-097/#fixed "Permanent link")

# SCWE-120: Missing Return Data Length Validation

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-120/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-697: Incorrect Comparison
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/697.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/697.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-120/#description "Permanent link")

Low-level calls that decode return values without checking `returndatasize` can read zeroed or truncated data. Attackers can craft contracts that return short payloads so callers mis-interpret success flags, prices, or balances.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-120/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Verify `returndatasize` matches expected length before decoding.
-   Prefer high-level interfaces that perform ABI decoding checks.
-   Revert on unexpected return sizes and log anomalies.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-120/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-120/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-120/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-120/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-120/#__codelineno-0-3)(bool ok, bytes memory data) = token.staticcall(abi.encodeWithSignature("balanceOf(address)", user)); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-120/#__codelineno-0-4)uint256 bal = abi.decode(data, (uint256)); // assumes length >= 32`


### Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-120/#fixed "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-120/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-120/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-120/#__codelineno-1-3)(bool ok, bytes memory data) = token.staticcall(abi.encodeWithSignature("balanceOf(address)", user)); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-120/#__codelineno-1-4)require(ok && data.length == 32, "bad returndata"); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-120/#__codelineno-1-5)uint256 bal = abi.decode(data, (uint256));`

# SCWE-121: Swallowed Revert Reasons

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-121/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-388: Error Handling
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/388.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/388.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-121/#description "Permanent link")

Ignoring revert data (e.g., using `require(ok)` without bubbling reason) hides the root cause of failures. Protocols may proceed under incorrect assumptions, misprice risk, or block user funds without actionable errors.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-121/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Bubble revert reasons from external calls (`(bool ok, bytes memory data)`, then `assembly { revert(add(data,32), mload(data)) }` when `!ok`).
-   Standardize error handling with custom errors and propagate upstream.
-   Emit diagnostics when external calls fail to aid monitoring.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-121/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-121/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-121/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-121/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-121/#__codelineno-0-3)(bool ok, ) = target.call(payload); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-121/#__codelineno-0-4)require(ok, "call failed"); // hides real reason`


### Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-121/#fixed "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-121/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-121/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-121/#__codelineno-1-3)(bool ok, bytes memory data) = target.call(payload); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-121/#__codelineno-1-4)if (!ok) {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-121/#__codelineno-1-5)    assembly {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-121/#__codelineno-1-6)        revert(add(data, 32), mload(data))    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-121/#__codelineno-1-7)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-121/#__codelineno-1-8)}`

# SCWE-122: Calldata Length Not Validated Before Decode

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-122/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-20: Improper Input Validation
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-122/#description "Permanent link")

Functions that `abi.decode` calldata without first checking expected length can revert unpredictably or read malformed inputs. Attackers can craft short calldata to trigger reverts that lock functionality or bypass logic that runs before decode.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-122/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Validate `msg.data.length` against expected sizes (including selector).
-   Prefer Solidity typed arguments but still guard against undersized calldata on low-level entrypoints.
-   Reject unexpected trailing data when strict parsing is required.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-122/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-122/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-122/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-122/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-122/#__codelineno-0-3)function execute(bytes calldata data) external {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-122/#__codelineno-0-4)    (address to, uint256 amount) = abi.decode(data, (address, uint256));    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-122/#__codelineno-0-5)    // ... [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-122/#__codelineno-0-6)}`


### Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-122/#fixed "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-122/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-122/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-122/#__codelineno-1-3)function execute(bytes calldata data) external {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-122/#__codelineno-1-4)    require(data.length == 64, "bad length"); // selector handled elsewhere    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-122/#__codelineno-1-5)    (address to, uint256 amount) = abi.decode(data, (address, uint256)); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-122/#__codelineno-1-6)}`

*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-123: Corrupt Free Memory Pointer in Assembly

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-123/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-693: Protection Mechanism Failure
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/693.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/693.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-123/#description "Permanent link")

Inline assembly that writes to memory without preserving the Solidity free-memory pointer (at `0x40`) can corrupt ABI encoding for later calls or returns. Downstream decodes may misread buffers, leading to unexpected reverts or data leaks.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-123/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Save and restore the free-memory pointer when using custom memory writes.
-   Prefer Solidity primitives unless assembly is necessary; encapsulate unsafe sections.
-   Use formalized patterns for encoding/decoding (e.g., `abi.encode`) to avoid manual pointer math.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-123/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-123/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-123/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-123/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-123/#__codelineno-0-3)assembly {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-123/#__codelineno-0-4)    mstore(0x40, add(0x40, 0x20)) // advances but later writes may clobber    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-123/#__codelineno-0-5)    mstore(0x00, value) [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-123/#__codelineno-0-6)} [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-123/#__codelineno-0-7)// subsequent abi.encode may read corrupted area`


### Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-123/#fixed "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-123/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-123/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-123/#__codelineno-1-3)assembly {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-123/#__codelineno-1-4)    let memPtr := mload(0x40)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-123/#__codelineno-1-5)    mstore(memPtr, value)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-123/#__codelineno-1-6)    mstore(0x40, add(memPtr, 0x20)) [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CODE/SCWE-123/#__codelineno-1-7)}`
