*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-128: Insecure Multicall Context Forwarding

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-128/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-841: Improper Enforcement of Behavioral Workflow
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/841.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/841.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-128/#description "Permanent link")

Multicall-style aggregators that forward calls without guarding against reentrancy or context changes let attackers reorder actions within one tx (e.g., deposit then withdraw) or impersonate `msg.sender` when inner calls use `tx.origin` or cached sender state.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-128/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Apply reentrancy guards around multicall entrypoints.
-   Avoid caching `msg.sender` across calls; pass explicit sender/context to internal functions.
-   Restrict callable selectors/targets or enforce allowlists.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-128/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-128/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-128/#__codelineno-0-1)function multicall(bytes[] calldata data) external {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-128/#__codelineno-0-2)    for (uint i; i < data.length; i++) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-128/#__codelineno-0-3)        (bool ok, ) = address(this).delegatecall(data[i]);        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-128/#__codelineno-0-4)        require(ok, "fail");    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-128/#__codelineno-0-5)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-128/#__codelineno-0-6)}`


### Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-128/#fixed "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-128/#__codelineno-1-1)function multicall(bytes[] calldata data) external nonReentrant {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-128/#__codelineno-1-2)    for (uint i; i < data.length; i++) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-128/#__codelineno-1-3)        _dispatch(msg.sender, data[i]); // explicit context, no delegatecall loops    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-128/#__codelineno-1-4)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-128/#__codelineno-1-5)}`

title: SCWE-134: Low-Level Call to Non-Contract Address
heading: Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-134/#fixed "Permanent link")
text:
*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-134: Low-Level Call to Non-Contract Address

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-134/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-252: Unchecked Return Value
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/252.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/252.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-134/#description "Permanent link")

When using low-level `call`, `staticcall`, or `delegatecall` to a user-supplied or dynamic address, the target may be an EOA (externally owned account) with no contract code. In that case, the call returns `success = true` and empty return data, but no code executes. Contracts that assume the target performed logic (e.g., a callback, validation, or state change) can proceed under false assumptions, leading to bypassed checks, unexecuted logic, or incorrect accounting.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-134/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Verify that the target address contains code using `extcodesize` (or `address.code.length` in Solidity 0.8.12+) before low-level calls.
-   Use allowlists for callable targets instead of accepting arbitrary addresses.
-   Prefer high-level interface calls when the target is known to be a contract.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-134/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-134/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-134/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-134/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-134/#__codelineno-0-3)contract PluginRegistry {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-134/#__codelineno-0-4)    function executeViaPlugin(address plugin, bytes calldata data) external {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-134/#__codelineno-0-5)        (bool ok, ) = plugin.call(data);        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-134/#__codelineno-0-6)        require(ok, "plugin failed");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-134/#__codelineno-0-7)        // If plugin is an EOA, call "succeeds" but no code ran — logic may be bypassed    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-134/#__codelineno-0-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-134/#__codelineno-0-9)}`


### Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-134/#fixed "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-134/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-134/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-134/#__codelineno-1-3)contract PluginRegistry {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-134/#__codelineno-1-4)    function executeViaPlugin(address plugin, bytes calldata data) external {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-134/#__codelineno-1-5)        require(plugin.code.length > 0, "target has no code");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-134/#__codelineno-1-6)        (bool ok, ) = plugin.call(data);        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-134/#__codelineno-1-7)        require(ok, "plugin failed");    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-134/#__codelineno-1-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-134/#__codelineno-1-9)}`

title: SCWE-138: Reentrancy via ERC721/ERC1155 Safe Transfer Callbacks
heading: Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#vulnerable "Permanent link")
text:
*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-138: Reentrancy via ERC721/ERC1155 Safe Transfer Callbacks

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-841: Improper Enforcement of Behavioral Workflow
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/841.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/841.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#description "Permanent link")

ERC721 `safeTransferFrom` and ERC1155 `safeTransferFrom` invoke `onERC721Received` or `onERC1155Received` on the recipient contract. If the recipient is a contract that accepts NFTs and performs sensitive logic (e.g., withdrawals, state updates) inside these callbacks without reentrancy protection, an attacker can reenter the sender contract during the transfer and exploit stale state—similar to ERC777 hooks (SCWE-104) but for NFTs.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Add `nonReentrant` guards around functions that perform NFT transfers and any logic that could be reentered via the receiver callback.
-   Update state (e.g., balances, accounting) before calling `safeTransferFrom`.
-   Consider using `transferFrom` instead of `safeTransferFrom` when the recipient is trusted, to avoid callbacks.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#examples "Permanent link")

title: SCWE-138: Reentrancy via ERC721/ERC1155 Safe Transfer Callbacks
heading: Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#fixed "Permanent link")
text:
### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-0-3)interface IERC721 {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-0-4)    function safeTransferFrom(address from, address to, uint256 tokenId) external; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-0-5)} [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-0-6)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-0-7)contract NFTVault {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-0-8)    mapping(address => uint256) public deposits;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-0-9)    IERC721 public nft; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-0-10)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-0-11)    function deposit(uint256 tokenId) external {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-0-12)        nft.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), tokenId);        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-0-13)        deposits[msg.sender]++;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-0-14)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-0-15)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-0-16)    function withdraw(uint256 tokenId) external {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-0-17)        require(deposits[msg.sender] > 0, "No deposit");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-0-18)        nft.safeTransferFrom(address(this), msg.sender, tokenId);  // Callback here—attacker reenters        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-0-19)        deposits[msg.sender]--;  // Too late: attacker already reentered and passed the check    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-0-20)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-0-21)}`

**Why vulnerable:** During `withdraw`, `safeTransferFrom` calls `onERC721Received` on the recipient before the state update. A malicious contract can reenter `withdraw` in that callback, pass the `deposits[msg.sender] > 0` check again, and withdraw a second NFT (double withdrawal).


### Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#fixed "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-1-2)import "@openzeppelin/contracts/security/ReentrancyGuard.sol"; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-1-3)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-1-4)contract NFTVault is ReentrancyGuard {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-1-5)    mapping(address => uint256) public deposits;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-1-6)    IERC721 public nft; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-1-7)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-1-8)    function withdraw(uint256 tokenId) external nonReentrant {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-1-9)        require(deposits[msg.sender] > 0, "No deposit");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-1-10)        deposits[msg.sender]--;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-1-11)        nft.safeTransferFrom(address(this), msg.sender, tokenId);    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-1-12)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-138/#__codelineno-1-13)}`

**Fix:** `nonReentrant` blocks reentry through the ERC721 receiver callback.

title: SCWE-149: Transfers to Addresses That Cannot Receive Funds
heading: Fixed (Pull-based)[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-149/#fixed-pull-based "Permanent link")
text:
*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-149: Transfers to Addresses That Cannot Receive Funds

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-149/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-755: Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/755.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/755.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-149/#description "Permanent link")

Sending ETH or tokens to addresses that cannot receive them (e.g., contracts with no `receive`/`fallback`, or that revert on receive) causes the transfer to fail. In push-based distributions (e.g., airdrops, reward payouts), if one recipient cannot receive, the entire transaction reverts—leading to denial of service for all recipients. Pull-based patterns avoid this by letting users claim individually.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-149/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Prefer pull-based over push-based distributions.
-   If push-based is required, use `try/catch` to skip failing recipients and track failures, or validate recipients (e.g., reject contracts that don't implement a receiver interface).


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-149/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-149/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-149/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-149/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-149/#__codelineno-0-3)contract RewardDistributor {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-149/#__codelineno-0-4)    function distribute(address[] calldata users, uint256[] calldata amounts) external {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-149/#__codelineno-0-5)        for (uint256 i = 0; i < users.length; i++) {            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-149/#__codelineno-0-6)            (bool ok, ) = users[i].call{value: amounts[i]}("");            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-149/#__codelineno-0-7)            require(ok, "Transfer failed");  // One failure reverts entire batch        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-149/#__codelineno-0-8)        }    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-149/#__codelineno-0-9)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-149/#__codelineno-0-10)}`


### Fixed (Pull-based)[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-149/#fixed-pull-based "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-149/#__codelineno-1-1)mapping(address => uint256) public pendingRewards; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-149/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-149/#__codelineno-1-3)function claim() external {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-149/#__codelineno-1-4)    uint256 amount = pendingRewards[msg.sender];    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-149/#__codelineno-1-5)    require(amount > 0, "Nothing to claim");    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-149/#__codelineno-1-6)    pendingRewards[msg.sender] = 0;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-149/#__codelineno-1-7)    (bool ok, ) = msg.sender.call{value: amount}("");    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-149/#__codelineno-1-8)    require(ok, "Transfer failed"); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMM/SCWE-149/#__codelineno-1-9)}`

# SCWE-057: Write to Arbitrary Storage Location

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-057/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-20: Improper Input Validation
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-057/#description "Permanent link")

Writing to arbitrary storage locations can occur when a contract fails to properly validate inputs before interacting with storage variables. An attacker may exploit this vulnerability to overwrite sensitive storage slots, leading to unintended contract behavior, state manipulation, or loss of funds.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-057/#remediation "Permanent link")

To mitigate this vulnerability, ensure that all inputs to storage-related operations are properly validated. Avoid allowing external users to specify arbitrary storage locations. Use access control mechanisms to restrict who can modify sensitive state variables and ensure that only trusted users or contract functions can write to critical storage locations.


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-057/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-057/#__codelineno-0-1)contract ArbitraryStorageWrite {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-057/#__codelineno-0-2)    uint256 public balance; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-057/#__codelineno-0-3)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-057/#__codelineno-0-4)    function setStorage(uint256 storageLocation, uint256 value) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-057/#__codelineno-0-5)        assembly {            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-057/#__codelineno-0-6)            sstore(storageLocation, value)  // Writing to arbitrary storage location        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-057/#__codelineno-0-7)        }    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-057/#__codelineno-0-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-057/#__codelineno-0-9)}`

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-057/#__codelineno-1-1)contract SecureStorageWrite {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-057/#__codelineno-1-2)    uint256 public balance;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-057/#__codelineno-1-3)    address public owner; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-057/#__codelineno-1-4)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-057/#__codelineno-1-5)    modifier onlyOwner() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-057/#__codelineno-1-6)        require(msg.sender == owner, "Not the owner");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-057/#__codelineno-1-7)        _;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-057/#__codelineno-1-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-057/#__codelineno-1-9)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-057/#__codelineno-1-10)    constructor() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-057/#__codelineno-1-11)        owner = msg.sender;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-057/#__codelineno-1-12)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-057/#__codelineno-1-13)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-057/#__codelineno-1-14)    function setBalance(uint256 value) public onlyOwner {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-057/#__codelineno-1-15)        balance = value;  // Only the owner can modify the balance    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-057/#__codelineno-1-16)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-057/#__codelineno-1-17)}`

*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-083: Failure to Handle Edge Cases

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-754: Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#description "Permanent link")

Failure to account for edge cases can result in unexpected behaviors, security vulnerabilities, and unintended contract failures. Edge cases are unusual but possible inputs or states that developers often overlook, leading to incorrect logic, reverts, or even exploits.


### Common scenarios include:[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#common-scenarios-include "Permanent link")

-   Arithmetic Issues (e.g., division by zero, integer overflow/underflow, precision loss).
-   Boundary Conditions (e.g., handling empty arrays, minimum/maximum values).
-   State-Dependent Bugs (e.g., failing to check for uninitialized variables, invalid state transitions).
-   Gas-Related Failures (e.g., unbounded loops consuming excessive gas).


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#remediation "Permanent link")

Ensure that all edge cases are properly considered and handled during the development of the contract. Utilize `require` and `assert` to ensure proper validation of inputs, outputs, and states. - Implement explicit validation for all possible edge cases. - Use Solidity's built-in safety features (e.g., SafeMath, Solidity 0.8 overflow checks). - Use require/assert statements to enforce input constraints and expected states. - Test contracts thoroughly, including stress tests, fuzzing, and invariant testing.


### Vulnerable Contract Example- (Arithmetic Issue)[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#vulnerable-contract-example-arithmetic-issue "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#__codelineno-0-1)contract Example {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#__codelineno-0-2)    function divide(uint256 _numerator, uint256 _denominator) public pure returns (uint256) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#__codelineno-0-3)        return _numerator / _denominator; // Division by zero is not checked    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#__codelineno-0-4)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#__codelineno-0-5)}`


### Fixed Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#fixed-contract-example "Permanent link")

-   Solution: Use `require` to check for division by zero.

    `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#__codelineno-1-1)contract Example {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#__codelineno-1-2)    function divide(uint256 _numerator, uint256 _denominator) public pure returns (uint256) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#__codelineno-1-3)        require(_denominator != 0, "Cannot divide by zero");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#__codelineno-1-4)        return _numerator / _denominator;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#__codelineno-1-5)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#__codelineno-1-6)}`

title: SCWE-083: Failure to Handle Edge Cases
heading: Fixed Code:[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#fixed-code "Permanent link")
text:
### Handling Empty Arrays[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#handling-empty-arrays "Permanent link")

-   Issue: A function assumes that the array is never empty, leading to an out-of-bounds error.

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#__codelineno-2-1)contract Example {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#__codelineno-2-2)    uint256[] public data; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#__codelineno-2-3)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#__codelineno-2-4)    function getLast() public view returns (uint256) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#__codelineno-2-5)        return data[data.length - 1]; // ❌ Reverts if array is empty    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#__codelineno-2-6)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#__codelineno-2-7)}`


### Fixed Code:[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#fixed-code "Permanent link")

-   Solution: Validate that the array is not empty before accessing elements.

    `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#__codelineno-3-1)contract Example {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#__codelineno-3-2)    uint256[] public data; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#__codelineno-3-3)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#__codelineno-3-4)    function getLast() public view returns (uint256) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#__codelineno-3-5)        require(data.length > 0, "Array is empty");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#__codelineno-3-6)        return data[data.length - 1];    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#__codelineno-3-7)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-083/#__codelineno-3-8)}`

title: SCWE-110: Fee-On-Transfer Token Misaccounting
heading: Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-110/#fixed "Permanent link")
text:
*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-110: Fee-On-Transfer Token Misaccounting

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-110/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-682: Incorrect Calculation
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/682.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/682.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-110/#description "Permanent link")

Assuming an ERC20 transfer moves the full requested amount fails with fee-on-transfer or deflationary tokens. Protocols that credit users for the requested amount instead of the received amount can be drained or mis-account balances.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-110/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Measure token balances before and after transfers to calculate the actual received amount.
-   Maintain allowlists/blocks for incompatible tokens or handle fee-on-transfer explicitly.
-   Validate that accounting uses the net amount when updating shares or debts.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-110/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-110/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

# SCWE-111: Rebase Token Balance Drift

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-111/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-682: Incorrect Calculation
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/682.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/682.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-111/#description "Permanent link")

Rebasing tokens change user balances over time. Protocols that track deposited amounts as fixed units (instead of shares) can become insolvent or let users withdraw more than their fair share after positive or negative rebases.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-111/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Track user positions using share-based accounting that scales with total supply.
-   Normalize balances on every interaction or use wrappers that expose a non-rebasing interface (e.g., wstETH).
-   Validate integrations against tokens with elastic supply and document unsupported assets.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-111/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-111/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-111/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-111/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-111/#__codelineno-0-3)contract Savings {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-111/#__codelineno-0-4)    IERC20 public rebasingToken;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-111/#__codelineno-0-5)    mapping(address => uint256) public deposits; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-111/#__codelineno-0-6)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-111/#__codelineno-0-7)    function deposit(uint256 amount) external {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-111/#__codelineno-0-8)        rebasingToken.transferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-111/#__codelineno-0-9)        deposits[msg.sender] += amount; // assumes static balance    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-111/#__codelineno-0-10)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-111/#__codelineno-0-11)}`

title: SCWE-135: ERC4626 Share Inflation via Donations

*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-135: ERC4626 Share Inflation via Donations

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-135/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-682: Incorrect Calculation
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/682.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/682.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-135/#description "Permanent link")

ERC4626 vaults that do not guard against free-asset donations can skew `totalAssets` and share price. Attackers can donate assets to inflate share value and then mint shares cheaply before normalization, extracting value from existing holders.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-135/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Normalize share price on every deposit/mint using current `totalAssets`.
-   Optionally block unsolicited donations by reverting on direct transfers or sweeping them into reserves before new share mints.
-   Add tests for donation and price-per-share edge cases.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-135/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-135/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-135/#__codelineno-0-1)// totalAssets() uses balanceOf; donations inflate it and skew share price [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-135/#__codelineno-0-2)function mint(uint256 shares) external {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-135/#__codelineno-0-3)    uint256 assets = previewMint(shares);    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-135/#__codelineno-0-4)    asset.transferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), assets);    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-135/#__codelineno-0-5)    _mint(msg.sender, shares); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-135/#__codelineno-0-6)}`


### Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-135/#fixed "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-135/#__codelineno-1-1)uint256 private _accountedAssets; // internal balance; excludes direct transfers [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-135/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-135/#__codelineno-1-3)function totalAssets() public view override returns (uint256) {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-135/#__codelineno-1-4)    return _accountedAssets; // donations do not affect share price [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-135/#__codelineno-1-5)} [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-135/#__codelineno-1-6)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-135/#__codelineno-1-7)function deposit(uint256 assets, address receiver) public override returns (uint256 shares) {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-135/#__codelineno-1-8)    uint256 before = asset.balanceOf(address(this));    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-135/#__codelineno-1-9)    shares = super.deposit(assets, receiver);    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-135/#__codelineno-1-10)    _accountedAssets += (asset.balanceOf(address(this)) - before); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-135/#__codelineno-1-11)} [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-135/#__codelineno-1-12)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-135/#__codelineno-1-13)function withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address owner) public override returns (uint256 shares) {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-135/#__codelineno-1-14)    shares = super.withdraw(assets, receiver, owner);    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-135/#__codelineno-1-15)    _accountedAssets -= assets; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-COMP/SCWE-135/#__codelineno-1-16)}`

# SCWE-025: Improper Cryptographic Key Management

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-025/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-310: Cryptographic Issues
    [CWE-310 Link](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/310.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-025/#description "Permanent link")

Improper cryptographic key management refers to the failure to securely generate, store, or use cryptographic keys. This can lead to: - Unauthorized access to sensitive data. - Exploitation of the contract's logic. - Loss of funds or data.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-025/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Use secure key management:** Leverage secure key management systems or libraries.
-   **Avoid hardcoding keys:** Never hardcode cryptographic keys in the contract.
-   **Regularly rotate keys:** Periodically update cryptographic keys to reduce risks.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-025/#examples "Permanent link")

-   **Improper Key Management**

    `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-025/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-025/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-025/#__codelineno-0-3)contract ImproperKeyManagement {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-025/#__codelineno-0-4)    bytes32 private key = keccak256("insecure-key"); // Hardcoded key [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-025/#__codelineno-0-5)}`

-   **Proper Key Management**

    `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-025/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-025/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-025/#__codelineno-1-3)contract ProperKeyManagement {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-025/#__codelineno-1-4)    bytes32 private key; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-025/#__codelineno-1-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-025/#__codelineno-1-6)    constructor(bytes32 _key) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-025/#__codelineno-1-7)        key = _key; // Configurable key    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-025/#__codelineno-1-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-025/#__codelineno-1-9)}`

# SCWE-026: Insufficient Hash Verification

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-026/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
    [CWE-347 Link](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/347.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-026/#description "Permanent link")

Insufficient hash verification refers to the failure to properly verify hashes, such as message hashes or transaction hashes. This can lead to: - Unauthorized actions by malicious actors. - Loss of funds or data. - Exploitation of the contract's logic.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-026/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Validate hashes:** Ensure all hashes are properly verified before processing.
-   **Use secure libraries:** Leverage well-audited libraries for hash verification.
-   **Test thoroughly:** Conduct extensive testing to ensure hash verification works as intended.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-026/#examples "Permanent link")

-   **Insufficient Hash Verification**

    `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-026/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-026/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-026/#__codelineno-0-3)contract InsufficientHashVerification {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-026/#__codelineno-0-4)    function processHash(bytes32 hash) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-026/#__codelineno-0-5)        // Process hash without verification    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-026/#__codelineno-0-6)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-026/#__codelineno-0-7)}`

-   **Sufficient Hash Verification**

    `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-026/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-026/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-026/#__codelineno-1-3)contract SufficientHashVerification {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-026/#__codelineno-1-4)    function processHash(bytes32 hash, bytes memory data) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-026/#__codelineno-1-5)        require(keccak256(data) == hash, "Invalid hash");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-026/#__codelineno-1-6)        // Process hash    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-026/#__codelineno-1-7)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-026/#__codelineno-1-8)}`

# SCWE-027: Vulnerable Cryptographic Algorithms

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-027/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   **CWE-327:** Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
    [CWE-327 Link](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/327.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-027/#description "Permanent link")

Vulnerable cryptographic algorithms refer to the use of outdated or insecure cryptographic algorithms, such as MD5 or SHA-1. This can lead to: - Exploitation of the contract’s logic. - Loss of funds or data. - Reduced trust in the contract’s security.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-027/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Use secure algorithms:** Leverage modern cryptographic algorithms like SHA-256 or Keccak-256.
-   **Avoid deprecated algorithms:** Do not use algorithms known to be insecure.
-   **Test thoroughly:** Conduct extensive testing to ensure cryptographic security.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-027/#examples "Permanent link")

-   **Vulnerable Algorithm**

    `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-027/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-027/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-027/#__codelineno-0-3)contract VulnerableAlgorithm {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-027/#__codelineno-0-4)    function hashData(bytes memory data) public pure returns (bytes32) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-027/#__codelineno-0-5)        return sha256(data); // Insecure algorithm    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-027/#__codelineno-0-6)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-027/#__codelineno-0-7)}`

-   **Secure Algorithm**

    `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-027/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-027/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-027/#__codelineno-1-3)contract SecureAlgorithm {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-027/#__codelineno-1-4)    function hashData(bytes memory data) public pure returns (bytes32) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-027/#__codelineno-1-5)        return keccak256(data); // Secure algorithm    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-027/#__codelineno-1-6)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-027/#__codelineno-1-7)}`

# SCWE-054: Signature Malleability

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-054/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-345: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/345.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/345.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-054/#description "Permanent link")

Signature malleability refers to the ability to modify a valid signature without changing its validity. This can occur when signatures are not properly verified or when certain components of a signature (like the `v`, `r`, and `s` values) can be altered while still producing a valid signature.

Attackers can modify a signature’s `s` value or flip `v` between 27 and 28, generating different valid signatures for the same message. This can lead to:

-   Replay attacks, where transactions can be re-executed with modified signatures.
-   Transaction hijacking, where a valid signature is altered to redirect funds or manipulate contract state.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-054/#remediation "Permanent link")

To mitigate signature malleability, ensure that the signature verification process is robust. Use secure cryptographic libraries that properly handle signature validation, such as ECDSA or EdDSA with additional checks to prevent malleability. When verifying signatures, consider using a canonical format for signature components to avoid malleability.


### Vulnerable Contract Example- (Allows Signature Malleability)[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-054/#vulnerable-contract-example-allows-signature-malleability "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-054/#__codelineno-0-1)contract MalleableSignatureExample {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-054/#__codelineno-0-2)    function verifySignature(bytes32 message, uint8 v, bytes32 r, bytes32 s) public pure returns (bool) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-054/#__codelineno-0-3)        address signer = ecrecover(message, v, r, s);  // Signature malleability risk        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-054/#__codelineno-0-4)        return signer != address(0);    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-054/#__codelineno-0-5)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-054/#__codelineno-0-6)}`

\- This contract does not restrict `s` values, allowing malleable signatures. - Issue: The contract does not check if `s` is in the lower half of the `curve (s < secp256k1n/2)`, allowing multiple valid signatures for the same message.

title: SCWE-054: Signature Malleability
heading: Fixed Contract Example- Prevents Signature Malleability)[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-054/#fixed-contract-example-prevents-signature-malleability "Permanent link")
text:
### Fixed Contract Example- Prevents Signature Malleability)[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-054/#fixed-contract-example-prevents-signature-malleability "Permanent link")

  `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-054/#__codelineno-1-1)  pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-054/#__codelineno-1-2)  [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-054/#__codelineno-1-3)  import "@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/cryptography/ECDSA.sol"; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-054/#__codelineno-1-4)  [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-054/#__codelineno-1-5)  contract SecureSignatureExample {      [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-054/#__codelineno-1-6)      using ECDSA for bytes32; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-054/#__codelineno-1-7)      [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-054/#__codelineno-1-8)      function verifySignature(bytes32 message, bytes memory signature) public pure returns (address) {          [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-054/#__codelineno-1-9)          return message.toEthSignedMessageHash().recover(signature);      [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-054/#__codelineno-1-10)      }  [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-054/#__codelineno-1-11)  }`

-   Fix: Uses `OpenZeppelin’s ECDSA library`, which ensures `s` is in the lower half and restricts `v` to 27 or 28.
-   Outcome: Prevents attackers from modifying valid signatures to create alternate, equally valid ones.

# SCWE-055: Missing Protection against Signature Replay Attacks

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-055/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-294: Authentication Bypass by Capture-replay
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/294.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/294.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-055/#description "Permanent link")

Signature replay attacks occur when a valid signature from a previous transaction is reused in a different context, such as a different transaction or contract call. Without proper protection, an attacker can capture and replay a signature, potentially bypassing authentication checks and causing unauthorized actions or transactions.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-055/#remediation "Permanent link")

To prevent signature replay attacks, include additional checks that ensure the signature is valid for a specific transaction or context. This can be done by incorporating unique identifiers like a nonce, timestamp, or a unique transaction hash into the signature to bind it to a specific use. Always verify that the signature is only valid for the intended action.


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-055/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-055/#__codelineno-0-1)contract ReplayAttackExample {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-055/#__codelineno-0-2)    mapping(address => uint256) public nonces; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-055/#__codelineno-0-3)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-055/#__codelineno-0-4)    function authenticate(bytes32 message, uint8 v, bytes32 r, bytes32 s) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-055/#__codelineno-0-5)        address signer = ecrecover(message, v, r, s);        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-055/#__codelineno-0-6)        require(signer == msg.sender, "Invalid signature");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-055/#__codelineno-0-7)        // No protection against replay attacks; attacker can reuse the same signature    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-055/#__codelineno-0-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-055/#__codelineno-0-9)}`

title: SCWE-055: Missing Protection against Signature Replay Attacks
heading: Fixed Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-055/#fixed-contract-example "Permanent link")
text:
### Fixed Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-055/#fixed-contract-example "Permanent link")

  `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-055/#__codelineno-1-1)  pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-055/#__codelineno-1-2)  [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-055/#__codelineno-1-3)  import "@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/cryptography/ECDSA.sol"; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-055/#__codelineno-1-4)  [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-055/#__codelineno-1-5)  contract SecureReplayProtectionExample {      [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-055/#__codelineno-1-6)      using ECDSA for bytes32; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-055/#__codelineno-1-7)      [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-055/#__codelineno-1-8)      mapping(address => uint256) public nonces; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-055/#__codelineno-1-9)      [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-055/#__codelineno-1-10)      function authenticate(bytes32 message, bytes memory signature) public {          [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-055/#__codelineno-1-11)          uint256 nonce = nonces[msg.sender]++;          [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-055/#__codelineno-1-12)          bytes32 messageWithContext = keccak256(abi.encodePacked(message, nonce, block.chainid));          [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-055/#__codelineno-1-13)          address signer = messageWithContext.toEthSignedMessageHash().recover(signature);          [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-055/#__codelineno-1-14)          require(signer == msg.sender, "Invalid signature");      [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-055/#__codelineno-1-15)      }  [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-055/#__codelineno-1-16)  }`

**Fixes Implemented:** - Binds signature to a nonce (ensuring it's only usable once). - Includes `chainId` (prevents cross-chain replay attacks). - Uses OpenZeppelin’s ECDSA library (avoids signature malleability risks).

# SCWE-056: Lack of Proper Signature Verification

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-345: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/345.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/345.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#description "Permanent link")

This vulnerability occurs when a smart contract fails to properly verify whether a signature was produced by an authorized entity. In Ethereum, contracts often use `ecrecover` to check signatures, but failing to validate who signed the message allows:

-   Unauthorized transactions, where attackers submit signatures from any key.
-   Replay attacks, where valid signatures are reused to repeat actions.
-   Malicious contract state manipulation, where attackers gain unauthorized access.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#remediation "Permanent link")

To mitigate this vulnerability, always implement proper signature verification using secure cryptographic methods. Use the `ecrecover` function to recover the signer’s address and ensure that the recovered address matches the expected address. Additionally, verify that the signature is valid for the intended message or transaction and that the signer is authorized to perform the action.


### Vulnerable Contract Example- (Lack of Signer Verification)[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#vulnerable-contract-example-lack-of-signer-verification "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#__codelineno-0-1)contract SignatureVerificationExample {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#__codelineno-0-2)    function authenticate(bytes32 message, uint8 v, bytes32 r, bytes32 s) public view returns (address) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#__codelineno-0-3)        address signer = ecrecover(message, v, r, s);        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#__codelineno-0-4)        return signer;  // No further validation of the signer or message    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#__codelineno-0-5)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#__codelineno-0-6)}`

\- Issue: The contract does not check if the recovered address matches an authorized signer. - Exploit: Any valid ECDSA signature can be used, even from an attacker’s key.

heading: Fixed Contract Example- (Proper Signature Verification)[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#fixed-contract-example-proper-signature-verification "Permanent link")

### Fixed Contract Example- (Proper Signature Verification)[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#fixed-contract-example-proper-signature-verification "Permanent link")

    `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#__codelineno-1-1)    pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#__codelineno-1-2)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#__codelineno-1-3)    import "@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/cryptography/ECDSA.sol"; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#__codelineno-1-4)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#__codelineno-1-5)    contract SecureSignatureVerificationExample {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#__codelineno-1-6)        using ECDSA for bytes32; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#__codelineno-1-7)        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#__codelineno-1-8)        address public authorizedSigner; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#__codelineno-1-9)        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#__codelineno-1-10)        constructor(address _authorizedSigner) {            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#__codelineno-1-11)            require(_authorizedSigner != address(0), "Invalid signer");            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#__codelineno-1-12)            authorizedSigner = _authorizedSigner;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#__codelineno-1-13)        } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#__codelineno-1-14)        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#__codelineno-1-15)        function authenticate(bytes32 message, bytes memory signature) public view returns (bool) {            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#__codelineno-1-16)            address signer = message.toEthSignedMessageHash().recover(signature);            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#__codelineno-1-17)            require(signer == authorizedSigner, "Unauthorized signer"); // Proper validation            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#__codelineno-1-18)            return true;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#__codelineno-1-19)        }    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-056/#__codelineno-1-20)    }`

\- Fix: The contract now explicitly checks that the recovered address matches `authorizedSigner`. - Outcome: Prevents attackers from submitting arbitrary signatures and ensures only authorized signatures are accepted.

# SCWE-074: Hash Collisions with Multiple Variable Length Arguments

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-074/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/347.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/347.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-074/#description "Permanent link")

When hashing multiple variable-length arguments, there is a potential risk of hash collisions, which can occur if two different sets of inputs produce the same hash output. This vulnerability is particularly relevant in situations where hashes are used as identifiers, signatures, or keys, and collisions may lead to incorrect behavior or security breaches, such as false validation of signatures or unexpected contract logic execution.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-074/#remediation "Permanent link")

To prevent hash collisions, use a strong cryptographic hashing function like `keccak256` or `sha256`, and ensure that the inputs to the hash function are well-structured. Consider combining different sources of entropy (e.g., timestamps, nonces) and always verify the integrity of the data before trusting a hash.


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-074/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-074/#__codelineno-0-1)contract Example {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-074/#__codelineno-0-2)    function verifyData(bytes memory data1, bytes memory data2) public pure returns (bytes32) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-074/#__codelineno-0-3)        // Vulnerable to hash collisions with multiple variable-length arguments        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-074/#__codelineno-0-4)        return keccak256(abi.encodePacked(data1, data2));  // Possible collision risk    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-074/#__codelineno-0-5)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-074/#__codelineno-0-6)}`


### Fixed Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-074/#fixed-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-074/#__codelineno-1-1)contract Example {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-074/#__codelineno-1-2)    function verifyData(bytes memory data1, bytes memory data2) public pure returns (bytes32) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-074/#__codelineno-1-3)        // Safe way to hash multiple variable-length arguments        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-074/#__codelineno-1-4)        return keccak256(abi.encode(data1, data2));  // More secure handling of variable-length inputs    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-074/#__codelineno-1-5)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-074/#__codelineno-1-6)}`

# SCWE-084: Insecure Use of blockhash

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-084/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-20: Improper Input Validation
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-084/#description "Permanent link")

The `blockhash` function is often misused to generate randomness in smart contracts. However, `blockhash` is publicly available and can be influenced by validators (or miners on PoW chains), making it an unreliable and insecure source of randomness.

Attackers can manipulate `blockhash` by controlling which transactions are included in a block, reordering transactions, or discarding unfavorable blocks. This can lead to predictable random outcomes, allowing malicious actors to exploit lotteries, gaming, and other randomness-dependent mechanisms.

**Attack Scenarios** - Lottery Manipulation: A validator (or miner on PoW) can withhold or reorder transactions to ensure a favorable `blockhash` that lets them win. - Game Exploitation: If a game outcome depends on `blockhash`, an attacker can predict future results and place bets accordingly.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-084/#remediation "Permanent link")

Do not rely on `blockhash` for generating randomness. Use more secure and unpredictable sources of randomness, such as using Chainlink VRF or other trusted oracles.


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-084/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-084/#__codelineno-0-1)// Vulnerable contract using blockhash for randomness [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-084/#__codelineno-0-2)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-084/#__codelineno-0-3)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-084/#__codelineno-0-4)contract InsecureRandomness {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-084/#__codelineno-0-5)    function getRandomNumber(uint256 _blockNumber) public view returns (uint256) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-084/#__codelineno-0-6)        return uint256(blockhash(_blockNumber)); // Predictable randomness    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-084/#__codelineno-0-7)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-084/#__codelineno-0-8)}`

**Why is this insecure?** - Validators (or miners on PoW) control block production — they can reorder or discard blocks to manipulate `blockhash`. - Predictability - Attackers can call this function for past block numbers, making randomness guessable.

title: SCWE-084: Insecure Use of blockhash

title: SCWE-114: ECDSA Nonce Reuse

*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-114: ECDSA Nonce Reuse

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-114/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-323: Reusing a Nonce, Key Pair in Encryption
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/323.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/323.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-114/#description "Permanent link")

Reusing the same ECDSA nonce (`k`) across signatures (or using predictable nonces) leaks the private key. Contracts that accept off-chain signatures for permits, meta-txs, or governance can be compromised if signing infrastructure mismanages nonces.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-114/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Use battle-tested libraries/wallets that generate unique, random or RFC6979 deterministic nonces per message.
-   Monitor and rotate keys if nonce reuse is suspected; support key revocation on-chain.
-   Avoid custom signing code or manual nonce management in scripts.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-114/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-114/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-114/#__codelineno-0-1)// Off-chain signer reuses k for two messages: [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-114/#__codelineno-0-2)// sig1 = (r, s1) with k [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-114/#__codelineno-0-3)// sig2 = (r, s2) with same k => private key can be recovered`


### Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-114/#fixed "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-114/#__codelineno-1-1)// Off-chain: Use libraries/wallets that follow RFC6979; never reuse k. [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-114/#__codelineno-1-2)// On-chain: Support key rotation so compromised keys can be revoked. [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-114/#__codelineno-1-3)mapping(address => bool) public revokedSigners; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-114/#__codelineno-1-4)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-114/#__codelineno-1-5)function execute(bytes calldata payload, bytes calldata sig) external {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-114/#__codelineno-1-6)    address signer = _recoverSigner(payload, sig);    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-114/#__codelineno-1-7)    require(!revokedSigners[signer], "key revoked");    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-114/#__codelineno-1-8)    // ... [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-114/#__codelineno-1-9)}`

# SCWE-115: Weak VRF Parameterization or Callback Validation

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-115/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/330.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/330.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-115/#description "Permanent link")

Using VRF services without validating `requestId`, sender, or subscription can let attackers spoof fulfillments or drain subscription balances. Misconfigured key hashes, gas limits, or shared subscriptions can cause predictable failures and force fallback logic that leaks randomness.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-115/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Bind VRF fulfillments to tracked `requestId` values and trusted coordinator addresses.
-   Use dedicated subscriptions, appropriate key hashes, and sane callback gas limits.
-   Revert on unexpected fulfillments and avoid using fallback pseudo-randomness.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-115/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-115/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-115/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-115/#__codelineno-0-2)import "@chainlink/contracts/src/v0.8/VRFConsumerBaseV2.sol"; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-115/#__codelineno-0-3)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-115/#__codelineno-0-4)contract Lottery is VRFConsumerBaseV2 {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-115/#__codelineno-0-5)    uint256 public randomWord; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-115/#__codelineno-0-6)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-115/#__codelineno-0-7)    function fulfillRandomWords(uint256, uint256[] memory words) internal override {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-115/#__codelineno-0-8)        randomWord = words[0]; // no requestId or sender validation    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-115/#__codelineno-0-9)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-115/#__codelineno-0-10)}`

title: SCWE-131: Missing Domain Separation in Aggregate Signatures
heading: Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-131/#fixed "Permanent link")
text:
*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-131: Missing Domain Separation in Aggregate Signatures

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-131/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/347.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/347.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-131/#description "Permanent link")

BLS/aggregate signature schemes that omit domain separation (e.g., chain id, contract, purpose) allow signature replay across domains. A valid signature for one network or message type can be reused elsewhere to authorize unintended actions.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-131/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Include explicit domain separation tags in the signed message for every aggregate signature.
-   Verify domains on-chain and reject signatures from unknown domains.
-   Use well-reviewed libraries and EIP-712 style typed data for aggregate schemes.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-131/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-131/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-131/#__codelineno-0-1)bytes32 message = keccak256(abi.encode(data)); // no domain tag`


### Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-131/#fixed "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-CRYPTO/SCWE-131/#__codelineno-1-1)bytes32 message = keccak256(abi.encode(DOMAIN_SEPARATOR, keccak256(data)));`

# SCWE-036: Inadequate Gas Limit Handling

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-036/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
    [CWE-400 Link](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/400.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-036/#description "Permanent link")

Inadequate gas limit handling occurs when a contract fails to manage gas constraints efficiently, leading to performance bottlenecks and denial-of-service (DoS) risks. Poor gas handling can result in: - Unoptimized execution: Unnecessary gas-heavy computations increasing costs. - DoS vulnerabilities: Transactions failing due to excessive gas usage, blocking operations. - Inefficient batch processing: Overloaded loops or storage updates causing out-of-gas (OOG) errors.

Unlike **SCWE-032**, which focuses on the protocol-level block gas limit, this issue arises due to poor gas management at the smart contract level.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-036/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Optimize gas usage:** Minimize gas consumption in contract operations.
-   **Avoid unbounded loops:** Ensure loops have a fixed upper limit.
-   **Test thoroughly:** Conduct extensive testing to ensure operations stay within gas limits.

title: SCWE-036: Inadequate Gas Limit Handling
heading: Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-036/#examples "Permanent link")
text:
## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-036/#examples "Permanent link")

-   **Inadequate Gas Handling**

    `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-036/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-036/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-036/#__codelineno-0-3)contract InefficientProcessing {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-036/#__codelineno-0-4)    mapping(address => uint) public balances; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-036/#__codelineno-0-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-036/#__codelineno-0-6)    function batchTransfer(address[] memory recipients, uint amount) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-036/#__codelineno-0-7)        for (uint i = 0; i < recipients.length; i++) {            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-036/#__codelineno-0-8)            balances[recipients[i]] += amount; // Gas-intensive operation        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-036/#__codelineno-0-9)        }    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-036/#__codelineno-0-10)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-036/#__codelineno-0-11)}`


**Issue:** Processes large arrays in a single transaction, which can fail due to out-of-gas errors.

Why is this a problem? - If recipients.length is too large, the transaction fails. - Attackers can exploit this by submitting large recipient lists, causing a DoS attack.

-   **Adequate Gas Handling**

    `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-036/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-036/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-036/#__codelineno-1-3)contract GasOptimizedProcessing {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-036/#__codelineno-1-4)    mapping(address => uint) public balances; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-036/#__codelineno-1-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-036/#__codelineno-1-6)    function batchTransfer(address[] memory recipients, uint amount) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-036/#__codelineno-1-7)        uint i = 0;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-036/#__codelineno-1-8)        while (i < recipients.length && gasleft() > 50000) { // Stop before out of gas            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-036/#__codelineno-1-9)            balances[recipients[i]] += amount;            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-036/#__codelineno-1-10)            i++;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-036/#__codelineno-1-11)        }    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-036/#__codelineno-1-12)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-036/#__codelineno-1-13)}`

    ✔️ Fix: Uses gasleft() to gracefully exit before running out of gas, ensuring some transfers complete. Why is this better? ✅ Prevents complete transaction failure by handling only as many iterations as gas allows. ✅ Reduces DoS risk by allowing partial execution instead of reverting everything. ✅ Enables retrying to complete all operations over multiple calls.

* * *
