# SCWE-058: DoS with Block Gas Limit

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-058/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/400.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/400.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-058/#description "Permanent link")

Denial of Service (DoS) with block gas limit occurs when a contract is designed in such a way that its execution depends on a large amount of gas, potentially exceeding the block gas limit. This can result in the transaction failing, causing the contract to become unavailable or unusable. Attackers can exploit this vulnerability by creating transactions that consume excessive gas, effectively locking the contract or preventing normal operation.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-058/#remediation "Permanent link")

To mitigate this vulnerability, ensure that operations that depend on gas consumption are efficient and that gas limits are taken into account when designing contract logic. Avoid functions that require large amounts of gas to complete, and consider implementing features like batching or chunking operations to spread the gas usage across multiple transactions.


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-058/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-058/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-058/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-058/#__codelineno-0-3)contract GasLimitDoS {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-058/#__codelineno-0-4)    uint256[] public data; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-058/#__codelineno-0-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-058/#__codelineno-0-6)    function addData(uint256[] memory newData) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-058/#__codelineno-0-7)        for (uint256 i = 0; i < newData.length; i++) {            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-058/#__codelineno-0-8)            data.push(newData[i]);  // Can consume a large amount of gas if the array is large        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-058/#__codelineno-0-9)        }    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-058/#__codelineno-0-10)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-058/#__codelineno-0-11)}`

# SCWE-059: Insufficient Gas Griefing

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-059/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/400.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/400.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-059/#description "Permanent link")

Insufficient gas griefing occurs when an attacker intentionally sends a transaction with insufficient gas to force the contract to fail. This can lead to resource consumption issues and potential denial of service for the contract or other users. If a contract relies on external calls or interacts with other contracts and does not properly handle gas estimation, it may be vulnerable to such attacks.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-059/#remediation "Permanent link")

To mitigate this vulnerability, ensure that gas estimation and proper gas limits are handled when performing contract calls, especially when interacting with other contracts. Additionally, use mechanisms to handle failures gracefully, such as revert messages and checks for sufficient gas before initiating important operations.


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-059/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-059/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-059/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-059/#__codelineno-0-3)contract GasGriefing {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-059/#__codelineno-0-4)    address public owner; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-059/#__codelineno-0-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-059/#__codelineno-0-6)    constructor() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-059/#__codelineno-0-7)        owner = msg.sender;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-059/#__codelineno-0-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-059/#__codelineno-0-9)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-059/#__codelineno-0-10)    function transferFunds(address payable recipient, uint256 amount) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-059/#__codelineno-0-11)        require(msg.sender == owner, "Not the owner");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-059/#__codelineno-0-12)        recipient.transfer(amount);  // Potential for griefing with insufficient gas    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-059/#__codelineno-0-13)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-059/#__codelineno-0-14)}`

*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-077: Lack of Rate Limiting

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   **CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling**
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/770.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/770.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#description "Permanent link")

Lack of rate limiting in a smart contract can lead to **Denial of Service (DoS)** attacks, excessive gas consumption, or contract state bloating. Without a mechanism to restrict the frequency of function calls, an attacker can flood the contract with transactions, causing delays, increased gas fees, or complete unavailability of critical functions.

This vulnerability is particularly dangerous in **DeFi protocols**, where unlimited function calls could drain funds, abuse governance mechanisms, or overload on-chain processing.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Implement **rate-limiting mechanisms** such as **time-based constraints** (e.g., requiring a cooldown period between calls).
-   Use **counters with expiration timestamps** to track and restrict repetitive actions.
-   Introduce **gas fees or staking requirements** to deter spam transactions.


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-0-1)contract Example {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-0-2)    mapping(address => uint) public userRequests; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-0-3)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-0-4)    // ❌ No rate limiting: users can spam this function indefinitely    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-0-5)    function request() public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-0-6)        userRequests[msg.sender]++;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-0-7)        // No restrictions or cooldowns, allowing abuse    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-0-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-0-9)}`

**Why is this vulnerable?** - No restrictions on how frequently a user can call `request()`. - An attacker can spam transactions, leading to high gas costs and DoS. - Storage bloat from excessive `userRequests` mappings.

title: SCWE-077: Lack of Rate Limiting
heading: Fixed Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#fixed-contract-example "Permanent link")
text:
### Fixed Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#fixed-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-1-1)contract SecureExample {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-1-2)    struct RequestData {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-1-3)        uint count;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-1-4)        uint lastReset;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-1-5)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-1-6)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-1-7)    mapping(address => RequestData) public userRequests;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-1-8)    uint public constant REQUEST_LIMIT = 5;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-1-9)    uint public constant TIME_WINDOW = 1 hours; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-1-10)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-1-11)    // ✅ Implement rate limiting with a cooldown period    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-1-12)    function request() public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-1-13)        RequestData storage requestData = userRequests[msg.sender]; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-1-14)        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-1-15)        if (block.timestamp > requestData.lastReset + TIME_WINDOW) {            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-1-16)            requestData.count = 0;  // Reset count after time window            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-1-17)            requestData.lastReset = block.timestamp;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-1-18)        } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-1-19)        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-1-20)        require(requestData.count < REQUEST_LIMIT, "Rate limit exceeded");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-1-21)        requestData.count++;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-1-22)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-077/#__codelineno-1-23)}`

**Why is this safe?** - Tracks request timestamps, resetting counts after a fixed period. - Restricts excessive calls, preventing abuse and DoS attacks. - Efficient state management, reducing unnecessary storage costs.

**By enforcing rate limits, contracts can prevent spam attacks and ensure fair access to on-chain resources.**

# SCWE-082: Lack of Proper Gas Management

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-082/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/400.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/400.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-082/#description "Permanent link")

Gas management is crucial in smart contracts to ensure that they do not run out of gas or cause excessive consumption. If gas consumption is not properly controlled, a contract can fail to execute or can be exploited by attackers to cause denial of service (DoS).


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-082/#remediation "Permanent link")

Properly estimate the gas required for functions and set appropriate gas limits. Use `require` or other mechanisms to handle gas consumption failures and ensure that gas usage remains within acceptable bounds.


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-082/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-082/#__codelineno-0-1)contract Example {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-082/#__codelineno-0-2)    function execute() public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-082/#__codelineno-0-3)        while (true) {            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-082/#__codelineno-0-4)            // Excessive gas consumption, no limit set        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-082/#__codelineno-0-5)        }    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-082/#__codelineno-0-6)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-082/#__codelineno-0-7)}`


### Fixed Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-082/#fixed-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-082/#__codelineno-1-1)contract Example {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-082/#__codelineno-1-2)    uint public counter; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-082/#__codelineno-1-3)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-082/#__codelineno-1-4)    function execute(uint _iterations) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-082/#__codelineno-1-5)        require(_iterations <= 100, "Too many iterations"); // Limit iterations to avoid excessive gas usage        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-082/#__codelineno-1-6)        for (uint i = 0; i < _iterations; i++) {            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-082/#__codelineno-1-7)            counter++;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-082/#__codelineno-1-8)        }    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-082/#__codelineno-1-9)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-082/#__codelineno-1-10)}`

# SCWE-109: Unbounded Loops on Untrusted Input

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-109/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-834: Excessive Iteration
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/834.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/834.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-109/#description "Permanent link")

Iterating over user-controlled arrays or mappings without bounds lets attackers submit large inputs that exhaust gas, causing denial of service. Functions like batch withdrawals, reward distribution, or liquidations may become permanently unusable.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-109/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Impose upper bounds on loop iterations or batch sizes.
-   Use pagination/iterative processing with checkpoints.
-   Avoid on-chain iteration over untrusted lists; rely on off-chain aggregation with verifiable proofs (Merkle leaves).


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-109/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-109/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-109/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-109/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-109/#__codelineno-0-3)contract Distributor {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-109/#__codelineno-0-4)    function airdrop(address[] calldata users) external {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-109/#__codelineno-0-5)        for (uint256 i = 0; i < users.length; i++) {            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-109/#__codelineno-0-6)            (bool ok, ) = payable(users[i]).call{value: 1 ether}("");            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-109/#__codelineno-0-7)            require(ok, "Transfer failed"); // can run out of gas with large arrays        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-109/#__codelineno-0-8)        }    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-109/#__codelineno-0-9)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-109/#__codelineno-0-10)}`


### Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-109/#fixed "Permanent link")

# SCWE-116: Missing Supply Cap Enforcement

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-116/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-693: Protection Mechanism Failure
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/693.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/693.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-116/#description "Permanent link")

Tokens or lending systems without hard supply caps allow privileged accounts or flawed logic to mint unlimited units, inflating supply and draining collateralized protocols. Lack of caps also breaks price assumptions in AMMs and oracles.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-116/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Define immutable max supply and enforce it on every mint path.
-   Separate minting roles with multi-sig and timelock; emit events for mint changes.
-   Include cap checks in upgrades and cross-chain minting/bridging logic.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-116/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-116/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-116/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-116/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-116/#__codelineno-0-3)contract Token {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-116/#__codelineno-0-4)    address public owner;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-116/#__codelineno-0-5)    uint256 public totalSupply; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-116/#__codelineno-0-6)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-116/#__codelineno-0-7)    function mint(address to, uint256 amount) external {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-116/#__codelineno-0-8)        require(msg.sender == owner, "not owner");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-116/#__codelineno-0-9)        totalSupply += amount; // no cap        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-116/#__codelineno-0-10)        // mint tokens...    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-116/#__codelineno-0-11)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-116/#__codelineno-0-12)}`


### Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-116/#fixed "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-116/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-116/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-116/#__codelineno-1-3)contract Token {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-116/#__codelineno-1-4)    address public owner;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-116/#__codelineno-1-5)    uint256 public totalSupply;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-116/#__codelineno-1-6)    uint256 public constant MAX_SUPPLY = 1_000_000 ether; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-116/#__codelineno-1-7)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-116/#__codelineno-1-8)    function mint(address to, uint256 amount) external {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-116/#__codelineno-1-9)        require(msg.sender == owner, "not owner");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-116/#__codelineno-1-10)        require(totalSupply + amount <= MAX_SUPPLY, "cap exceeded");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-116/#__codelineno-1-11)        totalSupply += amount;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-116/#__codelineno-1-12)        // mint tokens... *Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-125: Missing Post-Operation Health Check

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-125/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-754: Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-125/#description "Permanent link")

Lending/borrowing protocols that do not re-evaluate health factors after actions (borrow, withdraw, leverage) allow users to exit with unhealthy positions. Attackers can drain collateral or avoid liquidation by skipping post-operation solvency checks.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-125/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Recompute health factor after every state-changing action and revert if below threshold.
-   Lock price/oracle reads during the operation to avoid mid-tx manipulation.
-   Add invariant/fuzz tests to ensure every path enforces solvency.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-125/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-125/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-125/#__codelineno-0-1)function borrow(uint256 amount) external {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-125/#__codelineno-0-2)    _issueDebt(msg.sender, amount);    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-125/#__codelineno-0-3)    // no health check after debt increase [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-125/#__codelineno-0-4)}`


### Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-125/#fixed "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-125/#__codelineno-1-1)function borrow(uint256 amount) external {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-125/#__codelineno-1-2)    _issueDebt(msg.sender, amount);    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-125/#__codelineno-1-3)    require(_health(msg.sender) >= MIN_HF, "insolvent"); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-125/#__codelineno-1-4)}`

*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-126: Unbounded Withdrawal Queue Growth

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-126/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/400.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/400.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-126/#description "Permanent link")

Protocols that queue withdrawals without bounding length or processing batches can face gas exhaustion when executing large queues. Attackers can spam small requests to DoS withdrawal execution or force users to accept delays.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-126/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Cap queue size or use batched/paged processing with upper gas limits.
-   Charge fees or require minimum amounts to discourage spam.
-   Allow users to cancel/claim in smaller chunks rather than processing the entire queue at once.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-126/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-126/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-126/#__codelineno-0-1)function processAll() external {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-126/#__codelineno-0-2)    for (uint256 i = 0; i < queue.length; i++) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-126/#__codelineno-0-3)        _pay(queue[i]);    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-126/#__codelineno-0-4)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-126/#__codelineno-0-5)}`


### Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-126/#fixed "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-126/#__codelineno-1-1)function processBatch(uint256 start, uint256 max) external {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-126/#__codelineno-1-2)    uint256 end = start + max;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-126/#__codelineno-1-3)    if (end > queue.length) end = queue.length;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-126/#__codelineno-1-4)    for (uint256 i = start; i < end; i++) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-126/#__codelineno-1-5)        _pay(queue[i]);    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-126/#__codelineno-1-6)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-126/#__codelineno-1-7)}`

title: SCWE-148: Gas Exhaustion via Unbounded Loops with External Calls
heading: Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-148/#fixed "Permanent link")
text:
*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-148: Gas Exhaustion via Unbounded Loops with External Calls

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-148/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/400.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/400.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-148/#description "Permanent link")

Loops that iterate over user-controlled arrays and perform external calls (transfers, approvals, or other contract calls) in each iteration can exhaust gas when the array is large. Each external call consumes gas; unbounded loops cause the transaction to hit the block gas limit and revert, resulting in denial of service. SCWE-109 covers unbounded loops generally; this weakness focuses on loops that perform external calls.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-148/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Impose an upper bound on loop iterations or batch size.
-   Use pull-based patterns: let users claim individually instead of pushing to many addresses in one tx.
-   Process in chunks with pagination or checkpoints.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-148/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-148/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-148/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-148/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-148/#__codelineno-0-3)contract Airdrop {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-148/#__codelineno-0-4)    function distribute(address[] calldata recipients, uint256 amount) external {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-148/#__codelineno-0-5)        for (uint256 i = 0; i < recipients.length; i++) {            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-148/#__codelineno-0-6)            (bool ok, ) = recipients[i].call{value: amount}("");            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-148/#__codelineno-0-7)            require(ok, "Transfer failed");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-148/#__codelineno-0-8)        }    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-148/#__codelineno-0-9)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-148/#__codelineno-0-10)}`

**Why vulnerable:** Large `recipients.length` causes out-of-gas; one failed transfer reverts the entire batch.


### Fixed[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-148/#fixed "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-148/#__codelineno-1-1)uint256 public constant MAX_BATCH = 100; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-148/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-148/#__codelineno-1-3)function distribute(address[] calldata recipients, uint256 amount) external {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-148/#__codelineno-1-4)    require(recipients.length <= MAX_BATCH, "Batch too large");    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-148/#__codelineno-1-5)    for (uint256 i = 0; i < recipients.length; i++) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-148/#__codelineno-1-6)        (bool ok, ) = recipients[i].call{value: amount}("");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-148/#__codelineno-1-7)        require(ok, "Transfer failed");    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-148/#__codelineno-1-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-148/#__codelineno-1-9)}`

*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-151: Add/Remove Liquidity Without Minimum Output Validation

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-151/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-20: Improper Input Validation
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-151/#description "Permanent link")

Adding or removing liquidity in AMMs (e.g., Uniswap, Curve) without enforcing a minimum amount of LP tokens or underlying assets received can expose users to sandwich attacks or unfavorable execution. Similar to swap slippage (SCWE-090), LP operations can be front-run: an attacker manipulates the pool before the user's add/remove, then reverses after. Without `amountMin` or equivalent checks, users may receive far less than expected.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-151/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   Accept `amountMin` (or `minLPTokens`, `minAmounts`) from users and enforce it when adding/removing liquidity.
-   Use deadline parameters (SCWE-141) in addition to slippage protection.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-151/#examples "Permanent link")


### Vulnerable[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-151/#vulnerable "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-151/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-151/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-151/#__codelineno-0-3)interface IUniswapV2Router {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-151/#__codelineno-0-4)    function addLiquidity(address tokenA, address tokenB, uint256 amountADesired, uint256 amountBDesired, uint256 amountAMin, uint256 amountBMin, address to, uint256 deadline) external returns (uint256 amountA, uint256 amountB, uint256 liquidity); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-151/#__codelineno-0-5)} [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-151/#__codelineno-0-6)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-151/#__codelineno-0-7)contract LiquidityManager {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-151/#__codelineno-0-8)    function addLiquidity(address tokenA, address tokenB, uint256 amountA, uint256 amountB) external {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-151/#__codelineno-0-9)        IUniswapV2Router(router).addLiquidity(            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-151/#__codelineno-0-10)            tokenA, tokenB,            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-151/#__codelineno-0-11)            amountA, amountB,            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-151/#__codelineno-0-12)            0, 0,  // amountAMin, amountBMin = 0: no slippage protection            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-151/#__codelineno-0-13)            msg.sender,            [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-151/#__codelineno-0-14)            block.timestamp        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-151/#__codelineno-0-15)        );    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-151/#__codelineno-0-16)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-DEFI/SCWE-151/#__codelineno-0-17)}`

*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-012: Lack of Multisig Governance

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-285: Improper Authorization
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/285.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/285.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#description "Permanent link")

Lack of multisig governance occurs when critical smart contract functions, such as upgrades, fund withdrawals, or parameter changes, are controlled by a single entity. This creates a **single point of failure**, increasing the risk of **compromise, insider abuse, or unauthorized access**. Without multisig governance, attackers or malicious actors can easily exploit privileged functions if the private key of a single administrator is compromised.

Key risks associated with missing multisig governance: - **Centralization Risk**: A single entity can control and modify key contract parameters. - **Single Point of Failure**: Loss or compromise of the owner's private key can result in catastrophic consequences. - **Unauthorized Access**: An attacker gaining control of the private key can execute privileged functions without approval. - **Lack of Accountability**: Decisions are made unilaterally, reducing transparency and security.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Implement a Multisig Wallet**: Use multisignature schemes (e.g., Gnosis Safe) to require multiple signers for critical transactions.
-   **Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)**: Assign multiple roles with different privileges to prevent centralized control.
-   **Timelocks for Critical Functions**: Introduce a delay for privileged actions, allowing time for community intervention if needed.
-   **On-Chain Governance Mechanisms**: Decentralize decision-making using **DAO-based governance** where applicable.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#examples "Permanent link")

[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-0-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-0-6)    constructor() {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-0-7)        owner = msg.sender;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-0-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-0-9)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-0-10)    function upgradeContract(address newContract) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-0-11)        require(msg.sender == owner, "Only owner can upgrade");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-0-12)        // Only a single owner can perform critical actions    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-0-13)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-0-14)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-0-15)    function withdrawFunds(address payable recipient, uint256 amount) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-0-16)        require(msg.sender == owner, "Only owner can withdraw funds");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-0-17)        (bool ok, ) = recipient.call{value: amount}("");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-0-18)        require(ok, "Transfer failed"); // ❌ No multisig verification    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-0-19)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-0-20)}`

### Refactored to Use Multisig Governance[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#refactored-to-use-multisig-governance "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-1-3)interface IMultiSig {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-1-4)    function submitTransaction(address destination, uint256 value, bytes calldata data) external; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-1-5)} [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-1-6)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-1-7)contract SecureGovernance {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-1-8)    IMultiSig public multisigWallet; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-1-9)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-1-10)    constructor(address _multisigWallet) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-1-11)        multisigWallet = IMultiSig(_multisigWallet);    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-1-12)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-1-13)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-1-14)    function upgradeContract(address newContract) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-1-15)        bytes memory data = abi.encodeWithSignature("upgradeTo(address)", newContract);        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-1-16)        multisigWallet.submitTransaction(address(this), 0, data); // ✅ Requires multisig approval    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-1-17)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-1-18)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-1-19)    function withdrawFunds(address payable recipient, uint256 amount) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-1-20)        bytes memory data = abi.encodeWithSignature("transfer(address,uint256)", recipient, amount);        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-1-21)        multisigWallet.submitTransaction(address(this), 0, data); // ✅ Multisig verification for withdrawals    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-1-22)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-012/#__codelineno-1-23)}`

-   This improved version delegates authority to a multisig wallet, requiring multiple approvals before executing critical actions.

# SCWE-015: Poor Governance Documentation

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-015/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-933: Security Misconfiguration
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/933.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/933.html)

-   CWE-1118: Insufficient Documentation of Error Handling Techniques [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1118.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1118.html)



## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-015/#description "Permanent link")

Poor governance documentation refers to the **lack of clear, transparent, and publicly accessible records** regarding a smart contract system’s decision-making processes, upgrade mechanisms, and role-based permissions. Without proper documentation, **users, developers, and auditors struggle to understand the governance model**, leading to **reduced trust, misconfigurations, and potential security vulnerabilities**.

Key risks associated with poor governance documentation: - **Unclear Decision-Making Process**: Users may not understand how governance proposals are initiated, approved, or executed. - **Hidden Centralization Risks**: Critical governance powers may be concentrated in a small group without public awareness. - **Lack of Upgradeability Transparency**: If upgrade procedures are not well-documented, malicious or unintended changes may go unnoticed. - **Poor Incident Response Handling**: Without clear emergency protocols, governance failures can lead to slow or inadequate responses to attacks.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-015/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Comprehensive Governance Documentation**: Clearly outline roles, permissions, voting mechanisms, and upgradeability in technical and non-technical formats.
-   **Public Governance Reports**: Regularly publish governance decisions, major votes, and protocol updates in a transparent manner.
-   **Well-Defined Emergency Procedures**: Establish and document response plans for governance failures, protocol attacks, or keyholder compromises.
-   **On-Chain Governance Visibility**: Ensure that governance smart contracts expose relevant functions for transparency and accountability.
-   **Third-Party Audits of Governance Mechanisms**: Periodically review governance documentation and processes through independent audits.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-015/#examples "Permanent link")

Unlike code vulnerabilities, **poor governance documentation is a process failure rather than a direct coding flaw**. However, its consequences can be illustrated with real-world governance failures:


### Example: Unclear Upgradeability Policy Leads to a Security Breach[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-015/#example-unclear-upgradeability-policy-leads-to-a-security-breach "Permanent link")

A DeFi protocol allows smart contract upgrades but **fails to document the governance process for approving upgrades**. A small group of developers, holding majority control over the governance multisig, **pushes an unreviewed upgrade** that introduces a critical vulnerability, resulting in a protocol exploit.


### Fixed: Ensuring Transparent Upgradeability Policies[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-015/#fixed-ensuring-transparent-upgradeability-policies "Permanent link")

Protocols should establish a clear and documented upgradeability framework outlining who can propose, review, and approve upgrades. Implementing timelocks, community review periods, and independent security audits ensures upgrades are thoroughly vetted before execution. Additionally, maintaining an on-chain governance audit log enhances accountability and prevents unauthorized changes.

title: SCWE-015: Poor Governance Documentation
heading: Enhancing Transparency in Governance Voting[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-015/#enhancing-transparency-in-governance-voting "Permanent link")
text:
### Example: Lack of Transparency in Governance Voting[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-015/#example-lack-of-transparency-in-governance-voting "Permanent link")

A DAO implements an **opaque governance process**, where voting power is controlled by a few insiders without **a clear framework on how votes are counted or executed**. Community members later discover that **critical protocol changes were pushed without public discussion**, leading to governance disputes and loss of user trust.


### Enhancing Transparency in Governance Voting[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-015/#enhancing-transparency-in-governance-voting "Permanent link")

Governance processes should be transparent, well-documented, and resistant to centralization risks to maintain trust. Clearly defining voting mechanisms, proposal review procedures, and decision-making criteria prevents manipulation and governance capture. Public governance discussions, decentralized voting structures, and immutable records of voting outcomes further enhance credibility and community trust.

# SCWE-037: Insufficient Protection Against Front-Running

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-20: Improper Input Validation
    [CWE-20 Link](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#description "Permanent link")

Insufficient protection against front-running refers to vulnerabilities that allow malicious actors to exploit the order of transactions for profit. This can lead to: - Unauthorized actions by malicious actors. - Loss of funds or data. - Exploitation of the contract’s logic.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Use commit-reveal schemes:** Implement commit-reveal mechanisms to hide transaction details until they are finalized.
-   **Add delays:** Introduce time delays for critical operations to reduce the risk of front-running.
-   **Test thoroughly:** Conduct extensive testing to ensure front-running protection is effective.

title: SCWE-037: Insufficient Protection Against Front-Running
heading: Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#examples "Permanent link")
text:
## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#examples "Permanent link")

-   **Vulnerable to Front-Running**

    `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-0-3)interface IERC20 {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-0-4)    function transferFrom(address sender, address recipient, uint256 amount) external returns (bool);    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-0-5)    function balanceOf(address account) external view returns (uint256); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-0-6)} [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-0-7)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-0-8)contract FrontRunningVulnerable {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-0-9)    IERC20 public token;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-0-10)    uint256 public price = 1 ether; // 1 token = 1 ETH [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-0-11)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-0-12)    constructor(address _token) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-0-13)        token = IERC20(_token);    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-0-14)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-0-15)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-0-16)    function buyTokens(uint256 amount) public payable {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-0-17)        require(msg.value >= amount * price, "Insufficient ETH");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-0-18)        token.transferFrom(address(this), msg.sender, amount);    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-0-19)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-0-20)}`

    Why is this vulnerable?
-   Attackers see the transaction in the mempool and execute a transaction to buy first, raising the price.
-   Victim's transaction executes at a higher price or fails due to slippage.
-   Attacker sells at a profit, exploiting sandwich attacks.

-   **Protected Against Front-Running- Commit-Reveal to Hide Trade Intent**

    `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-1-3)contract SecureTrade {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-1-4)    mapping(address => bytes32) public commitments;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-1-5)    uint256 public price = 1 ether; // 1 token = 1 ETH [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-1-6)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-1-7)    function commitTrade(bytes32 hash) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-1-8)        commitments[msg.sender] = hash;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-1-9)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-1-10)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-1-11)    function executeTrade(uint256 amount, bytes32 secret) public payable {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-1-12)        require(commitments[msg.sender] == keccak256(abi.encodePacked(amount, secret)), "Invalid commitment");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-1-13)        require(msg.value >= amount * price, "Insufficient ETH"); [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-1-14)        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-1-15)        commitments[msg.sender] = 0; // Prevent reusing commitment        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-1-16)        /

title: SCWE-037: Insufficient Protection Against Front-Running
heading: Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#examples "Permanent link")

/ Execute trade after revealing the commitment    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-1-17)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-037/#__codelineno-1-18)}`

    Why is this better?

*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-043: Insecure Use of Fallback Functions

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   **CWE-250: Execution with Unnecessary Privileges**
    [CWE-250 Link](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/250.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#description "Permanent link")

Insecure use of fallback functions refers to vulnerabilities that arise when fallback functions are used improperly. This can lead to: - Unauthorized actions by malicious actors. - Loss of funds or data due to unintended execution. - Exploitation of contract logic if the fallback function allows arbitrary interactions.

Fallback functions are triggered when a contract receives a call with no matching function signature. They can be used to handle Ether transfers or proxy unknown function calls. If misconfigured, they may enable unintended behaviors, such as unauthorized access or fund loss.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Restrict logic execution in fallback functions**: Avoid placing critical execution logic inside fallback functions unless necessary.
-   **Separate Ether reception**: Use `receive()` explicitly to handle Ether transfers instead of overloading `fallback()`.
-   **Validate calls**: Ensure fallback functions do not execute unintended behavior. If required, use access control for specific use cases (e.g., controlled proxy calls).
-   **Use explicit function definitions**: Instead of relying on fallback functions for critical operations, define explicit functions with proper access control.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#examples "Permanent link")


### 🚨 **Insecure Fallback Function**[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#insecure-fallback-function "Permanent link")

#### *Problem: No access control or validation, allowing unintended execution.*[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#problem-no-access-control-or-validation-allowing-unintended-execution "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#__codelineno-0-3)contract InsecureFallback {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#__codelineno-0-4)    fallback() external {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#__codelineno-0-5)        // No access control or validation    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#__codelineno-0-6)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#__codelineno-0-7)}`

\- This contract allows any call with an unknown function signature to trigger the fallback function, which could result in unintended behavior.

title: SCWE-043: Insecure Use of Fallback Functions
heading: Secure Fallback Function (Safe Handling of Ether)[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#secure-fallback-function-safe-handling-of-ether "Permanent link")
text:
### Secure Fallback Function (Safe Handling of Ether)[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#secure-fallback-function-safe-handling-of-ether "Permanent link")

-   Solution: Explicitly handle Ether transfers using receive()

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#__codelineno-1-3)contract SecureFallback {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#__codelineno-1-4)    address public admin; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#__codelineno-1-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#__codelineno-1-6)    constructor(address _admin) {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#__codelineno-1-7)        admin = _admin;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#__codelineno-1-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#__codelineno-1-9)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#__codelineno-1-10)    // Explicitly define a receive function to safely accept Ether    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#__codelineno-1-11)    receive() external payable {} [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#__codelineno-1-12)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#__codelineno-1-13)    // Safe fallback function (does nothing if unintentionally called)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#__codelineno-1-14)    fallback() external payable {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#__codelineno-1-15)        // Optional: Log unexpected calls for security monitoring    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#__codelineno-1-16)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-043/#__codelineno-1-17)}`

This version properly separates Ether reception from fallback execution, preventing unintended behavior.

## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-044/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-20: Improper Input Validation
    [CWE-20 Link](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-044/#description "Permanent link")

Insecure use of storage refers to vulnerabilities that arise when storage variables are improperly managed. This can lead to: - Unauthorized access to sensitive data. - Loss of funds or data. - Exploitation of vulnerabilities in contract logic.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-044/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Encrypt sensitive data:** Encrypt sensitive data before storing it.
-   **Validate inputs:** Ensure all storage updates are properly validated.
-   **Test thoroughly:** Conduct extensive testing to ensure storage is secure.


## Examples[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-044/#examples "Permanent link")

-   **Insecure Storage Usage**

    `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-044/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-044/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-044/#__codelineno-0-3)contract InsecureStorage {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-044/#__codelineno-0-4)    uint public balance; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-044/#__codelineno-0-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-044/#__codelineno-0-6)    function updateBalance(uint newBalance) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-044/#__codelineno-0-7)        balance = newBalance; // No validation    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-044/#__codelineno-0-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-044/#__codelineno-0-9)}`

-   **Secure Storage Usage**

    `[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-044/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-044/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-044/#__codelineno-1-3)contract SecureStorage {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-044/#__codelineno-1-4)    uint public balance; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-044/#__codelineno-1-5)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-044/#__codelineno-1-6)    function updateBalance(uint newBalance) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-044/#__codelineno-1-7)        require(newBalance > 0, "Invalid balance"); // Input validation        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-044/#__codelineno-1-8)        balance = newBalance;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-044/#__codelineno-1-9)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-044/#__codelineno-1-10)}`

# SCWE-075: Incorrect Ether Balance Tracking

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-852: Untrusted Control Sphere
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/852.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/852.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#description "Permanent link")

Incorrect Ether balance tracking occurs when a contract manually maintains an internal balance variable instead of relying on `address(this).balance`. This creates inconsistencies when Ether is received outside of expected functions (e.g., via `selfdestruct()`, `transfer()`, or direct deposits).

Attackers can exploit this by artificially inflating the contract's perceived balance, leading to unauthorized withdrawals or failed transactions. This issue is common in poorly designed deposit/withdraw systems that do not properly verify the actual contract balance.


## Attack Scenario[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#attack-scenario "Permanent link")

An attacker sends Ether to the contract using `selfdestruct()`, increasing its actual balance without updating the internal tracking variable. Later, a user tries to withdraw funds, but the contract incorrectly assumes it has more Ether than it actually does, causing unexpected failures or exploits.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#remediation "Permanent link")

-   **Use `address(this).balance`** instead of manually tracking Ether balance.
-   **Prevent external Ether deposits** by disabling the fallback function unless explicitly needed.
-   **Ensure proper accounting** by always reconciling balances before allowing withdrawals.


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-0-1)// ❌ Vulnerable to incorrect balance tracking due to external Ether deposits [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-0-2)contract IncorrectBalanceTracking {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-0-3)    uint public balance;  // ❌ Manually tracking Ether balance [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-0-4)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-0-5)    function deposit() public payable {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-0-6)        balance += msg.value;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-0-7)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-0-8)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-0-9)    function withdraw(uint _amount) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-0-10)        require(balance >= _amount, "Insufficient funds");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-0-11)        payable(msg.sender).transfer(_amount);        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-0-12)        balance -= _amount;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-0-13)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-0-14)}`

**Why is this vulnerable?** - The contract does not account for direct Ether transfers outside deposit(). - An attacker can send Ether via `selfdestruct()`, inflating the contract balance without updating balance. - This can lead to withdrawals being blocked or excessive withdrawals.

title: SCWE-075: Incorrect Ether Balance Tracking
heading: Fixed Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#fixed-contract-example "Permanent link")
text:
### Fixed Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#fixed-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-1-3)// ✅ Secure implementation: per-user accounting + address(this).balance for consistency [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-1-4)contract CorrectBalanceTracking {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-1-5)    mapping(address => uint) public balances; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-1-6)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-1-7)    function deposit() public payable {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-1-8)        balances[msg.sender] += msg.value;    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-1-9)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-1-10)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-1-11)    function withdraw(uint _amount) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-1-12)        require(balances[msg.sender] >= _amount, "Insufficient funds");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-1-13)        require(address(this).balance >= _amount, "Contract balance insufficient");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-1-14)        balances[msg.sender] -= _amount;        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-1-15)        (bool success, ) = payable(msg.sender).call{value: _amount}("");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-1-16)        require(success, "Transfer failed");    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-1-17)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-1-18)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-1-19)    receive() external payable {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-1-20)        revert("Direct deposits not allowed");    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-1-21)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-075/#__codelineno-1-22)}`

**Why is this secure?** - Per-user `balances` mapping ensures only depositors can withdraw their funds. - Reconciles with `address(this).balance` before transfer to detect unexpected inflows (e.g. `selfdestruct`). - Uses `call{value}` for flexible gas; `receive()` reverts on direct deposits.

# SCWE-078: Improper Handling of Ether Transfers

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-078/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-703: Improper Check or Handling of Exceptional Conditions
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/703.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/703.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-078/#description "Permanent link")

Improper handling of Ether transfers in Solidity can lead to unexpected behaviors, such as failed transactions or loss of funds. For instance, when using `transfer()` or `send()`, failure to check for successful execution or not handling exceptions correctly can cause Ether to be locked or lost in the contract.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-078/#remediation "Permanent link")

Always handle exceptions properly when transferring Ether. Ensure that you check for success or failure using `require()` or `assert()` after Ether transfers. Additionally, use `call()` with a specified gas limit for greater flexibility and error handling.


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-078/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-078/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-078/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-078/#__codelineno-0-3)contract Example {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-078/#__codelineno-0-4)    function transferEther(address payable _to) public payable {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-078/#__codelineno-0-5)        // Fails silently if transfer fails        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-078/#__codelineno-0-6)        _to.transfer(msg.value);  // No error handling, can cause issues    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-078/#__codelineno-0-7)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-078/#__codelineno-0-8)}`


### Fixed Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-078/#fixed-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-078/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-078/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-078/#__codelineno-1-3)contract Example {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-078/#__codelineno-1-4)    function transferEther(address payable _to) public payable {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-078/#__codelineno-1-5)        (bool success, ) = _to.call{value: msg.value}("");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-078/#__codelineno-1-6)        require(success, "Transfer failed");    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-078/#__codelineno-1-7)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-078/#__codelineno-1-8)}`

*Last updated: August 19, 2026*



# SCWE-079: Insecure Use of Transfer and Send

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-079/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/400.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/400.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-079/#description "Permanent link")

The use of `.transfer()` and `.send()` for Ether transfers in Solidity is insecure because they impose a fixed gas limit of 2300 gas. This restriction can cause transactions to fail unexpectedly when the receiving contract has complex logic that requires more gas. Additionally, it can result in a Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerability if the receiving contract cannot execute due to insufficient gas.

This issue is especially problematic in upgradable smart contracts or protocol interactions, where the gas requirements of a receiving contract might change over time.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-079/#remediation "Permanent link")

Instead of `.transfer()` and `.send()`, use `.call{value: msg.value}("")`, which allows more flexible gas allocation and prevents DoS risks. Always check for the return value of `.call()` to ensure the transfer was successful.


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-079/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-079/#__codelineno-0-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-079/#__codelineno-0-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-079/#__codelineno-0-3)contract Example {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-079/#__codelineno-0-4)    function transferEther(address payable _to) public payable {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-079/#__codelineno-0-5)        // Fixed gas limit of 2300 gas can cause unintended failures        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-079/#__codelineno-0-6)        _to.transfer(msg.value);    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-079/#__codelineno-0-7)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-079/#__codelineno-0-8)}`

**Problem**: - If `_to` is a contract that requires more than `2300 gas` (e.g., it has a fallback function with state changes), this transfer will fail. - The contract has no error handling, meaning the sender won't be aware of the failure.


### Fixed Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-079/#fixed-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-079/#__codelineno-1-1)pragma solidity ^0.8.0; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-079/#__codelineno-1-2)[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-079/#__codelineno-1-3)contract Example {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-079/#__codelineno-1-4)    function transferEther(address payable _to) public payable {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-079/#__codelineno-1-5)        // Use call() for better gas flexibility and proper error handling        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-079/#__codelineno-1-6)        (bool success, ) = _to.call{value: msg.value}("");        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-079/#__codelineno-1-7)        require(success, "Transfer failed");    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-079/#__codelineno-1-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-079/#__codelineno-1-9)}`

**Why is this better?** - `.call{value: msg.value}("")` does not impose a gas limit, allowing the receiving contract to execute as needed. - It includes a `require(success, "Transfer failed");` check, ensuring failures are properly handled.

# SCWE-081: Improper Handling of Nonce

Stable Version v1.0

This content is in the **version-(v1.0)** and still under active development, so it is subject to change any time (e.g. structure, IDs, content, URLs, etc.).

[Send Feedback](https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-smart-contract-security-testing-guide/discussions/categories/scwe-scstg-v2-beta-feedback)


## Relationships[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-081/#relationships "Permanent link")

-   CWE-20: Improper Input Validation
    [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html)


## Description[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-081/#description "Permanent link")

Nonce values are used to ensure that transactions are processed in the correct order and prevent replay attacks. Improper handling or validation of nonces can lead to issues such as transaction replay or improper sequencing of transactions, which can be exploited by attackers.


## Remediation[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-081/#remediation "Permanent link")

Always validate nonce values to ensure that they are correctly incremented and avoid reusing nonces. Ensure that nonce handling is robust, especially in cases where external calls are involved, to prevent replay attacks or transaction malleability.


### Vulnerable Contract Example[¶](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-081/#vulnerable-contract-example "Permanent link")

`[](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-081/#__codelineno-0-1)contract Example {     [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-081/#__codelineno-0-2)    mapping(address => uint256) public nonces; [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-081/#__codelineno-0-3)    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-081/#__codelineno-0-4)    function transfer(address _to, uint256 _amount) public {        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-081/#__codelineno-0-5)        uint256 nonce = nonces[msg.sender]; // Nonce is not validated properly        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-081/#__codelineno-0-6)        nonces[msg.sender] = nonce + 1;     // This could allow replay attacks        [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-081/#__codelineno-0-7)        // Transfer logic    [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-081/#__codelineno-0-8)    } [](https://scs.owasp.org/SCWE/SCSVS-GOV/SCWE-081/#__codelineno-0-9)}`

Why is this better? - Nonce is no longer user input: It is validated as part of a signed message, preventing arbitrary replay attempts. - Prevents transaction replay attacks: By signing the message, an attacker cannot reuse an old transaction because the signature includes the nonce. - Ensures integrity & authenticity: The contract only processes the transaction if the signed message is valid and matches the expected sender.
